title: Client Services Manager
description:
Continental is hiring a Client Services Manager! You'll take our accounts directly, and serve as a liaison between our long-standing clients and our operations. You will own our customer relationships end to end: the quote that goes out, the order that comes in, the shipment that leaves on time, and the answer that reaches the customer. Our customers are diagnostics companies around the world, many of which have purchased biological raw materials from us for decades. You'll send quotes, receive the PO’s, and communicate between our internal operations team and the external customers. You will serve as the main point of contact our customers communicate with, and you’ll be the one who answers their requests about shipments, pricing and feasibility of products and projects. Pricing sits with you, inside limits we set together.


Continental has been in business for over 55 years and is a private for-profit blood banking company. We service pharmaceutical and research companies all over the world, and our product is used for research and diagnostic testing materials. With two centers, one in Fort Lauderdale and one in Miami, we provide our blood donors with quality customer services.


Your Responsibilities Will Include

  • Owning our customer relationships. You become the primary point of contact for our largest accounts, which are located both domestically and internationally
  • Owning the RFQ and quoting process: preparing quotes, pricing within established floors, and getting them out on a committed timeline rather than when we get to them
  • Owning the order-to-shipment process end to end, coordinating with our laboratory, production, fulfillment and warehouse teams so that what we promise is what we deliver
  • Building and managing a small client services team, starting with a Client Services Representative you will help us hire
  • Setting and holding service standards: response times, quote turnaround, and proactive communication when something slips
  • Working with our CEO and Controller on pricing strategy, margin and where our numbers need to move
  • Bringing customer feasibility questions to the right internal people and closing the loop, rather than letting questions sit
  • Representing Continental at industry meetings may be required
  • Reporting discrepancies and incidents into our Quality Management System, and completing assigned tasks in our HR and QMS systems accurately and on time


Ideal Candidates Meet the Following Requirements

  • Five or more years in account management, client services, commercial operations or inside sales management
  • Experience managing at least one direct report, or clear readiness to start
  • Comfortable with cost, margin and pricing conversations; able to read a cost model and hold a floor
  • Must fluently speak, understand and write English at a high standard. Much of this role is written communication with customers for whom English is a second language
  • Proficient computer skills; experience with an ERP or order management system
  • Background in life sciences, diagnostics, laboratory supply, biologics, medical devices or another regulated manufacturing environment is strongly preferred
  • Experience working inside an ISO 9001 or FDA-regulated quality system is a plus
  • Experience with international shipping, customs documentation or cold-chain logistics is a plus
  • Being bilingual, Spanish and English, a plus


What You Can Expect from Us

  • You'll Be Treated Fairly-- We are a family-owned and operated company, and we consider each of our employees as part of our larger family. We operate and make our decisions based on merit, qualifications and performance.
  • You'll Be Challenged-- We hold very specialized and several regulatory licenses, which means our work environment is constantly evolving as agencies continue to update and improve their standards.
  • You'll Have Real Authority-- This is not a coordination role with a manager's title. You will carry pricing discretion within agreed floors, you will own the accounts, and you will build your own team. We are hiring you so that these decisions stop sitting on the CEO's desk.
  • You'll Have Reasonable Hours-- Our standard working hours are roughly 7:30am to 5:00pm, and roughly 7:30am to 3:00pm on Fridays. Because many of our customers are in Europe and Asia, some mornings start early, but we do not expect nights, weekends, or on-call.
  • You'll Be Provided with Benefits-- After a probationary period, you have the option to partake in the health insurance plans we provide. You also have the option to start a 401k, all expenses of setting up the account covered by us.


What We Expect From You

  • Ownership - This is the heart of the job. When a customer asks us something, we expect you to be the person who makes sure it gets answered, not the person who forwards it. If an answer requires somebody else, you go get it.
  • Communication - We feel this is the most important aspect of any job. You must be in communication with your supervisor, and make sure they are familiar with and in agreement with your everyday tasks. With customers, the standard is simple: answer them, and if you don't have the answer yet, tell them so and tell them when you will.
  • Timeliness - Everything we do, from shipping out specialty products to scheduling specific donors, is on a schedule. While we are very flexible in terms of time off and scheduling, we operate on the assumption that our employees will be timely, and if necessary, gives plenty of notice of their future absence.
  • Team Work - Our operations, testing and systems are complex and multifaceted, so we expect you to work well with our current team members, from those in the lab to those in administration, to ensure we work most cohesively.
  • Flexibility - We have two centers: our home office in Miami, and a second in Fort Lauderdale. We expect that if necessary, you are willing to work at either location. We also expect that you'll be willing to jump in anywhere in the office where we might need you.
  • Willingness to Learn - While we expect you'll come in with a variety of basic skills, we ask that you come also knowing you'll learn a lot here. Blood banking is a specialized field and nobody arrives knowing all of it; we will teach you.


Salary & Benefits

  • Competitive salary within the field. Final determination will depend on experience level and qualifications.
  • Profit Sharing & 401k after 1-Full Year of Service - Fully funded and invested. All administrative and investment fees are paid for by Continental.

description:
Overview

Job Title: Senior Planner / Scheduler

Reports to: Director of Project Controls

Department: Project Controls

Status: Regular Full-Time Position – Exempt/Salary

About Us

GrayWolf is a national leader in heavy industrial construction, specializing in complex installations involving steel, millwright, piping, vessels, and electrical systems. We are known for safe execution, high performance, and commitment to doing the job right.

Position Summary

We are seeking an experienced Senior Planner/Scheduler to lead schedule development and execution across complex, large-scale heavy industrial construction projects. This is a senior-level role for a seasoned planning professional who has owned the full scheduling lifecycle. The ideal candidate brings deep expertise in integrated master scheduling, critical path management, earned value, and subcontractor governance and can operate with authority across field, engineering, and client teams.

Responsibilities

Core Responsibilities

  • Develop and maintain integrated, cost- and resource-loaded master project schedules supporting field execution across engineering, procurement, construction, commissioning, and startup activities.
  • Lead schedule development and coordinate planning alignment across construction, engineering, procurement, fabrication, and subcontractor teams.
  • Drive weekly critical path reviews, variance analysis, and recovery planning efforts to protect key project milestones and field execution objectives.
  • Lead 3-week lookahead planning sessions with superintendents, general foremen, and engineers to coordinate executable work plans and maintain field execution alignment.
  • Support the implementation of Advanced Work Packaging (AWP) and Field Installation Work Package (FIWP) methodologies to improve field productivity, labor efficiency, and planning discipline.
  • Oversee earned value management (EVM), earned labor tracking, and progress measurement systems to support accurate forecasting and performance reporting.
  • Conduct schedule health reviews to proactively identify execution risks, productivity impacts, and schedule variances.
  • Maintain active field engagement with superintendents and construction leadership to validate progress, identify execution constraints, and support accurate schedule forecasting.
  • Facilitate subcontractor pre-mobilization meetings, weekly coordination sessions, and progress reviews to ensure schedule alignment and execution readiness.
  • Mentor junior planners and subcontractor schedulers on scheduling standards, planning best practices, and field execution coordination.
  • Partner with Project Managers and construction leadership on forecasting, change management, manpower planning, cash flow projections, and executive reporting.
  • Produce manpower forecasts, commodity curves, performance dashboards, and variance analyses for internal leadership and client stakeholders.
  • Identify schedule recovery and acceleration opportunities while driving continuous improvement initiatives across planning, productivity, and field operations.
  • Experience supporting schedule recovery efforts, delay analysis, and change management processes strongly preferred.

Qualifications

Qualifications

Education & Training

  • Bachelor's degree in Construction Management, Engineering, or related field preferred.
  • Equivalent combination of technical training and hands-on multi-discipline scheduling experience will be considered.

Work Experience

  • Minimum 10+ years of progressive planning and scheduling experience on large-scale heavy industrial construction projects, preferably including EPC, Power Generation Oil & Gas, LNG, Petrochemical, Pulp & Paper, Pharmaceutical or related heavy industrial sectors.
  • Proven track record leading integrated project scheduling, subcontractor coordination, and multi-discipline planning execution on complex industrial projects.

Skills & Knowledge

  • Expert-level proficiency in CPM scheduling methodology, critical path analysis, and schedule risk assessment.
  • Ability to read and interpret construction drawings, specifications, and multi-discipline resource plans.
  • Experience producing executive-level schedule analytics.
  • Strong leadership presence with the ability to mentor junior planners and influence subcontractor scheduling teams.

Technical Proficiency

  • Expert-level proficiency in Primavera P6.
  • Familiarity with Oracle, SAP, or similar systems for procurement tracking and cost management a plus.
  • Proficient in MS Office Suite; experience with Navisworks and Microsoft Project a plus.

Physical / Site Requirements

  • Must be able to work extended hours, including evenings and weekends as needed.
  • Ability to visit construction sites
  • Climb stairs/ladders as needed
  • Wear PPE
  • Work in industrial environments

title: Field Technician – Pool Construction & Service
location: West Palm Beach, Florida, United States
description:
Craft Master Custom Pools is a premier custom pool construction company dedicated to delivering exceptional quality and craftsmanship to our clients. We take pride in our work and are looking for a skilled, dependable Field Technician to join our growing team.

Position Overview

The Field Technician plays a hands-on, critical role in the installation, repair, and maintenance of custom swimming pools. The ideal candidate brings well-rounded pool industry experience, works independently in the field, and takes pride in delivering quality results on every job.

Key Responsibilities

  • Equipment Plumbing – Install and connect pool equipment including pumps, filters, heaters, and automation systems following manufacturer specifications and local code requirements.

  • Troubleshooting – Diagnose and resolve mechanical, plumbing, and equipment issues efficiently; identify root causes and recommend effective repair solutions.
  • Autofill Installation – Install and calibrate automatic water levelers/autofill systems to manufacturer and customer specifications.
  • Skimmer Replacement – Remove and replace skimmers, ensuring proper sealing, alignment, and connection to the plumbing system.
  • Bond Wire – Install and inspect bonding wire in compliance with NEC and local electrical codes to ensure pool safety.

Qualifications

  • Strong knowledge of pool plumbing systems, equipment, and industry best practices
  • Familiarity with Florida building codes and pool safety regulations
  • Ability to read and interpret pool plans and equipment manuals
  • Valid driver's license with a clean driving record
  • Reliable, punctual, and able to work independently in the field
  • CPO (Certified Pool Operator) certification is a plus
  • Bilingual (English/Spanish) a plus

Physical Requirements

  • Ability to work outdoors in varying weather conditions
  • Ability to lift up to 75 lbs and perform physically demanding tasks
  • Comfortable working in confined spaces and around water

What We Offer

  • Competitive hourly pay based on experience
  • Company vehicle and/or mileage reimbursement
  • Tools and equipment provided
  • Opportunities for growth within a reputable, expanding company
  • Consistent, year-round work

title: Case Manager - RC
description:
We are hiring for full-time grave shift (Mon-Fri 11pm - 7am)

Job Description: Provide immediate, short-term care and recovery supportive services for adult individuals experiencing mental health or substance use crises. Provide rapid-care coordination to effectively de-escalate and stabilize the individual, facilitating crisis interventions, if needed. Provide observation of Receiving Center clients. Collaborate with a multidisciplinary planning team for a needs assessment and service plan. Connect patients to necessary medical, mental health, and other available community services, ensuring a safe and efficient transition to lower levels of care. Communicate with family members and support systems (when appropriate ROI is in place) to provide education and ensure a continuum of care/support, and maintain independent recovery upon discharge. Provide transportation to appropriate services, as needed. Responsible for light meal prep and laundry services. Other duties and procedures as specified by the supervisor.

Traditional Case Management Services: Help clients gain access to needed medical, social, or educational services and teach them and their families how to access community services to better their manage mental and substance use disorders. Assess clients' status/functioning as it relates to the above services. (History, input from family, medical providers, social workers, educators, etc.) Complete Needs Assessments (NA) that identify areas of service need, with input from clients and others who participated in the Needs Assessments. Link clients to needed community resources identified in the Service Plan. Assist clients in integrating their behavioral, social, educational, dental, and physical health care needs by facilitating attendance at appointments, communicating with health care providers, assisting clients in understanding health care instructions and information; obtain/maintain eligibility for entitlements. Coordinate the ongoing delivery of services to clients with various agencies/providers clients have been linked with. Contact family members for feedback and alert them to changes in status/needs when appropriate releases are in place. Facilitate regular contact with behavioral, social, educational, dental, and physical health care providers, as needed, to help clients obtain any needed level of care. Instruct clients/caretakers, in independently accessing needed community services. Monitor/follow-up of behavioral, social, educational, dental, and physical health care needs with non-BRMH providers of shared clients that need further care or have on-going behavioral, social, educational, dental or physical health care needs and ensure sure timely access, quality and effectiveness of service, symptomatology, the need for face-to-face care, and appropriate Service Plan implementation. Other duties as assigned.

Provide services that treat specific "behavioral problems" using a psychoeducational approach (stress management, relaxation techniques, assertiveness training, conflict resolution, behavior modification, etc.). Provide needed instructions about the importance of regularly attending to dental and physical health care needs, including timely appointments and specialty care, which may include role play, problem solving, etc.

Help clients regain or enhance basic living skills needed for living in the least restrictive environment possible by teaching socialization, interpersonal and communication skills, appropriate behaviors, medication compliance, grooming and hygiene skills, etc. in a psychosocial rehabilitative service or outpatient setting with the goal of restoring the client to his/her best possible functional level. Assist clients to eliminate or reduce symptoms of their diagnosis and improve personal motivation and self-esteem. Provide needed instructions about the importance of regularly attending to behavioral, social, educational, dental and physical health care needs, including timely appointments and specialty care.

May provide Peer Support Services, as assigned by supervisor, by coaching, mentoring, role modeling, and using one's own recovery experiences as tools to assist in actualization of client recovery goals. Assist in client empowerment, community living development, problem-solving support, positive self affirmation, socialization, communication, health, etc. and emphasize the importance of attending to dental and physical healthcare needs. Model adherence to recovery skills. Work on a treatment team and assist in development of recovery plans.

Pick up and deliver clients to or from Center services. Provide respite care, which is temporary care for the client for the purpose of providing time away and relief to the parents or caregivers. Provide Personal Services which include assisting clients with shopping, cleaning, banking, picking up prescriptions, paying bills, transporting, budgeting, etc.

Secondary Activities: Complete up-to-date quality service documentation including accurate time sheet records with appropriate service codes and progress notes by 30 minutes past closing of the next business day in the Center's automated clinical records system. Obtain approval from immediate supervisor on any and all leave taken. Attend supervision appointments and team and organization meetings as scheduled. Maintain an automated schedule, reflecting the FTE availability within Center hours, in order to be consistently available and visible to Center staff and clients. Prepare materials for groups. Attend trainings within, and outside of the Center for job development.

title: Manager, Legal & Business Affairs
description:
ANOTHERLAND is a creative community in music and marketing, with offices in Los Angeles and Nashville. We exist to reimagine the partnership between music creators and the support they need, offering record label, music publishing and agency services for artists, songwriters and brands.

The Legal & Business Affairs Manager is Anotherland's in-house counsel primarily for its label and publishing businesses. The role drafts and negotiates the company's recorded music and publishing agreements, advises the business on contractual and legal obligations, supports the company's corporate and catalog acquisition work, and manages outside counsel on specialist matters. The position reports to the Head of Label Services.



Responsibilities

  • Draft and negotiate a wide range of recorded music agreements, including exclusive recording, license, distribution, profit-share and third-party agreements with artists, producers and mixers.
  • Draft and negotiate music publishing agreements, including co-publishing, administration and songwriter agreements.
  • Negotiate label and side-artist waivers, distribution and label-services agreements, and joint venture arrangements with major labels, publishers and distributors.
  • Advise on option exercises, renewals and terminations, and prepare and review the related notices.
  • Standardize terms, notice provisions and accounting clauses across existing agreements, and maintain agreement templates, a clause library and technology-assisted processes.
  • Prepare and review sync, LOD, NDA, contractor and vendor agreements.
  • Advise A&R, Publishing, Rights Management and Finance on contractual obligations, legal risk, and the royalty and accounting consequences of deal terms.
  • Assess risks, recommend courses of action, and obtain management approval on key business terms.
  • Manage relationships with the representatives of artists, songwriters and counterparties.
  • Support the company's corporate legal work, including company structure, the formation and maintenance of entities, operating agreements, resolutions and consents, and intercompany agreements.
  • Prepare and manage corporate filings, annual reports and registrations, maintain corporate records, and track compliance with regulatory requirements.
  • Support catalog acquisitions from letter of intent through closing, including legal due diligence on chain of title, underlying agreements, royalty obligations and encumbrances, and the drafting and negotiation of purchase agreements and closing documents.
  • Coordinate the post-closing transfer of acquired catalogs with Rights Management and Finance, including assignments, copyright recordations, letters of direction and notices to payees and counterparties.
  • Engage and manage outside counsel on specialist matters, including financing, tax, litigation, audits, disputes and trademarks, and on larger corporate and catalog transactions.

Qualifications

  • J.D. and active membership in good standing of at least one U.S. state bar; eligibility to register as in-house counsel in California or Tennessee.
  • 4+ years of music or entertainment transactional experience at a law firm or in-house at a record label, publisher or distributor, covering both recorded music and publishing agreements.
  • In-depth knowledge of music deal structures, including recoupment, cross-collateralization, option and reversion provisions, and royalty accounting.
  • Working knowledge of copyright law as it applies to sound recordings and musical compositions.
  • Experience negotiating directly with the business and legal affairs teams of major labels and publishers.
  • Strong drafting, negotiation, organizational and communication skills, and the ability to manage a high volume of agreements independently.
  • Ability to provide clear recommendations and see matters through to execution.
  • No outside legal practice or client conflicts.

Preferred

  • Experience with joint venture, profit-share, catalog acquisition or corporate matters.
  • Experience with counterparties in the UK, Australia or Canada.
  • Experience with AI-assisted drafting and review tools.
  • Familiarity with the Christian and gospel music market.

Location

Nashville, TN, Costa Mesa, CA, or Los Angeles, CA.

Hybrid; remote arrangements may be considered for the right candidate.

title: Cultural Resources Principal Investigator
description:
POSITION SUMMARY

Allen Engineering and Science is seeking a Cultural Resources Principal Investigator to lead and manage cultural resources projects from proposal development through project completion. This position is responsible for project acquisition support, research design, regulatory compliance, budgeting, scheduling, staffing, technical quality, and successful project delivery.


The Principal Investigator may also supervise or participate in field activities depending on project needs. This role works with clients, regulatory agencies, landowners, project managers, technical staff, field crews, and multidisciplinary teams to ensure work is completed safely, on schedule, within budget, and in accordance with project scope and applicable professional and regulatory standards.


RESPONSIBILITIES

Key responsibilities include:

  • Lead and manage cultural resources projects from proposal development through project completion.
  • Support project acquisition through strategic planning, proposal preparation, procurement activities, and development of project scopes and cost estimates.
  • Develop and refine research designs, methodologies, field strategies, and project procedures.
  • Manage project planning, budgets, schedules, staffing, logistics, and overall execution.
  • Oversee fieldwork and coordinate personnel assignments, equipment, documentation, and other project resources.
  • Monitor project progress and adjust schedules, staffing, field methods, or documentation procedures as needed.
  • Provide leadership and guidance on field decisions, crew safety, conflict resolution, and project-related problem-solving.
  • Perform quality assurance and quality control reviews of technical reports, regulatory documents, and client communications.
  • Manage or oversee cultural resources surveys, testing, mitigation, monitoring, artifact analysis, laboratory activities, and technical report preparation.
  • Ensure project objectives are achieved in accordance with approved research designs, client expectations, company standards, and applicable regulatory requirements.
  • Coordinate and communicate with clients, regulatory agencies, landowners, and other project stakeholders.
  • Support additional project and practice needs as assigned.


QUALIFICATIONS

Required:

  • Master’s degree or Ph.D. in Anthropology, Archaeology, or a closely related field from an accredited institution.
  • At least five years of documented archaeological field experience, including at least two years of project management and supervisory experience at the Project Archaeologist level or equivalent.
  • Strong knowledge of local, state, and federal cultural resources regulations and compliance requirements, including Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act, NEPA, ARPA, and NAGPRA.
  • Experience conducting and managing cultural resources surveys, testing, mitigation, monitoring, and technical report preparation.
  • Experience managing project scope, budgets, schedules, staffing, field logistics, and technical deliverables.
  • Ability to conduct thorough quality assurance and quality control reviews of technical reports, regulatory documents, and client communications.
  • Experience coordinating and communicating with regulatory agencies, clients, landowners, and other stakeholders.
  • Regional experience in the southeastern United States, including knowledge of applicable state regulations and permitting requirements.
  • Ability to work independently and collaborate effectively with multidisciplinary teams.Willingness and ability to travel and conduct fieldwork as needed.
  • Ability to navigate rugged terrain and conduct shovel testing at prescribed intervals, potentially covering up to 10 miles per day while carrying field equipment weighing up to 40 pounds.
  • Valid driver’s license and ability to meet company driving requirements.


Preferred:

title: AOC Internship Program
description:
Welcome to AOC!

AOC Outreach Services is a behavioral health company dedicated to serving children through evidence-informed skills training and comprehensive case management services. Our Practicum and Internship Program is designed to support Counseling and Social Work master’s students as they complete their required clinical training while making a meaningful impact in the Greater Houston community.


As an approved internship site, we provide master’s-level students with the opportunity to gain hands-on experience working with children and families across diverse settings. Interns are integrated into a multidisciplinary team and supported through structured supervision, professional development, and real-world application of counseling and behavioral health principles.


By partnering with Counseling and Social Work master’s programs, our internship program aims to develop competent, compassionate future clinicians while expanding access to high-quality behavioral health services for children throughout Houston. This program reflects our commitment to workforce development, community wellness, and the long-term growth of the behavioral health field.



Practicum and Internship Requirements

In order to match compliance with all master’s program requirements (LPC, LMSW), interns must meet the following:

Practicum

  • Successful completion of a minimum of 40 hours of direct services and a minimum of 60 hours of indirect services for clients over the course of one full semester
  • One hour of weekly individual or triadic site supervision

Internship

  • Successful completion of a minimum of 120 hours of direct services and

a minimum of 180 hours of indirect services for clients over the course of one full

semester

  • One hour of weekly individual or triadic site supervision

AOC Specifics

  • Students will provide 1-on-1 focused intervention with clients in home or community settings (local park, school, etc). Students will complete progress notes documenting interactions with clients per AOC policy for both Skills Training and Targeted Case Management services.
  • Students are expected to maintain a 2-3 client caseload (10+ hours of direct contact) over the course of the practicum or semester.
  • All hours worked are unpaid for practicum/internship students. If the student is a current employee of AOC Outreach, that student will be expected to take on an additional 2-3 client caseload to fulfill the duties of the program.
  • Students will attend a scheduled introductory orientation, complete all required trainings (CANS, TB test, CPR/Basic Life Support, etc.), attend biweekly staff meetings, and attend weekly supervision with Internship Supervisor.

Direct contact hours may be comprised of any of the following:

  1. Skills training/therapy sessions - Time spent with the client completing therapeutic intervention.
  2. Targeted case management – Direct contact with guardians, Foster care agencies, CPS case workers, etc. This also includes finding and connecting clients to resources and client and family education.
  3. Group/Family counseling – conducting a group session with more than one client or with a family.
  4. Crisis intervention - therapeutic assessment of a client if they are experiencing an active crisis
  5. Other – this category is reserved for any direct work with a client that is not covered in the preceding categories. (The Other category should rarely be utilized).

Indirect contact hours may be comprised of any of the following:

  1. Individual or group supervision – individual supervision occurs when you meet individually with your Field Instructor to discuss clients. Students are required to receive 1 hour of supervision (either individual or group) weekly.
  2. Bi-weekly staff meetings – Staff meetings are not clinical in nature and typically focus on the business aspects of the facility; employee issues or concerns may be discussed in these meetings.
  3. In-service training – students frequently attend training within the facility to learn how the process works at that particular agency (i.e., training on how to complete progress notes, HIPPA regulations, CPR/first aid, etc.).
  4. Treatment Planning & Development – treatment planning is a critical aspect of working with clients. Agencies require that a treatment plan be developed for each new client, based on his/her unique strengths and needs. Any time spent on developing and writing the treatment plan is counted towards the total number of field experience hours for the course.
  5. Progress notes – progress notes are completed after skills training/counseling/targeted case management sessions. Progress notes must be completed within 48 hours.
  6. Client Preparation – Preparing for clients can take extra research or clinical direction from a supervisor. Any time spent on preparing for a client is counted towards the total number of hours.
  7. Organizational Structure - understanding how the organization is managed and its policies.
  8. Other – this category is reserved for any indirect work that is not covered in the preceding categories.

title: Sr. Client Service Associate, Private Wealth
description:
Sr. Client Service Associate, Private Wealth



REPORTS TO:

The Sr. Client Service Associate will report directly to the Sr. Advisor as well as to the Managing Director of Investment Operations, or their designee.



POSITION SUMMARY:

The position of Senior Client Service Associate for The Coury Firm's Private Wealth division (the “Firm”) is a senior-level client service role responsible for supporting Advisors and clients through exceptional service, operational excellence, and accurate execution of client account activities.



The Senior Client Service Associate will provide advanced support in client onboarding, account administration, custodial coordination, money movement processing, workflow management, and client service matters. This individual serves as a key resource to Advisors and fellow Client Service Associates, handling more complex client requests while helping maintain consistency, efficiency, and best practices across the client service team.



This position works collaboratively with Advisors, Client Service Associates, Investment Operations, Compliance, Reporting, and Senior Management to support the delivery of investment management, comprehensive financial planning, risk management, estate planning, and other wealth management services. The role also assists with Advisor-directed trading activities, custodial processes, and operational initiatives, while helping mentor and develop less experienced team members.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Client Service & Relationship Management
    • Assist with client onboarding processes and account establishment.
    • Attend client meetings as requested and assist with data gathering, meeting preparation, meeting notes, and follow-up activities.
    • Serve as a primary point of contact for complex client service requests and account-related inquiries.
    • Assist with maintenance of client relationships by responding to questions regarding investment accounts, service requests, and Firm procedures.
    • Interact with clients regarding various requests, including money movement requests, account balances, charitable giving confirmations, check requests, account maintenance, and other service-related matters.
    • Maintain accurate and current client information within CRM and document management systems.
    • Manage the distribution and receipt of client paperwork and documentation.
    • Prepare client letters, correspondence, and emails as needed.
    • Schedule restaurant and meeting reservations for client events as needed.
    • Take ownership of certain daily operational and client service functions.

    Operations & Custodial Administration

    • Independently prepare and process account opening, maintenance, transfer, and closure documentation with custodians and applicable vendors.
    • Facilitate and monitor account transfers and account maintenance requests to ensure timely completion.
    • Execute money movement transactions, including wires, ACH transfers, journals, and standing authorization requests in accordance with Firm policies and regulatory requirements.
    • Serve as a primary liaison with Schwab and other custodial partners regarding account administration, service requests, and issue resolution.
    • Assist in resolving operational issues, exceptions, and escalations related to client account servicing.
    • Work closely with Advisors, Reporting, Compliance, Investment Operations, and other internal teams to ensure timely execution of client requests and deliverables.
    • Assist with Advisor-directed trading activities, rebalancing support, and related custodial processing in accordance with Firm policies and procedures.
    • Monitor workflows and communicate proactively regarding deadlines, outstanding items, and operational constraints.

    Workflow Management & Process Improvement

    • Utilize CRM systems to submit and assign tasks, create and maintain client records, monitor workflows, generate reports, and track service requests.
    • Assist in identifying opportunities to improve workflows, efficiencies, and client service processes.
    • Help develop, document, and maintain operational procedures, workflows, templates, and reference materials.
    • Demonstrate advanced proficiency with firm systems, custodial platforms, CRM systems, and operational tools.
    • Escalate operational risks, client service concerns, and process exceptions in a timely and professional manner.
    • Assist with special projects and operational initiatives as assigned.

    Leadership & Team Development

    • Serve as a resource and mentor for Client Service Associates and newer team members.
    • Assist with onboarding and training of Client Service Associates.
    • Share best practices and promote consistency in client service and operational processes across the team.
    • Take ownership of complex client service and operational matters requiring advanced knowledge and experience.
    • Support department initiatives designed to improve scalability, efficiency, and service quality.

QUALIFICATIONS:

A Sr. Client Service Associate at the Firm must possess the following qualifications:

  • Bachelor's Degree with five (5) or more years of related experience in wealth management, client service, financial services, or investment operations.
  • Series 65 or 66 license required or ability to obtain within 180 days of employment.
  • Experience with Schwab Advisor Center and custodial platforms preferred.
  • Understanding of wealth management operations, account administration, money movement procedures, and client service workflows.
  • Knowledge of industry rules, regulations, and custodial practices.
  • Possess exceptional professional verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to interface in a professional, cordial, and confident manner.
  • Demonstrate strong organizational and time management skills to successfully manage multiple projects, workflows, and competing priorities.
  • Ability to exercise discretion and professionalism when handling confidential information.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively and work well within a team structure.
  • Ethically driven with an unwavering commitment to client service.
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite, including Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint, Word, and OneNote.
  • Proficiency in CRM systems, document management platforms, and portfolio management software.
  • Demonstrated ability to work independently while maintaining accountability and accuracy.

PROFESSIONAL QUALITIES & FOUNDING PRINCIPLES

The Sr. Client Service Associate must possess the following characteristics and principles:

  • Leadership: The ability to direct and contribute to initiatives and processes within the organization.
  • Ethical Practice: The ability to integrate core values, integrity, trustworthiness, and accountability throughout all organizational and business practices.
  • Effective Communication: The ability to effectively cooperate and exchange information with stakeholders, staff, and clients.
  • Critical Evaluation: The ability to interpret information to make business decisions and recommendations.
  • Global & Cultural Sensitivity and Effectiveness: The ability to value and consider the backgrounds and perspectives of all parties.
  • Relationship Management: The ability to manage interactions to provide service and to support the organization and its clients.
  • Business Acumen: The ability to understand and apply information that can contribute to the organization's strategic plan.

BENEFITS

At The Coury Firm, we believe our people are our greatest asset. We offer a comprehensive and competitive benefits package designed to support your personal, professional, and financial well-being.


Our benefits include:

Competitive base salary with performance-based bonus opportunities

Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance

401(k) plan with company match

Paid time off (PTO) and paid holidays

Continuing education and professional development support

Life and disability insurance

Opportunities for career advancement within a growing, entrepreneurial firm

Collaborative, team-oriented work culture


FOUNDING PRINCIPLES
Unwavering Integrity - be ethical in everything you do

Tenacious work ethic - Always be prepared and one step ahead

Selfless Service - Act with selflessness, caring humility and passion

Strong Leadership - Do what is right, and not just what is easy

Devotion to Education - Be committed to personal client continued education


OUR CULTURE
At The Coury Firm, we foster a collaborative, entrepreneurial environment where team members are empowered to take initiative, think strategically, and grow both personally and professionally. title: Collections Specialist
description:
Company Description

At Informa, no two days and no two people are the same, and you'll find the freedom, opportunity and support of a fantastic community to make a real impact.


We’re an international business that connects specialists with knowledge, helping them to learn more, know more and do more through live and on demand events, digital and data-driven services and academic research.


We are home to over 14,000 colleagues across 30 countries and are a member of the UK’s FTSE 100 group of leading public companies.


In Global Support, we provide expert guidance and hands-on support to the Informa Group and Informa’s many business teams. Across tech, finance, legal, corporate development, HR, communications, operations and many other areas, we work collaboratively and flexibly to help our brands serve their customers and help the company succeed.



Job Description

This role is based in our Cairo Festival City Business Park, New Cairo, Cairo, Egypt office.


This role follows a Monday to Friday working week, applicants should be comfortable with this schedule as a requirement of the position.


Role Profile:


This role is a critical part of Informa's GBS function, responsible for managing global, division-agnostic processes to deliver enhanced quality, consistency, and scalability across financial operations.


We are seeking a proactive Collections Specialist to manage a high-volume portfolio of low-risk and medium-risk customer accounts.


This role focuses on efficient, email-based collection activities for customers with established payment histories, utilizing data-driven insights to prioritize collection efforts.


The position requires strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and the ability to manage multiple accounts simultaneously while maintaining accurate records in our Master Data Management systems. Event attendance might be required, primarily within the MEA region, to support on-site collections and customer engagement activities.


Key Responsibilities:


The Collections Specialist is expected to assume the following key responsibilities plus any other reasonable duties as required:


  • Manage collections activities for customers in GBS who are generally prompt in paying their debts.
  • Manage an assigned portfolio of small and medium-risk customer accounts across multiple regions and legal entities.
  • Conduct debt collection primarily through email communication, ensuring a professional and courteous approach.
  • Responsible for collecting all debts owing to Informa within credit control policies and procedures to ensure that collection targets are met.
  • Monitor customer aging reports and prioritize collection activities based on risk, overdue balances, and payment behaviour.
  • Manage the outstanding sales balances falling due and contact customers to obtain payment before the invoice due date, if applicable to your division.
  • Build close internal relationships with Sales, the rest of O2C team, and the Local Credit teams.
  • Responsible for ensuring all customer contact notes are entered on a formalized standards and updated into the collections tool or the appropriate system.
  • To resolve queries were possible and refer complex disputes to the local credit team in a timely fashion and collect aged debt with a view to minimising bad debt provision.
  • Ensure the customer portal is highlighted to customers when contacted.
  • Responsible for looking after any unallocated cash items sitting on your set of accounts and work with the Cash Application team to have the monies applied if you can gain the appropriate back up from the customer.
  • To achieve the monthly cash collection targets set for your specific section of accounts.
  • Accountable for meeting all defined KPIs and SLAs, with performance monitored through regular reporting and review cycles.

Qualifications

Qualifications and Experience:


  • Relevant experience in Credit Control, Accounts Receivable, Collections, Order-to-Cash operations or Customer Service.
  • Experience working in a shared service centre or GBS functionis preferred.
  • Experience supporting multiple countries or global operations is an advantage.
  • Experience in ERP systems for invoice processing, accounting (SAP, Oracle) is preferred.
  • Experience using collections or credit management tools is preferred.
  • Customer service orientation while maintaining firm collection practices.
  • Collaborative approach when working with sales and finance teams.
  • Attention to detail and ability to manage multiple accounts efficiently.

Skills & Abilities:


  • Strong written & verbal communication skills for effective email correspondence.
  • Problem-solving capabilities for resolving payment disputes.
  • Knowledge and ability to use relevant internal systems.
  • Act with integrity, tact and diplomacy.
  • Highly organised, diligent with attention to detail and the ability to maintain these skills whilst working under pressure.
  • Moderate skills in Excel, Word and Outlook are essential.
  • Ability to work independently and meet deadlines.
  • Fluency in Arabic and English.

Additional Information

We work hard to make sure Life at Informa is rewarding, supportive and enjoyable for everyone. Here’s some of what you can expect when you join us. But don’t just take our word for it – see what our colleagues have to say at LifeAt.Informa.com


Our benefits include:


  • Great community: a welcoming culture with in-person and online social events, our fantastic Walk the World charity day and active diversity and inclusion networks
  • Broader impact: take up to four days per year to volunteer, with charity match funding available too
  • Career opportunity: the opportunity to develop your career with bespoke training and learning, mentoring platforms and on-demand access to thousands of courses on LinkedIn Learning. When it’s time for the next step, we encourage and support internal job moves
  • Time out: Enjoy 15 days of annual leave during your first year of employment, increasing to 21 days thereafter, plus a birthday leave day and the chance to work from (almost!) anywhere for up to four weeks a year
  • A comprehensive company funded private medical insurance with international coverage
  • A ShareMatch scheme that allows you to become an Informa shareholder from the start of your employment, and benefit from free matching shares
  • Strong wellbeing support through EAP assistance, mental health first aiders, and access to health apps and more
  • Recognition for great work, with global awards and kudos programmes
  • As an international company, the chance to collaborate with teams around the world

We’re not solely focused on a checklist of skills. We champion energy and ambition and look for colleagues who will roll their sleeves up, join in and help make things happen. If it sounds like a match and you have most – although not all – of the skills and experience listed, we welcome your application.


If you would like to request reasonable adjustments or accommodations to assist your participation in the hiring process and, or in the advertised position, please inform the appropriate Talent Acquisition Partner for the role once they have been in touch. Your request will be reviewed and considered in confidence. At Informa, you'll find inclusive experiences and environments where all perspectives and backgrounds are welcomed. As part of this approach and our diversity and inclusion commitments, we are also formally an Equal Opportunities Employer. This means we base decisions on relevant qualifications and merit and do not discriminate on the basis of key characteristics and statuses, including all of those protected by law. Ask us or see our website for full information.

title: Senior Operational Risk Analyst
description:
Overview

Connecting clients to markets – and talent to opportunity.With 5,400+ employees and over 80,000 institutional, commercial, and payments clients, we operate from more than 80 offices spread across six continents. As a Fortune 100, Nasdaq-listed provider, we connect clients to the global markets – focusing on innovation, human connection, and providing world-class products and services to all types of investors.Whether you want to forge a career connecting our retail clients to potential trading opportunities, or ingrain yourself in the world of institutional investing, StoneX Group is made up of four business segments that offer endless potential for progression and growth.

Business Segment Overview:

Corporate: Engage in a deep variety of business-critical activities that keep our company running efficiently. From strategic marketing and financial management to human resources and operational oversight, you’ll have the opportunity to optimize processes and implement game-changing policies.

Position purpose: StoneX Group Inc. is seeking an experienced Senior Operational Risk Analyst to lead the program for all North America legal entities out of our Chicago office. Reporting to the Operational Risk Manager.

The Senior Operational Risk Analyst is responsible for supporting the execution and ongoing enhancement of the organization's Operational Risk Management framework. The role will have primary responsibilities across Risk and Control Self-Assessments (RCSAs), Incident Management, control testing, independent review and challenge, and operational risk governance and reporting.

The Senior Operational Risk Analyst will partner with business and functional stakeholders to identify and assess operational risks, evaluate the design and effectiveness of controls, analyze operational risk incidents, challenge risk assessments and remediation activities, and provide management with timely and meaningful risk information.

The role requires strong analytical skills, sound risk judgment, attention to detail, and the ability to translate risk information into actionable insights for business leaders, Risk Management, and governance committees.

Responsibilities

Primary duties will include:

Risk and Control Self-Assessments (RCSA)

  • Coordinate and execute RCSA activities across assigned businesses and functions in accordance with the company's Operational Risk framework and methodology.
  • Partner with business stakeholders to identify and assess key processes, operational risks, and controls.
  • Facilitate RCSA workshops and risk discussions with business and functional stakeholders.
  • Evaluate inherent risk, control effectiveness, residual risk, and alignment with established risk appetite and assessment criteria.
  • Review the completeness and quality of risk and control documentation and supporting evidence.
  • Provide independent review and challenge of business risk assessments, control evaluations, and residual risk conclusions.
  • Identify inconsistencies, emerging risks, control weaknesses, and opportunities to strengthen the risk and control environment.
  • Monitor RCSA remediation activities and ensure actions are appropriately documented and tracked through completion.
  • Support ongoing enhancements to RCSA methodology, guidance, tools, and reporting.

Operational Risk Incident Management

  • Support the identification, assessment, documentation, escalation, and reporting of operational risk incidents and losses.
  • Partner with business owners to ensure incidents are recorded accurately, completely, and in a timely manner.
  • Review incident classifications, risk taxonomy mapping, financial and non-financial impacts, root causes, control failures, and remediation actions.
  • Facilitate or challenge root cause analysis for significant or recurring incidents.
  • Assess whether incidents indicate broader control weaknesses, emerging risks, or potential systemic issues.
  • Identify trends and recurring themes across incidents and provide recommendations for risk mitigation or enhanced controls.
  • Monitor incident remediation activities through completion and challenge whether actions sufficiently address identified root causes.
  • Support escalation of material incidents in accordance with established governance and reporting requirements.
  • Assess whether incidents should trigger reassessment of related RCSA risks, controls, or other elements of the Operational Risk framework.

Control Testing & Assurance

  • Plan, coordinate, and execute risk-based control testing in accordance with established control testing methodology and standards.
  • Assess both the design and operating effectiveness of key controls.
  • Define testing procedures, evidence requirements, sampling approaches, and evaluation criteria.
  • Obtain and evaluate supporting evidence to determine whether controls are operating consistently and as designed.
  • Maintain complete and defensible testing documentation, including testing procedures, evidence reviewed, exceptions identified, and conclusions reached.
  • Clearly document identified control deficiencies and communicate results to relevant stakeholders.
  • Work with control owners to develop appropriate remediation activities for identified deficiencies.
  • Track remediation actions and perform or support validation activities prior to closure.
  • Identify common control themes and systemic weaknesses across business areas and processes.
  • Support enhancements to control testing methodology, procedures, documentation standards, and quality assurance.

Review & Challenge

  • Provide objective and constructive second-line review and challenge of operational risk activities performed by the business.
  • Challenge the appropriateness of risk ratings, control effectiveness assessments, remediation plans, risk acceptances, and closure conclusions.
  • Evaluate whether risks have been identified and assessed consistently with the organization's risk taxonomy, methodology, and risk appetite.
  • Review business-provided evidence to determine whether conclusions are adequately supported.
  • Escalate material concerns, overdue actions, recurring control weaknesses, or areas outside risk appetite through appropriate governance channels.
  • Document review and challenge activities to provide a clear record of the rationale, evidence, conclusions, and management responses.
  • Balance effective challenge with constructive partnership to support sustainable improvements within the business.

Operational Risk Governance & Reporting

  • Prepare regular Operational Risk reporting for senior management, risk committees, and other governance forums.
  • Develop and maintain Key Risk Indicators (KRIs), Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), risk appetite metrics, dashboards, and other management information.
  • Analyze data from RCSAs, incidents, control testing, issues, remediation activities, and other risk sources to identify trends and areas requiring management attention.
  • Produce concise written analysis explaining significant risk movements, emerging trends, control weaknesses, and areas of heightened exposure.
  • Monitor outstanding actions, overdue assessments, control deficiencies, incidents, and other Operational Risk deliverables.
  • Support preparation of Operational Risk Committee materials and management presentations.
  • Help ensure governance reporting is accurate, complete, timely, and supported by appropriate underlying data.
  • Support periodic reporting to senior management and, where appropriate, Board-level risk governance forums.

Risk Identification, Data & Analytics

  • Perform analysis across Operational Risk data to identify emerging risks, concentrations, recurring events, and control themes.
  • Connect information across RCSAs, incidents, control testing, issues, audit findings, KRIs, and other risk information to develop a holistic view of Operational Risk exposure.
  • Perform trend and thematic analysis to identify areas requiring further review or enhanced monitoring.
  • Monitor changes in the business, operating environment, technology, regulatory landscape, and external events that could affect the organization's Operational Risk profile.
  • Support development and enhancement of Operational Risk dashboards and analytical capabilities.
  • Assist with data quality reviews and reconciliation of Operational Risk information.

Operational Risk Framework & Program Enhancement

  • Support ongoing implementation and enhancement of the Operational Risk Management framework.
  • Assist with development and maintenance of Operational Risk policies, standards, methodologies, procedures, and guidance.
  • Identify opportunities to improve the efficiency, consistency, scalability, and effectiveness of Operational Risk processes.
  • Support enhancements to Operational Risk systems, workflows, reporting, and automation.
  • Participate in risk transformation and remediation initiatives.
  • Support regulatory examinations, internal audits, compliance reviews, and other independent assessments relating to Operational Risk.
  • Assist in demonstrating sustainable remediation of identified findings and control weaknesses.

Stakeholder Partnership

  • Build effective working relationships with business leaders, risk owners, control owners, and other first- and second-line stakeholders.
  • Provide guidance to the business regarding Operational Risk policies, methodologies, and expectations.
  • Communicate risk findings clearly and constructively to stakeholders at different levels of the organization.
  • Work collaboratively with related functions, including Compliance, Internal Controls, Information Security, Technology Risk, Third Party Risk Management, Business Resilience, and other risk disciplines.
  • Promote strong risk ownership and reinforce business accountability for identifying and managing Operational Risk.

Qualifications

To land this role you will need:

  • Relevant experience in Operational Risk, Enterprise Risk Management, Internal Controls, Audit, Compliance, or another risk and control discipline.
  • Practical experience conducting or supporting RCSAs, risk assessments, control assessments, or similar risk management processes.
  • Experience analyzing operational risk incidents, control failures, or risk events.
  • Working knowledge of control design and operating effectiveness principles.
  • Experience performing control testing, risk reviews, audit testing, or equivalent assurance activities.
  • Demonstrated ability to critically evaluate information and provide effective review and challenge.
  • Strong analytical, documentation, and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to analyze data, identify trends, and communicate meaningful risk insights.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines in a dynamic environment.

What makes you stand out:

  • Experience within a financial services or other highly regulated environment.
  • Experience within financial services or another highly regulated industry.
  • Knowledge of operational risk management frameworks, risk taxonomies, risk appetite frameworks, and governance practices.
  • Experience preparing Operational Risk reporting for senior management or risk committees.
  • Experience with Governance, Risk and Compliance (GRC) platforms or Operational Risk technology.
  • Experience participating in regulatory, internal audit, or independent assurance reviews.
  • Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint; experience with data visualization or analytics tools is advantageous.

Education / Certification Requirements:

  • Bachelor's degree in Risk Management, Business, Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience.

Working Style:

  • 4 days per week onsite, 1 day per week remote

Key Competencies

  • Operational Risk Expertise - Understands core Operational Risk principles and can practically apply them through RCSAs, incident management, control testing, and governance processes.
  • Risk Judgment - Demonstrates sound judgment when analyzing risk exposure, control effectiveness, residual risk, and remediation activities.
  • Effective Review & Challenge - Constructively challenges business conclusions while maintaining productive stakeholder relationships.
  • Analytical Thinking - Connects information across Operational Risk processes to identify trends, emerging risks, recurring control weaknesses, and broader themes.
  • Control Mindset - Understands how controls mitigate risk and can determine whether controls are appropriately designed and operating effectively.
  • Attention to Detail - Maintains accurate, complete, and defensible risk documentation capable of withstanding management, audit, and regulatory scrutiny.
  • Communication & Influence - Explains complex risk matters clearly and appropriately to business stakeholders, Risk Management, and senior leadership.
  • Execution & Accountability - Takes ownership of assigned deliverables, proactively manages deadlines, and follows risk matters through resolution.
  • Continuous Improvement - Identifies opportunities to strengthen methodologies, processes, controls, data quality, reporting, and overall Operational Risk program maturity.

Hiring Salary Range $90,000 - $110,000. Salary to be determined by the education, experience, knowledge, skills and abilities of the applicant, internal equity and alignment with market data.) Subject to business performance and recommendations of management, this role may be eligible to participate in an incentive compensation plan. This compensation package, in addition to a full range of medical, financial, and/or other benefits, dependent on the position, is offered.

title: Service Coordinator | Al-Futtaim Automotive - BYD | KSA
description:
Position Summary

The Service Coordinator is responsible for managing service bookings, workshop capacity planning, and customer communication to ensure smooth and efficient aftersales operations.

The role acts as the operational backbone between customers, Service Advisors, and the workshop by ensuring all appointments are accurately scheduled, workshop capacity is optimized, and customer interactions are handled professionally across all touchpoints. By maintaining booking discipline and proactive communication, the Service Coordinator directly contributes to workshop utilization, reduced no-show rates, and improved customer experience.

This position plays a critical role in aligning customer demand with workshop capacity while supporting operational efficiency and service revenue generation.

Key Responsibilities

Appointment Booking & Capacity Planning

• Manage inbound service booking requests via calls, online platforms, and walk-in customers using the Dealer Management System (DMS)

• Optimize workshop loading by aligning technician availability, bay capacity, job complexity, and service priorities

• Schedule appointments in a structured manner to maximize workshop utilization and minimize idle capacity

• Coordinate priority bookings including VIP customers, fleet accounts, recall campaigns, and OEM service programs

• Monitor booking pipeline and adjust schedules dynamically based on operational changes

Customer Communication & Engagement

• Confirm service appointments in advance and send reminders to minimize no-show and cancellation rates

• Conduct pre-arrival calls to capture additional customer concerns and ensure Service Advisors are fully prepared for reception

• Manage outbound campaigns for service reminders, recalls, and OEM customer engagement programs

Operational Support & Coordination

• Coordinate customer mobility solutions such as loan vehicles, shuttle services, and waiting area arrangements

• Support Service Advisors by tracking open Repair Orders and escalating delayed jobs or aging work-in-progress (WIP) cases

• Ensure accurate and up-to-date customer data in the DMS, including contact details, ownership updates, and service preferences

• Assist in balancing daily operational workload and supporting smooth workshop flow

Reporting & Performance Monitoring

• Prepare daily, weekly, and monthly reports on booking volumes, show-up rates, workshop capacity utilization, and operational trends

• Track key performance indicators such as appointment conversion, no-show rate, outbound call performance, and booking efficiency

• Identify capacity constraints, booking gaps, and operational inefficiencies, escalating issues to the Service Manager with recommended actions

• Maintain data accuracy within CRM and DMS systems to support reliable reporting and business insights

Customer Experience & Compliance

• Handle customer inquiries and initial complaints professionally, ensuring timely escalation of sensitive or complex cases to the Service Manager

• Support post-service follow-up activities in coordination with CRM and Customer Care teams

• Ensure compliance with OEM communication standards, customer data protection regulations, and internal audit requirements

Skills

Educational Requirements

• Diploma or Bachelor’s Degree in Business Administration, Automotive, or a related field

Experience Requirements

• Minimum 2–4 years of experience in an automotive dealership aftersales environment, contact center, or customer coordination role

• Prior experience in appointment booking, workshop scheduling, or service CRM operations is strongly preferred

• Exposure to high-volume service operations and customer interaction environments is an advantage

Technical Skills

• Proficiency in Dealer Management Systems (DMS) for service booking, customer data management, and appointment tracking

• Strong Microsoft Excel skills for reporting, analysis, and performance tracking

• Familiarity with CRM systems, outbound calling platforms, and customer engagement tools

title: Co-Occurring Counselor – Men's Inpatient Services
description:
The Orenda Center of Wellness is seeking a compassionate, skilled Co-Occurring Counselor to join our Men’s Inpatient Services team in Buckeystown, Maryland. This position provides integrated treatment for adult men experiencing substance use disorders and co-occurring mental health conditions within a residential treatment setting serving up to 32 clients.


We are looking for a clinician who builds strong therapeutic relationships, brings sound clinical judgment to complex needs, and values collaboration, accountability, and professional growth. You will work alongside clinical, nursing, medical, case management, and direct care professionals to help clients develop the skills and stability needed for lasting recovery.


Position Responsibilities

  • Provide individual and group counseling addressing substance use, mental health symptoms, trauma, coping skills, and relapse prevention.
  • Complete clinical assessments and develop individualized treatment plans that reflect each client’s needs, strengths, and recovery goals.
  • Manage an assigned caseload of 8 to 12 clients, assess progress, and adjust interventions in collaboration with the treatment team.
  • Use evidence-based approaches, including motivational interviewing, cognitive behavioral strategies, and trauma-informed care.
  • Identify changes in client functioning, respond to clinical concerns, and coordinate appropriate support and safety interventions.
  • Maintain accurate, timely clinical documentation in the electronic medical record.
  • Collaborate on discharge planning, aftercare referrals, and continuity of care.
  • Participate in treatment team meetings, weekly clinical supervision, and professional development.
  • Report directly to the Clinical Manager and maintain professional, ethical, and confidential clinical practices.

Required Qualifications

  • A master’s degree in counseling, social work, or a related clinical field.
  • An active Maryland graduate-level or independent clinical license is required, such as LGPC, LMSW, LCPC, or LCSW-C, appropriate to the services provided. Graduate-level clinicians must practice under the required supervision.
  • Knowledge of substance use disorders, co-occurring mental health conditions, and integrated treatment.
  • Strong assessment, counseling, documentation, organization, and communication skills.
  • Ability to maintain therapeutic boundaries and work effectively within a multidisciplinary team.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience treating adults with co-occurring mental health and substance use disorders.
  • Experience in residential, inpatient, or other structured behavioral health treatment settings.
  • Familiarity with ASAM criteria, collaborative treatment planning, and electronic medical records.

Clinical Support and Professional Growth

Weekly clinical supervision is included as part of the employment offer. Orenda supports ongoing clinical development through case consultation, treatment guidance, and collaboration with an experienced team. For graduate-level clinicians, supervision toward independent licensure will be coordinated according to the applicable Maryland board requirements.


This full-time opportunity offers competitive compensation, access to Orenda’s employee benefits package, and meaningful work supporting men as they build a foundation for recovery.

To apply, submit your résumé and include your current Maryland license type and status. Please highlight your experience with co-occurring disorders, individual and group therapy, and residential treatment.

title: Employment Tax Advisory Manager
description:
JOB SPECIFICATION

Job Title: Employment Tax Advisory Manager

Reporting to: Tax Partner or nominated Tax Director / Associate Director

Base: 40 Mespil Road, with flexible working arrangements

Contract type: Full time / Permanent

ABOUT CROWE IRELAND

Crowe is a leading business advisory and accountancy firm, ranking among the top 10 firms in Ireland. The firm currently has 19 partners and over 200 staff and provides audit, tax, advisory and consulting services to a broad range of indigenous and international businesses, owner-managed companies and not-for-profit organisations.

Crowe Ireland is an independent member of Crowe Global, one of the world's leading accounting and advisory networks, comprising more than 770 offices, 42,000 professionals and member firms across over 150 countries. This global reach enables us to combine deep local market knowledge with international expertise, providing clients with access to specialist advice and cross-border support wherever required.

ROLE PURPOSE

The Employment Tax Advisory Services team is seeking an experienced Manager to join its growing specialist practice. The successful candidate will manage a varied portfolio of Irish and cross-border employment tax assignments and will work directly with partners, directors and clients on complex and commercially significant matters.

KEY RESULT AREAS

Client and assignment delivery

  • Manage the day-to-day delivery of employment tax assignments across a diverse client portfolio, with appropriate partner or director oversight.
  • Take ownership of project planning, scheduling, budgeting, resourcing and delivery, ensuring that assignments are completed to a high standard and within agreed timescales.
  • Act as a key day-to-day contact for clients, providing clear, practical and commercially focused advice.
  • Manage multiple assignments concurrently and make effective use of available time and team resources.
  • Maintain clear and properly documented technical and commercial rationales for advice provided.

Technical advisory work

  • Advise clients across a broad range of employment tax matters, including PAYE and benefit-in-kind, global mobility, social security, executive reward, termination payments, remote and cross-border working, Revenue interventions and employer compliance.
  • Research and interpret tax legislation, Revenue guidance and relevant case law, and apply that analysis to clients’ circumstances. Prepare and review tax advisory reports, technical memoranda, client correspondence and other written advice.
  • Prepare and review tax advisory reports, technical memoranda, client correspondence and other written advice.
  • Identify tax risks, planning opportunities and practical solutions, escalating novel or higher-risk matters where appropriate.
  • Keep abreast of relevant Irish and international tax developments and contribute to the team’s technical knowledge.

People and team development

  • Lead defined engagements and workstreams, including briefing team members on the scope, objectives and timing of each assignment.
  • Review work prepared by junior colleagues and provide clear, constructive feedback.
  • Coach and support team members through on-the-job learning and formal training.
  • Work collaboratively with colleagues across tax and the wider firm, including Audit, Corporate Finance and Company Secretarial.

Business development and practice growth

  • Build trusted relationships with existing and prospective clients and identify opportunities to provide additional support.
  • Prepare and contribute to proposals, tenders, scoping documents and fee quotations.
  • Support the development of employment tax services, technical materials and client communications.
  • Contribute to the continued growth of the Employment Tax Advisory Services practice and the wider firm.

PERSON SPECIFICATION

Essential Knowledge & Skills:-

Qualifications and experience

  • AITi Chartered Tax Adviser, ACA, ACCA or an equivalent relevant professional qualification.
  • Relevant post-qualification experience in employment tax, global mobility, personal tax or a closely related advisory field.
  • Strong technical knowledge of Irish income tax and PAYE, with relevant experience of employment tax advisory and compliance matters.
  • Experience of managing client assignments, budgets and deadlines, including the ability to handle several workstreams at the same time.
  • Experience of reviewing technical work and supporting the development of junior colleagues.
  • A strong record of preparing clear, accurate and practical written advice for clients and colleagues.
  • Experience across a range of clients or industry sectors is desirable.

Candidate competencies

  • Technical judgement: analyses complex issues carefully, reaches supportable conclusions and knows when to seek senior input.
  • Client service: understands the client’s circumstances and provides advice that is technically sound, practical and responsive.
  • Communication: explains complex tax matters clearly in writing and in discussion, adapting the level of detail to the audience.
  • Ownership: takes responsibility for assignments, follows matters through and addresses issues promptly.
  • Commercial awareness: understands scope, budgets and recovery, and recognises opportunities to add value for clients.
  • People development: provides clear direction, constructive review points and practical support to colleagues.
  • Collaboration: builds effective working relationships across teams and contributes positively to the department and the wider firm.
  • Professional development: remains tax-curious and takes responsibility for maintaining and developing specialist knowledge.

What we offer

  • Direct involvement with partners and directors from the outset.
  • Meaningful responsibility for client relationships and assignments.
  • A clear pathway for progression to Senior Manager and beyond.
  • Flexible working arrangements, including working from home in line with firm policy.
  • Exposure to complex and developing employment tax issues across a broad range of clients and sectors.
  • Structured technical, commercial and leadership development.

EQUAL OPPORTUNITY

Crowe is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We value diversity and anyone seeking employment at Crowe is considered based on merit, qualifications, competence and talent. We don’t regard colour, religion, race, national origin, sexual orientation, ancestry, citizenship, sex, marital or family status, disability, gender, or any other legally protected status when making our hiring decisions. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please let us know.

AGENCY POLICY

Crowe is working on an exclusive search for this role.

Crowe Ireland endeavours to recruit and fill vacancies directly. However, at times when we do need to engage with recruitment agencies, we operate within a preferred supplier list (PSL). We only work and partner with recruitment suppliers where our agreed contractual terms fully in place. If unsolicited CVs are received from any agency not on our PSL, then we will not be liable for payment of introduction fees.
