title: Cultural Resources Project Archaeologist
description:
POSITION SUMMARY

Allen Engineering and Science is seeking a motivated and experienced Cultural Resources Project Archaeologist to support and lead cultural resources projects through all phases of execution. Working under the guidance of a Principal Investigator, this position directs technical work, supports regulatory compliance, prepares archaeological documentation, and supervises field and laboratory personnel.


The Project Archaeologist contributes to successful project delivery by balancing technical requirements with project scope, schedule, and budget objectives. The ideal candidate will demonstrate strong technical expertise, project coordination skills, and a commitment to delivering high-quality cultural resources management services.


RESPONSIBILITIES

Key responsibilities include:

  • Lead and oversee technical archaeological investigations under the direction of a Principal Investigator.
  • Support compliance with applicable federal, state, and local cultural resources regulations, including Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act.
  • Assist with coordination and communication among clients, regulatory agencies, Tribal representatives, and other project stakeholders.
  • Supervise and provide technical guidance to archaeological field crews and laboratory teams.
  • Prepare and review technical reports, research designs, treatment plans, monitoring reports, and other project deliverables.
  • Balance technical requirements with project scope, schedule, and budget objectives.
  • Manage the processing, cataloging, documentation, and curation of archaeological collections and records.
  • Conduct preliminary analysis and interpretation of cultural materials and provide recommendations to the Principal Investigator.
  • Maintain complete and accurate field records, datasets, and project documentation.
  • Develop expertise in specialized areas such as artifact analysis, GIS, geoarchaeology, bioarchaeology, or technical reporting.
  • Mentor and train early-career archaeologists and field technicians.
  • Promote accountability, professionalism, collaboration, and respect across project teams.
  • Support additional project and practice needs as assigned.



QUALIFICATIONS

Required:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Anthropology, Archaeology, or a related discipline from an accredited institution.
  • At least four years of professional archaeological experience.
  • Experience conducting or supporting Phase I, Phase II, and Phase III cultural resources investigations.
  • Experience with artifact analysis, archaeological documentation, and technical report preparation.
  • Experience writing technical reports from project initiation through final submission.
  • Working knowledge of Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act, NEPA, the Antiquities Code of Texas, and other applicable cultural resources regulations.
  • Experience supporting permit applications and regulatory coordination.Experience using digital field-data collection systems, GPS equipment, and archaeological databases.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Excel and the management of large datasets.
  • Ability to plan, organize, and coordinate archaeological field and laboratory activities.
  • Strong written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills.Ability to work outdoors in varying weather and terrain conditions.
  • Ability to walk, stand, bend, kneel, excavate, and perform other physical activities for extended periods.
  • Ability to safely lift and carry equipment, supplies, and archaeological materials weighing up to 40 pounds.
  • Willingness to work extended hours or weekends and complete overnight travel when required by project or client needs.
  • Ability to travel to project sites and Allen Engineering and Science office locations as needed.
  • Valid driver’s license and acceptable driving record.


Preferred:

  • Completion of an accredited archaeological field school.
  • Experience with archaeological testing, evaluation, and data recovery projects.
  • Experience conducting archival and historical research.
  • Familiarity with curation standards used by agencies in the southeastern United States.
  • Basic understanding of project budgets, cost estimating, and financial tracking.
  • Registered Archaeologist status through the Register of Professional Archaeologists.
  • Specialized experience in artifact analysis, GIS, geoarchaeology, bioarchaeology, technical reporting, or a related cultural resources discipline.


WHY ALLENES?

Allen Engineering and Science offers competitive compensation, a generous benefits package, professional development opportunities, and the chance to work alongside talented professionals on impactful projects.


EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER

Allen Engineering and Science is an Equal Opportunity Employer and considers all qualified applicants without regard to protected status under applicable federal, state, or local laws.

title: BODY TECH-BEECHER
description:
Our team is expanding, and we are looking for an experienced Auto Body Technician to join our team. What does joining our team offer?

A unique blend of independence, excitement, growth opportunities, and a supportive work culture. We are an employee-centric team, and we want you to join us!

What do our Auto Body Technicians do?


SUMMARY:

The Auto Body Technician is responsible for repairing damaged vehicle body parts in accordance with company specifications, processes and time standards. The Auto Body Technician is skilled in analyzing, assessing and fixing damaged vehicles. This role is responsible for repairing, replacing and refinishing outer body parts. This position will also be skilled in fixing internal automotive structures.


ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Repairs vehicles per estimate and according to established standards. This position prepares vehicles for body repair work. Additionally, the Auto Body Technician will be challenged with restoring bodywork to its original condition. This may include removing damaged parts and installing replacement parts utilizing specialized tools to repair the damage and realign structural components.
  • Communicates with management regarding any additional repairs that may be needed on a customer’s vehicle. Notifies management of any difficulties or problems that may prevent a quality job from being performed or cause a change in the promised completion/delivery time.
  • Maintains tools and equipment in good working order. Operates all tools and equipment in a safe manner. Ensures that work area is organized, clean and free of safety hazards.
  • Maintains and wears all required safety and health personal protective equipment, including eye protection.
  • Cooperates and assists other personnel in the repair and prepping of vehicles, often dependent upon schedule and area of expertise.
  • Understands, keeps abreast of and complies with federal, state and local regulations that affect body shop operations, such as hazardous waste disposal.


QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Solid working knowledge of the processes, techniques and materials used in repairing automotive equipment with a minimum of 1-3 years of experience working in the collision repair arena.
  • Possess extensive knowledge of vehicle structure to remove and replace damaged components, such as doors, windscreens and fenders.
  • Demonstration of safety precautions required in performing the work in this position.
  • Possess a strong attention to detail in addition to the ability to follow written and verbal instructions.
  • Strength to perform average lifting up to 35 pounds and occasionally over 70 pounds.
  • Demonstrated agility, equilibrium and coordination as required when climbing, stooping, kneeling, crouching, crawling and balancing under precarious conditions.
  • Strong arm, hand and finger dexterity with demonstrated physical capacity to reach, handle, finger and feel.
  • Comfortable working in a fast-paced, production-oriented environment.


This position description is intended to be dynamic and subject to change. Position requirements and essential functions may be altered from time to time based upon the needs of the organization and department. This position may be required to execute special projects or other related duties on occasion.

title: Physiotherapy Assistant (PTA)
description:
RNS Health Care Services is currently seeking a dedicated and skilled Physiotherapy Assistant (PTA) to join our dynamic Rehabilitation team. In this community-based role, you’ll support Registered Physiotherapists in delivering rehabilitation services that help clients improve mobility, maintain independence, and achieve their functional goals.


The successful candidate will demonstrate strong communication skills, sound judgment, and the ability to work collaboratively with supervising Physiotherapists while performing duties within their scope of responsibilities.


Service Areas: Bradford, Barrie, Keswick, Queensville, Holland Landing, East Gwillimbury, Mount Albert, Sharon, Newmarket, Aurora, Georgina, Beeton, and Tottenham.

Employment Type: Full-time / Part-time

Wage: $20.00 to $27.00 per hour

Rehabilitation and Client Care

  • Carry out designated physiotherapy interventions and rehabilitation activities as assigned by the supervising Registered Physiotherapist, in accordance with the established plan of care and applicable supervision requirements.
  • Assist with individual rehabilitation programs, including prescribed therapeutic exercises, mobility activities, stretching, strengthening, balance, coordination, and functional training.
  • Support clients in improving and maintaining mobility, strength, flexibility, endurance, functional independence, and overall as required.
  • Reinforce prescribed exercise techniques, safe movement strategies, and rehabilitation recommendations provided by the supervising Physiotherapist.
  • Encourage client participation, motivation, and adherence to prescribed rehabilitation programs while respecting individual abilities, preferences, and goals.
  • Provide client-centered services that promote dignity, independence, safety, and respect for cultural backgrounds and personal preferences.

Client Safety and Risk Management

  • Monitor clients' tolerance and responses to prescribed interventions and promptly report changes in condition, increased pain, dizziness, shortness of breath, fatigue, falls, or other concerns to the supervising Physiotherapist.
  • Follow established safety procedures when assisting clients with mobility, transfers, positioning, and prescribed exercises.
  • Identify and report environmental hazards, equipment concerns, and other risks that may affect client safety during service delivery.
  • Document and report incidents, near misses, falls, and other safety concerns in accordance with RNS policies and procedures.
  • Recognize the limits of the PTA role and promptly seek guidance from the supervising Physiotherapist when client needs fall outside the established plan of care or assigned responsibilities.

Clinical Documentation and Communication

  • Complete accurate, timely, and objective documentation of treatment activities, client participation, responses to interventions, and other required service information.
  • Communicate relevant observations, progress, concerns, and changes in client status to the supervising Physiotherapist to support ongoing clinical decision-making.
  • Maintain complete and confidential client records in accordance with organizational policies, applicable privacy legislation, and documentation requirements.
  • Communicate professionally with clients, families, caregivers, retirement home personnel, and other relevant stakeholders within the scope of the role and applicable confidentiality requirements.
  • Report missed visits, cancellations, scheduling issues, and other service delivery concerns through established organizational processes.

Infection Prevention and Equipment Management

  • Comply with RNS infection prevention and control procedures, including hand hygiene, appropriate use of personal protective equipment, and cleaning of reusable equipment.
  • Use rehabilitation equipment safely and appropriately in accordance with established instructions and the supervising Physiotherapist's direction.
  • Identify and report damaged, defective, or unsuitable equipment and environmental conditions that may compromise client safety.


Operational Performance and Accountability

  • Deliver assigned services in accordance with established schedules, care plans, organizational policies, and applicable service requirements.
  • Notify the appropriate personnel of scheduling conflicts, service interruptions, client unavailability, and other operational concerns in a timely manner.
  • Collaborate with the supervising Physiotherapist and relevant RNS team members to support continuity of care and effective service coordination.
  • Participate in required training, team meetings, and quality improvement initiatives to maintain service standards and support organizational objectives.
  • Follow established treatment plans and seek direction before implementing changes to prescribed interventions or activities.
  • Maintain professional boundaries and demonstrate respectful, ethical, and client-centered conduct in all interactions.
  • Protect client privacy and confidentiality and comply with applicable legislation, professional requirements, and RNS policies and procedures.
  • Perform other related duties consistent with the position and assigned by the appropriate supervisor.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • Minimum of one (1) year of experience in a clinical, community-based, homecare, rehabilitation, or retirement home setting.
  • Diploma from an accredited community college Physiotherapist Assistant/Physiotherapy Assistant (PTA) program, or an equivalent recognized qualification.
  • Demonstrated understanding of rehabilitation principles, therapeutic exercise techniques, mobility assistance, and functional rehabilitation.
  • Experience working with older adults and individuals with mobility limitations, physical disabilities, or complex functional needs is an asset.
  • Experience providing services in clients’ homes and/or retirement home environments is an asset.
  • Strong understanding of client safety, fall prevention, infection prevention and control, and safe equipment use.
  • Excellent interpersonal, verbal, and written communication skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to establish positive, respectful, and therapeutic relationships with clients, families, caregivers, and healthcare team members.
  • Strong organizational, time-management, problem-solving, and documentation skills.
  • Ability to work independently in community settings while following established treatment plans and communicating effectively with the supervising Physiotherapist.
  • Ability to recognize changes in a client's condition and escalate concerns appropriately.
  • Demonstrated professionalism, reliability, patience, empathy, and commitment to client-centered care.
  • Availability to work a flexible schedule, including days, evenings, and weekends, as required.
  • Valid Ontario driver's license, access to a reliable motor vehicle, and proof of valid automobile insurance.
  • Ability to travel between client locations within the assigned service area.

title: Volunteer Coordinator
description:

Recent research demonstrates that kindness benefits our physical and mental health, and that recognizing kindness in others increases a person’s happiness and satisfaction. But just as solving a calculus problem requires advanced math skills, the challenges of daily life require advanced kindness skills. title: Clinical Assistant
description:
Position Summary

The Clinical Assistant supports the Clinical Director and supervising physicians in delivering high-quality, patient-centred fertility care. Working collaboratively with physicians, nurses and other healthcare professionals, the Clinical Assistant assists with patient consultations, fertility cycle monitoring, treatment coordination, clinical procedures and follow-up care.



The role involves supporting patients throughout their fertility journey, reviewing clinical information and coordinating next steps in treatment under physician direction. The successful candidate must demonstrate sound clinical judgement within their authorized scope of practice, strong communication skills and a compassionate approach to patient care.

All clinical activities, including any controlled acts, must be performed within the individual's authorized scope of practice and in accordance with applicable legislation, delegation requirements, clinic policies and physician supervision arrangements. Although this role is advertised as Full-time, we are open to Part-time applicants as well. Please advise us in your application.



Key Responsibilities



1. Clinical Support and Patient Care

  • Support the Clinical Director and supervising physicians in delivering patient care as an extension of the physician-patient relationship.
  • Perform delegated clinical duties and controlled acts where legally authorized and appropriately delegated by the supervising physician.
  • Assist physicians during clinical assessments, consultations and procedures.
  • Collaborate with physicians, nurses and other healthcare professionals to promote safe, coordinated and high-quality patient care.
  • Establish professional, ethical and trusting relationships with patients, families and members of the healthcare team.
  • Deliver patient care in a manner consistent with True Care Fertility's mission, values, policies and standards of practice.



2. Patient Consultations and Fertility Education

  • Assist with initial patient consultations and follow-up appointments, including fertility cycle monitoring visits.
  • Provide patients with information about fertility investigations, treatment options, procedures and next steps following their initial investigative cycle.
  • Explain treatment processes and clinical instructions within the scope of the role and under physician direction.
  • Respond to patient questions and concerns, escalating clinical questions or decisions to the supervising physician when appropriate.
  • Provide compassionate emotional support to patients throughout their fertility journey, recognizing the sensitive and personal nature of fertility treatment.

3. Treatment Planning and Coordination

  • Review patient files, medical histories, investigation results and relevant clinical documentation in preparation for consultations and follow-up appointments.
  • Discuss investigation findings and potential next steps with the treating physician to support the development and coordination of individualized treatment plans.
  • Assist with coordinating treatment plans, follow-up appointments, investigations and cycle monitoring activities as directed by the physician.
  • Ensure treatment-related follow-ups and outstanding investigations are tracked and communicated to the appropriate clinical team members.
  • Communicate treatment instructions to patients only in accordance with the supervising physician's direction and the Clinical Assistant's authorized scope of practice.



4. Clinical Procedures and Treatment Support

  • Assist physicians during fertility-related clinical procedures and ensure the necessary documentation and supplies are prepared.
  • Perform intrauterine insemination (IUI) procedures only where legally authorized, appropriately delegated and supported by the required training, competence and supervision arrangements.
  • Carry out delegated clinical orders in accordance with physician instructions, clinic protocols and applicable professional requirements.
  • Support patient preparation, procedural coordination and post-procedure follow-up as directed by the supervising physician.
  • Maintain appropriate infection prevention, patient safety and clinical documentation standards.



5. Results Review and Patient Follow-Up

  • Review patient files, laboratory results, diagnostic investigations and imaging reports in preparation for physician review.
  • Identify abnormal or outstanding laboratory and imaging results requiring attention and promptly escalate them to the supervising physician in accordance with established protocols.
  • Communicate results and follow-up instructions to patients after the supervising physician has reviewed the findings and provided appropriate direction.
  • Respond to patient emails and messages relating to treatment, investigations and follow-up care within the scope of the role and in accordance with clinic procedures.
  • Coordinate follow-up appointments and ensure physician instructions are documented and communicated accurately.
  • Maintain appropriate follow-up processes to support continuity of care and timely clinical decision-making.



6. Clinical Documentation and Administrative Support

  • Maintain accurate, complete and timely patient records, including medical histories, investigation results, treatment plans, progress notes and follow-up documentation.
  • Document consultations, clinical activities and delegated orders in accordance with clinic policies and applicable documentation standards.
  • Conduct administrative reviews and audits of abnormal laboratory results, imaging reports and other outstanding clinical items to support appropriate follow-up.
  • Ensure patient records and clinical communications are handled confidentially and in accordance with applicable privacy legislation.
  • Perform other duties consistent with the position, qualifications, scope of practice and operational needs of True Care Fertility.



Qualifications and Requirements



Education and Professional Credentials

Required

  • Graduate of a recognized Physician Assistant program or an equivalent qualification accepted by True Care Fertility for the duties of the role.
  • Current Basic Cardiac Life Support (BCLS) certification.

Preferred / Considered an Asset

  • Additional education or training in Obstetrics and Gynecology, reproductive medicine or fertility care.
  • Membership in the Canadian Association of Physician Assistants (CAPA), now known as the Canadian Association of Physician Assistants (CAPA) where applicable.



Experience

  • At least one year of relevant experience in a comparable clinical role.
  • Experience working in an interprofessional healthcare environment.
  • Experience in fertility, reproductive health, Obstetrics and Gynecology, or a related clinical setting is an asset.



Skills and Competencies

  • Excellent interpersonal, verbal and written communication skills.
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail, particularly when reviewing clinical documentation and tracking patient follow-ups.
  • Ability to work collaboratively within an interdisciplinary healthcare team.
  • Ability to work independently and manage responsibilities within the authorized scope of practice.
  • Strong professional judgement, accountability and commitment to patient safety.
  • Compassionate and respectful approach to patients experiencing sensitive or emotionally challenging circumstances.
  • Ability to manage competing priorities in a busy clinical environment.
  • Commitment to confidentiality, ethical conduct and continuous learning.


Professional Standards and Patient Safety

The Clinical Assistant is expected to comply with applicable Ontario legislation, professional requirements, True Care Fertility's clinical protocols and privacy policies.

The employee must perform clinical activities only where authorized, appropriately trained and competent to do so. Physician delegation and supervision must comply with applicable legal and professional requirements. Clinical decisions, interpretation of results and treatment changes must remain with the appropriately authorized healthcare professional unless the Clinical Assistant is independently authorized to perform those activities.


General Disclaimer

This job description outlines the primary responsibilities and requirements of the position and is not exhaustive. Additional duties may be assigned where consistent with the role, the employee's qualifications and competence, and applicable legal and professional requirements.

title: Line Tech III or Higher
description:
Are you ready to take the next step in your line technician career? Blue Ridge Energy is looking for an Apprentice Line Technician III or higher to join our team in Watauga, North Carolina. This role is part of our structured training and progression program, designed to develop skilled, safety-driven, and knowledgeable line technicians who help us deliver reliable power and outstanding service to our members.


What You'll Do

As an Apprentice Line Technician III or higher, you'll be hands-on in the construction, maintenance, and repair of our electric distribution and transmission system.


What You Bring:

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Performing routine work on secondary and primary voltages on energized lines under supervision.
  • Learning to install transformers, reclosers, capacitors, and voltage regulators.
  • Operating and maintaining aerial bucket trucks, digger derricks, and other line equipment.
  • Assisting in substation and underground distribution system work.
  • Building confidence in reading system maps, specifications, wiring diagrams, and electrical codes.
  • Practicing and modeling strict safety standards in every task.
  • Supporting outage restoration efforts in all weather conditions, day or night.


Why Blue Ridge Energy?

At Blue Ridge, you won't just be building power lines-you'll be building a career. We value teamwork, member service, and a safety-first culture. You'll be joining a cooperative where your work truly makes a difference in people's lives every single day.


Our training progression provides clear steps for advancement. Depending on your starting level and experience, you'll continue progressing through our structured apprentice program with increased responsibility and skill development at each level. Apprentice Levels are: I, II, III, IV, Class B, and Class A.


What We're Looking For

  • High school diploma or equivalent (Associate degree in Line Technology preferred for advancement).
  • A minimum of three years of cumulative line work experience for Apprentice III (more for higher classification).
  • Strong knowledge of line work practices, equipment, and safety standards.
  • Ability to work outdoors in all conditions and respond quickly to outage situations.
  • Valid commercial driver's license (CDL), safe driving record, D.O.T. physical, and ability to pass all required screenings.
  • Commitment to teamwork, continuous learning, and delivering excellent service to our members.
  • Resides within 30 minutes of the district office location or is willing to relocate at their own expense.



Work Schedule

  • Regular schedule: Monday–Friday, 7:00 AM – 3:30 PM
  • Outage and emergency response: required regardless of weather, time of day, or holiday.


Grow With Us

If you're passionate about line work, thrive in a team environment, and want a career that challenges you while serving your community, this could be your next step. Join Blue Ridge Energy and power the future with us.


Apply today to advance your career as an Apprentice Line Technician III (or higher)!

Interested candidates are encouraged to apply early, as this posting may be closed at any time once a sufficient candidate pool has been established.

title: Director, Operations
description:
Overview

The Director, Operations is responsible for the safe, reliable, and efficient operation of the mission critical facilities L5 manages for its clients. This role owns operational performance across a portfolio of sites, including uptime, service level compliance, safety, maintenance excellence, and client satisfaction. The Director leads site and regional operations leaders, sets the operating standards that govern how L5 runs critical infrastructure, and ensures every site is staffed, trained, and equipped to prevent, detect, and respond to incidents. It is a highly cross-functional role, partnering closely with training, safety, human resources, vendor management and procurement, finance, commissioning, project delivery, and executive leadership to deliver consistent results across a fast-growing national platform.

Responsibilities

Operational Performance & Uptime

  • Own operational performance across the site portfolio, including availability, incident response, service level agreement (SLA) compliance, and client-defined key performance indicators.
  • Direct the operation and maintenance of critical power, cooling, and building systems, including electrical distribution, UPS and battery systems, generators, chillers, and controls.
  • Lead incident management and emergency response, including escalation, root cause analysis, corrective action, and client communication.
  • Ensure rigorous use of methods of procedure (MOPs), standard and emergency operating procedures (SOPs/EOPs), and change management on every site.
  • Drive preventive and predictive maintenance programs, asset management, and capacity and lifecycle planning to extend the life of client infrastructure.

Safety, Compliance & Risk

  • Enforce a zero-incident safety culture, including electrical safety, lockout/tagout, work permitting, and site access protocols.
  • Ensure sites are audit-ready and compliant with client requirements, regulatory obligations, and industry standards.
  • Identify operational risks across the portfolio, set mitigation plans, and escalate issues early with clear recommendations.
  • Lead drills, readiness reviews, and post-incident reviews to build operational discipline and improve response.

Client & Financial Management

  • Serve as a senior operational contact for clients, building trusted relationships through transparent reporting, regular performance reviews, and proactive communication.
  • Manage operating budgets, labor plans, and vendor spend, and deliver site and portfolio financial targets in partnership with finance.
  • Manage subcontractors and service providers in partnership with vendor management & procurement, holding them accountable to performance and safety standards.
  • Support business development with operating plans, staffing models, transition plans, and risk review for new site mobilizations and pursuits.

People & Process

  • Lead, develop, and hold accountable regional and site operations leaders, building a strong bench for growth.
  • Partner with talent acquisition and training to staff sites ahead of mobilization and to qualify personnel before they work on critical systems.
  • Establish scalable operating standards, playbooks, and governance suited to a fast-growing platform business.
  • Track and report operational performance, incident trends, and lessons learned to continuously improve results.
  • Serve as a key advisor to executive leadership on operational risk, resourcing, and growth.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Operations, Business, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
  • 12+ years of experience in mission critical operations, data center operations, or facilities management, including 5+ years leading multi-site or large-scale operations teams.
  • Deep working knowledge of critical power and cooling infrastructure and the procedures used to operate and maintain it in live environments.
  • Demonstrated success delivering uptime and SLA performance for demanding clients, including hyperscale, colocation, or enterprise customers.
  • Strong experience managing incident response, root cause analysis, and corrective action.
  • Strong financial acumen, including budget management, labor planning, and cost control.
  • Strong understanding of safety and compliance standards for electrical and mechanical work, such as NFPA 70E and OSHA requirements.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to engage technicians, clients, and executives.
  • Proven ability to lead and influence cross-functional teams across multiple sites.
  • Willingness to travel regularly to client sites across North America.
  • Experience in a high-growth or outsourced services environment preferred.
  • Industry certifications, such as Uptime Institute, CDCP, CDFOM, or CFM preferred.
  • Experience mobilizing new sites and transitioning operations from clients or prior providers preferred.

What Success Looks Like

  • Sites operate safely and reliably, with uptime and SLA targets consistently met or exceeded.
  • A repeatable, scalable operating model that supports L5’s national growth.
  • Fewer incidents and faster, more disciplined response when issues occur.
  • Strong, trusted relationships with clients and across training, safety, human resources, finance, and executive leadership.

EEO/AA Employer M/F/D/V

L5 Mission Critical is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local law.

title: SENIOR ELECTRICAL MAINTENANCE ENGINEERING
description:
Ariston Group is a global leader in sustainable climate and water comfort, listed on Euronext Milan. In 2025 the group reported 2.7 billion-euro revenues, with almost 11,000 employees, direct presence in 41 countries in 5 continents, 32 production sites and 31 research and development centers. The group demonstrates its commitment to sustainability through renewable and high-efficiency solutions, including heating heat pumps, water heating heat pumps, hybrids, domestic ventilation, air handling, electric components, and solar thermal systems, while continuously investing in technological innovation, digitalization, and advanced connectivity solutions. The group operates under global strategic brands Ariston, Wolf and Elco, and brands such as Calorex, NTI, Atag, Domotec, Brink, Chromagen, Racold, as well as Thermowatt and Ecoflam in the components and combustion technologies business.


Are you an experienced electrical maintenance professional who enjoys solving complex technical problems and preventing equipment failures?
We are looking for a Senior Electrical Maintenance Engineer with strong hands-on expertise in industrial electrical systems and automation. You will play a key role in ensuring the safe and efficient operation of our production equipment while improving long-term performance.


Your challenge
In this role, you will diagnose complex faults, eliminate recurring issues and strengthen our preventive maintenance approach. Working closely with Production, Engineering and Maintenance, you will implement sustainable technical solutions and support equipment upgrades.


What you will do




  • Diagnose and resolve complex electrical, electronic, automation and control-system failures.

  • Troubleshoot PLCs, HMIs, drives, motors, sensors, control panels and automated production equipment.

  • Lead root-cause analyses and implement sustainable corrective actions.

  • Develop and optimize preventive and planned maintenance programs.

  • Analyze maintenance data to reduce downtime and improve equipment availability.

  • Contribute to TPM and Lean Maintenance initiatives.

  • Support electrical modifications, equipment upgrades and automation projects.

  • Ensure all activities comply with applicable safety requirements and plant procedures.

  • Keep electrical schematics and technical documentation up to date following modifications.

  • Serve as the technical reference for complex electrical issues and coach maintenance technicians.

What you bring

title: Jr Technical Training Engineer
description:

title: Director, Community Food & Nutrition Services
description:

General Summary: This on-site role is a mission-driven member of the San Antonio Food Bank (SAFB) leadership team who leads all meal production and meal program operations. This includes the Mays Culinary Center, satellite kitchens at Haven for Hope and New Braunfels Food Bank, federal child nutrition programs, vended meal contracts, Catalyst Catering, the culinary training program, and Hunters for the Hungry. The Director makes sure every meal is safe, good to eat, on time, reimbursable, and within budget, and helps SAFB grow into new services such as medically tailored meals and emergency feeding.

Department Leadership

  • Lead the department as one team, supervising the Assistant Director, Mays Kitchen Managers, Dietitian, and Executive Chef (about 40 positions across three kitchens).

• Ability to maintain concentration and attention to detail while performing complex administrative and project-related tasks.• Work is generally performed in an office, fabrication shop, manufacturing facility, or project site environment.• Light work requiring exertion of up to 20 pounds occasionally and up to 10 pounds frequently.• Compliance with company attendance standards.

title: Blood Donor Aide & Interviewer
description:
*Are you a customer oriented person interested in the medical field and in making a difference? We could be a match! We will train you in ALL ASPECTS of the position; NO LICENSE OR CERTIFICATION REQUIRED!*


Continental is expanding our team of Blood Donor Aides and Interviewers! Our Donor Services Staff has great working hours and work as a strong, cross-trained and versatile team. Individuals joining this team are responsible to interview and process blood donors visiting our blood bank. EMT or LPN certification is a plus! We’re looking for someone who has strong customer service skills, has an eye for detail when reading, and is interested in joining a team of compassionate and effective Donor Service Processors. This is a full-time position and has opportunity for growth.


Continental has been in business for over 55 years and is a private for-profit blood banking company. We service pharmaceutical and research companies all over the world, and our product is used for research and diagnostic testing materials. With two centers, one in Fort Lauderdale and one in Miami, we provide our blood donors with quality customer services.


Your Responsibilities Will Include:


  • Taking the blood pressure, pulse, temperature and other vitals of our donors
  • Asking all FDA-required questions to make sure each donor is eligible and safely processed
  • Ensuring donors’ hematocrit levels are up to FDA standards
  • Assigning donors to a specific section of our complex list of products
  • Answering any questions or concerns blood donors may have during the process
  • May perform phlebotomy in accordance to CSG Standard Operating Procedures and FDA guidelines (*Training not required.)


Ideal Candidates Meet the Following Requirements:


  • Must fluently speak, understand and write English
  • Must be bilingual - Spanish & English
  • Must have proficient computer skills
  • LPN/EMT certification is a plus
  • May have previously demonstrated exceptional customer service in another work environment
  • May have a background and interest in the medical health field


What You Can Expect from Us:


  • You’ll Be Treated Fairly-- We are a family-owned and operated company, and we consider each of our employees as part of our larger family. We operate and make our decisions based on merit, qualifications and performance.
  • You’ll Be Challenged-- We hold very specialized and several regulatory licenses, which means our work environment is constantly evolving as agencies continue to update and improve their standards.
  • You'll have Phenomenal Hours-- We will not ask you to operate outside of our standard working hours, which are roughly 7:30am - 5:00pm. On Fridays, our working hours are roughly 7:30am-3:00pm. You will not be asked to work weekends, nights, or to be on call on any regular basis.
  • You’ll Be Provided with Benefits-- After a probationary period, you have the option to partake in the health insurance plans we provide. You also will have the option to start a 401k, all expenses of setting up the account covered by us.


What We Expect From You:


  • Communication - We feel this is the most important aspect of any job. You must be in communication with your supervisor, and make sure they are familiar and in agreement with your everyday tasks.
  • Timeliness - Everything we do--from shipping out specialty products to scheduling specific donors--is on a schedule. While we are very flexible in terms of time off and scheduling, we operate on the assumption that our employees will be timely, and if necessary, gives plenty of notice of their future absence.
  • Team Work - Our operations, testing and systems are complex and multifaceted, so we expect you to work well with our current team members--from those in the lab to those in administration--to ensure we work most cohesively.
  • Flexibility - We have two centers: our home office in Miami, and a second in Fort Lauderdale. We expect that if necessary, you are willing to work at either location, in the case of an emergency. Your gas and time would be compensated for a short period, if we ask that you work in a station that is not your home station. We also expect that you’ll be willing to jump in anywhere in the office where we might need you.
  • Willingness to Learn - While we expect you’ll come in with a variety of basic skills, we ask that you come also knowing you’ll learn a lot here.


Salary & Benefits


  • Competitive salary within the field. Final determination will depend on experience level and qualifications.
  • Profit Sharing & 401k after 1-Full Year of Service - Fully funded and invested. All administrative and investment fees are paid for by Continental.
  • Health Insurance - A majority of the insurance fees is paid for by Continental. This includes gap, vision and dental insurance. We can talk to you about what kind of plan will work for you.


About Continental Services Group Inc.


We are an FDA-licensed company that has been in business for over 55 years. We provide blood components and other biological raw materials to our customers, who use the material for the further manufacturing of in-vitro diagnostic products. The vast majority of the product we sell is used for manufacturing test kits and controls, which are used in hospitals around the world. Holding some of the industry's most specialized certifications, we draw the blood and other raw material from a wide base of donors, a majority of which repeatedly and consistently visits every 56 days. This repeat-donor base allows us to provide extensively tested and unique products to the pharmaceutical industry.


Continental has been an FDA licensed facility since 1971, holding multiple city, state and federal licenses. Our laboratory is CLIA certified since 1971, and our facilities have been ISO 9001 certified since 2003. Continental Services Group is an Equal Opportunity Employer and maintains a smoke and drug-free workplace. All offers of employment are contingent upon successful completion of drug and background checks.

title: Construction Project Manager, Mission Critical
description:
Overview

The Construction Project Manager is responsible for the end-to-end delivery of construction, retrofit, and infrastructure upgrade projects in data centers and other mission critical environments. This role owns scope, schedule, budget, quality, and safety, and ensures that work in or adjacent to live, operating facilities is planned and executed with no impact to client uptime. The Project Manager serves as the primary point of contact for the client, directing subcontractors, vendors, and L5 field teams from preconstruction through commissioning and closeout. It is a highly cross-functional role, partnering closely with operations, commissioning, safety, vendor management & procurement, finance, and business development to deliver projects on time, on budget, and without incident.

Responsibilities

Project Planning & Execution

  • Own the project lifecycle from award through closeout, including scope definition, work breakdown, schedule development, and budget management.
  • Plan and sequence work in live data center environments, including method of procedure (MOP) development and review, change management, and maintenance window coordination.
  • Lead retrofit and upgrade projects involving critical power and cooling systems, such as switchgear, UPS and battery systems, generators, chillers, and controls.
  • Manage submittals, RFIs, long-lead equipment, change orders, and project documentation to keep work moving and protect margin.
  • Coordinate closely with L5 commissioning teams so testing, integrated systems testing, and turnover are planned from the start of the project.
  • Manage project closeout, including punch lists, as-built documentation, operations and maintenance manuals, and turnover to client operations teams.

Safety, Quality & Risk Management

  • Enforce a zero-incident safety culture, including electrical safety, lockout/tagout, work permitting, hot work, and site access requirements.
  • Identify, document, and mitigate risks to uptime, schedule, cost, and safety, and escalate issues early with clear recommendations.
  • Hold the project team and subcontractors accountable to quality standards, client requirements, and code and regulatory compliance.
  • Lead pre-task planning, risk reviews, and post-project lessons learned to improve future projects.

Client, Subcontractor & Team Leadership

  • Serve as the day-to-day client lead, providing clear and proactive communication on progress, risks, and changes.
  • Select, direct, and manage subcontractors, trade partners, and vendors in partnership with vendor management & procurement.
  • Lead project meetings, progress reporting, and client updates, and prepare financial forecasts, cost reports, and invoicing.
  • Lead, mentor, and develop project engineers, superintendents, and coordinators.
  • Support business development with scoping, estimating, schedule input, and risk review for new pursuits.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Construction Management, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
  • 7+ years of construction project management experience, including delivery of projects in data centers, critical facilities, or other mission critical environments.
  • Demonstrated success managing multimillion-dollar projects in live, operating facilities with strict uptime and safety requirements.
  • Working knowledge of critical power and cooling infrastructure and the construction methods used to install and upgrade it.
  • Strong command of scheduling, cost control, contract administration, and change management.
  • Experience developing and executing MOPs and working within client change management processes.
  • Strong understanding of construction safety standards, including OSHA requirements and NFPA 70E.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to lead clients, subcontractors, and field teams.
  • Proficiency with project management and scheduling tools (e.g., Microsoft Project, Primavera P6, Procore) and Microsoft Office/Excel.
  • Proven ability to manage multiple concurrent priorities and deadlines under pressure.
  • Willingness to travel to project sites and client locations as needed.
  • PMP, CCM, OSHA 30, or similar certifications preferred.
  • Experience with hyperscale, colocation, or enterprise data center clients preferred.

What Success Looks Like

  • Projects delivered safely, on schedule, and on budget, with no impact to client
  • Strong, trusted client relationships that lead to repeat work and expanded
  • Seamless handoff between construction, commissioning, and
  • Strong working relationships across operations, commissioning, safety, procurement, finance, and executive leadership.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local law.

title: Engineering Manager

This is an exciting opportunity to make a lasting impact on the future of our electric infrastructure while working with a team committed to innovation, safety, and member service.


What You’ll Do

As the Engineering Manager, you will provide leadership and technical expertise to support the growth, reliability, and operation of Blue Ridge Energy's electric system. Key responsibilities include:

  • Lead and develop a team of technical professionals.
  • Prepare and manage Construction Work Plans and Long-Range System Plans.
  • Oversee electric system planning, design, and analysis, including:
    • Load flow studies
    • Voltage drop studies
    • Capacitor studies
    • System loss studies

  • Develop, implement, and audit transmission and distribution design standards.

  • Manage systemwide Land Rights
  • Support substation and transmission construction projects through planning, budgeting, scheduling, and cost control.
  • Ensure compliance with RUS, NESC, environmental, and construction standards.
  • Provide engineering support for system loading, switching, outage restoration, and power quality investigations.
  • Develop and manage departmental capital and operating budgets.
  • Review and prepare transmission, substation, and distribution switching orders.
  • Deliver engineering training and technical support to operations personnel across the cooperative.
  • Serve as a trusted advisor to the Director of Engineering Services and collaborate across departments to achieve organizational goals.

What You’ll Bring

We're looking for a strategic leader who combines strong technical expertise with a commitment to teamwork, safety, and exceptional service.

  • Proven leadership and supervisory skills.
  • Strong knowledge of electric transmission and distribution system design and operation.
  • Expertise in system planning, protection, coordination, and engineering analysis.
  • Experience developing budgets, cost estimates, schedules, and project plans.
  • Strong problem-solving abilities and sound engineering judgment.
  • Ability to communicate effectively with technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • A collaborative leadership style that encourages employee involvement and continuous improvement.
  • Dedication to safety, operational excellence, and outstanding member service.

What Is Required

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering with a power systems emphasis, or equivalent experience.
  • Professional Engineer (PE) registration required.
  • Minimum of 7 years of engineering experience in electric transmission and distribution systems.
  • Experience with transmission and distribution system protection and coordination.
  • Demonstrated knowledge of RUS and NESC standards.
  • Valid driver's license and safe driving record.
  • Experience with Milsoft WindMil required.
  • Experience with Eaton CYMTCC and Power Monitors Inc. ProVision software preferred.
  • Supervisory experience preferred.

title: Medical Billing and Coding Specialist
description:
General Summary:

We are seeking a detail-oriented, highly organized Medical Billing and Coding Specialist to join our healthcare team. In this role, you will be responsible for translating complex patient medical records into standardized codes and managing the end-to-end insurance claims process. Your primary objective is to optimize our Revenue Cycle Management (RCM) by ensuring accurate, timely clinical documentation translation and securing maximum, compliant reimbursement from insurance payers.

We are a mission-driven organization focused on providing judgement-free sexual and reproductive healthcare, including abortion care, gynecologic services, gender-affirming care.


Key Responsibilities:

  • Medical Coding: Review, analyze, and translate clinical documentation, physician notes, and laboratory reports into accurate alphanumeric codes using ICD-10-CM, CPT, and HCPCS Level II code sets.
  • Claims Submission: Prepare, validate, and electronically transmit clean insurance claims to commercial insurance carriers, Medicare, and Medicaid.
  • Insurance Verification: Verify patient insurance eligibility, benefits coverage, and coordinate necessary pre-authorizations or referrals prior to patient visits.
  • Denials & Appeals Management: Monitor claim status, identify root causes for rejections or denials, correct errors, and submit formal appeals to insurance companies.
  • Accounts Receivable (AR) Tracking: Maintain and follow up on outstanding patient and insurance aging balances to reduce days in AR.
  • Patient Accounts & Support: Answer patient inquiries regarding statement balances, explain insurance Explanation of Benefits (EOBs), and establish authorized payment plans.
  • Regulatory Compliance: Maintain absolute confidentiality and strictly adhere to HIPAA guidelines, OIG regulations, and internal compliance protocols.

Any other duties as assigned by the supervisor.


Skills/Qualifications:

  1. Education: High School Diploma or equivalent required; an Associate Degree in Health Information Technology or a related field is highly preferred.
  2. Experience: Minimum of 2-3 years of direct experience in medical billing and coding within a clinic, hospital, or billing agency with preferred expertise in women’s health (OBGYN, family planning)
  3. Technical Skills: Proficiency with electronic health records (EHR/EMR) software (e.g.,AthenaHealth) and clearinghouse platforms.
  4. Medical Knowledge: Understanding of medical terminology, anatomy, physiology, and diverse insurance payer guidelines.
  5. Soft Skills: Excellent analytical thinking, strong mathematical accuracy, clear communication skills, and high attention to detail. Ability to work with minimal supervision and direction. Ability to work and interact with a diverse team and patient population.

title: Surgery Manager
description:
Join the Team at Cincinnati Animal CARE

At Cincinnati Animal CARE (CAC), we do work that matters.

Every day, our team protects animals, supports our community, and helps save thousands of lives each year through compassionate care, advocacy, and education.

This work is meaningful, fast-paced, and can be challenging, but for the right person, it’s incredibly rewarding.

We are a team built for impact, made up of people who care deeply, work hard, support one another, and show up every day committed to making a difference.

If you are passionate about animals, thrive in a mission-driven environment, and want your work to have purpose, we’d love to have you join us.

About the Role

We are looking for a Surgery Manager to join our team and play an important role in supporting CAC’s mission.

In this position, you will:

  • Lead Cincinnati Animal Care’s volume surgery program.
  • Establish departmental goals, implement new initiatives, and advance Cincinnati Animal Care as a progressive leader in shelter medicine

This is a great opportunity for someone who enjoys meaningful work, takes pride in helping others, and wants to contribute to a growing organization making a real impact in the community.

What You’ll Be Responsible For

Department Leadership

  • Directly supervise surgery staff, anesthesia staff, surgery assistants, surgery coordinators, and volunteers.
  • Provide coaching, mentoring, accountability, and performance evaluations.
  • Develop staff through continuing education, cross-training, and leadership opportunities.
  • Foster a positive, collaborative, and solutions-oriented team culture.
  • Participate in interviewing, hiring, onboarding, and disciplinary processes.
  • Develop future leaders within the surgery department.

Surgical Operations

  • Oversee all daily surgical operations and workflow.
  • Ensure efficient scheduling of veterinarians, staff, volunteers, and surgery cases.
  • Coordinate daily surgery assignments based on patient needs and staffing.
  • Maintain smooth patient flow from intake through recovery and discharge.
  • Ensure animals receive timely surgical care to meet adoption, transport, medical, and behavioral goals.
  • Assist clinically during surgery or anesthesia as operational needs require.

Quality & Patient Care

  • Maintain the highest standards of anesthesia safety and patient care.
  • Ensure compliance with departmental Standard Operating Procedures.
  • Monitor anesthesia records and surgical documentation for accuracy.
  • Lead quality assurance reviews and identify opportunities for improvement.
  • Monitor surgical complication rates and implement corrective actions when necessary.
  • Promote Fear Free handling and low-stress patient care throughout the surgical process.

Program Development

  • Evaluate workflow and develop strategies to increase surgical efficiency.
  • Lead initiatives to reduce surgical backlog.
  • Develop new programs that expand access to lifesaving surgery.
  • Collaborate with medical leadership to introduce progressive surgical techniques and best practices.
  • Assist in developing departmental policies and SOPs.

Inventory & Equipment Management

  • Oversee all surgical inventory, pharmaceuticals, and medical supplies.
  • Maintain appropriate inventory levels while controlling costs.
  • Coordinate servicing and maintenance of anesthesia machines, autoclaves, oxygen systems, and surgical equipment.
  • Ensure controlled substance documentation complies with DEA and Ohio regulations.

Administrative Responsibilities

  • Oversee surgery scheduling and surgical records.
  • Ensure anesthesia logs, invoices, medical records, and reporting are accurate.
  • Complete monthly surgery reports and grant reporting requirements.
  • Analyze surgery metrics and provide recommendations to medical leadership.
  • Monitor departmental budgets and purchasing.

Community Partnerships

  • Coordinate surgical services with rescue organizations, transport partners, community veterinarians, and TNR programs.
  • Maintain strong communication with external veterinary partners.
  • Support community access-to-care initiatives and surrender prevention programs.

Regulatory Compliance

  • Ensure OSHA compliance within the surgery department.
  • Maintain AAHA-inspired standards where applicable.
  • Ensure proper sterilization and infection prevention protocols.
  • Monitor compliance with controlled substance regulations.
  • Ensure all surgery staff follow biosecurity and disease-control protocols.

Leadership Competencies

  • Lead with integrity and professionalism.
  • Inspire a culture of accountability.
  • Develop others through coaching and mentorship.
  • Make timely, evidence-based decisions.
  • Adapt quickly in a high-volume environment.
  • Anticipate operational challenges before they occur.
  • Communicate effectively across all departments.
  • Maintain a calm and organized presence during high-stress situations.
  • Supporting additional organizational needs as they arise

What Makes Someone Successful in This Role

We’re looking for someone who:

  • Is passionate about CAC’s mission and animal welfare
  • Brings a positive, team-first attitude
  • Communicates openly and professionally
  • Takes ownership and solves problems proactively
  • Thrives in a fast-paced, ever-changing environment
  • Can balance compassion with accountability
  • Is dependable, adaptable, and eager to learn

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

  • Minimum three years of leadership experience in veterinary medicine or animal welfare.
  • Minimum five years of veterinary clinical experience.
  • Demonstrated experience supervising teams.
  • Experience managing workflow in a fast-paced environment.
  • Strong organizational and project management skills.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication.
  • Computer proficiency including Microsoft Office and shelter software.
  • Ability to analyze operational data and implement process improvements.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Registered Veterinary Technician (RVT/LVT/CVT)
  • Veterinary Technician Specialist (preferred but not required)
  • Shelter medicine experience
  • High-volume spay/neuter experience
  • Anesthesia monitoring experience
  • Inventory management experience
  • Experience managing departmental budgets
  • Grant reporting experience

Why Join CAC?

At CAC, you’ll be part of more than just a workplace. You’ll join a team of people doing meaningful work together.

We offer:

  • The opportunity to make a real difference every day
  • A mission-driven, supportive team culture
  • Growth and development opportunities
  • Competitive benefits package
  • A workplace where your work directly impacts animals and the community

Benefits

  • Retirement plan with employer match
  • Health, Dental, and Vision Insurance
  • Paid Time Off
  • Life Insurance

Working Conditions / Physical Requirements

  • Lift up to 50 pounds.
  • Safely restrain dogs and cats of varying sizes.
  • Stand for extended periods during surgical procedures.
  • Perform repetitive bending, lifting, and reaching.

  • Manage Windows, iOS/iPadOS, Android, and corporate endpoint devices.
  • Configure device enrollment, compliance policies, configuration profiles, security policies, and application deployment.
  • Support Windows Autopilot, MAM, and endpoint security policies.
  • Integrate Intune with Microsoft Entra ID, Conditional Access, and Microsoft Defender.
  • Troubleshoot device enrollment, compliance, policy, application, and authentication issues.
  • Support certificate deployment to endpoints through Intune and enterprise PKI.

title: Quality Assurance Analyst
description:
Title: Quality Assurance Analyst

Compensation: $60-72k

Location: College Park, Georgia

Benefits: Medical, Dental, Vision, FSA/HSA

About the Company:
Nitro is a Brazilian multinational that marked 90 years in business in 2025, tracing its roots back to its founding in 1935. The company is recognized as a pioneer in Brazil's modern chemical industry and is one of the country's largest suppliers of nitrocellulose. Nitro serves clients in more than 70 countries and operates in Brazil, Uruguay, the United States, and Europe. Since 2019, the company has expanded into agribusiness specialty products through the acquisition of several units, broadening its portfolio to serve all of Brazil. In recent years, Nitro has seen strong growth, with revenue increasing more than 30% annually and sales growth exceeding 40%, supported by a workforce of over 1,200 employees.

In the U.S., Nitro operates as Nitro Quimica Corporation, located at 2300 West Point Avenue in the Atlanta, Georgia area (College Park), where the company supports its North American operations and customer base.

Job Summary:
The Quality Assurance Analyst plays a critical role in supporting Nitro's quality management system across the Quality Control Laboratory and broader manufacturing operations. This position is responsible for reviewing and approving analytical and batch documentation, verifying compliance with established procedures and specifications, and driving continuous improvement in quality processes—particularly for pharmaceutical raw materials, in-process materials, and finished products. The role also owns document control and training records within MasterControl, and supports FDA and ISO 9001 compliance through internal and external quality audits. As a key member of the Quality team, this role works cross-functionally with the laboratory, production, and customer-facing teams to ensure every batch and shipment meets Nitro's quality standards prior to release.

Job Duties and Responsibilities:

Quality Review & Release

  • Review and approve contract and internal laboratory results for raw materials and finished products.
  • Review testing status and approve pharmaceutical raw materials prior to use in production.
  • Review and approve labeled raw material containers and finished product drums prior to shipment.
  • Confirm and sign off on pharmaceutical production batches, verifying compliance with specifications.

Documentation & Batch Records

  • Prepare and maintain pharmaceutical batch documentation for use in manufacturing.
  • Review, verify, and file completed pharmaceutical batch documentation for accuracy and completeness.
  • Maintain accurate records of testing, retesting, and approval status for incoming raw materials.

Document Control & Training

  • Own document control processes within MasterControl, including creation, revision, routing, and approval of SOPs, specifications, and quality records.
  • Maintain and audit employee training records to ensure completion and compliance with current procedures.
  • Coordinate training assignments in MasterControl when documents are created or revised, and track completion status.
  • Ensure documentation practices meet FDA requirements for OTC pharmaceutical manufacturing and ISO 9001 record-keeping standards.

Regulatory Compliance & Audits

  • Support compliance with FDA regulations applicable to OTC pharmaceutical manufacturing (21 CFR 210/211) and the site's ISO 9001 quality management system.
  • Plan, lead, and conduct internal quality audits; support external and regulatory audits and inspections.
  • Identify audit findings and nonconformances, and track corrective and preventive actions (CAPA) to closure.
  • Support maintenance and continuous improvement of the quality management system to sustain FDA and ISO 9001 compliance.

Laboratory & Quality Systems Oversight

  • Oversee and coordinate analytical and physical testing performed in support of production batches (lacquer, acid, and topical pharmaceutical batches), including methods such as gas chromatography and HPLC.
  • Coordinate sampling of pharmaceutical raw materials upon receipt.
  • Manage submission and tracking of active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) testing.
  • Monitor and maintain calibration schedules for laboratory instrumentation (gas chromatographs, HPLC, balances, standard thermometers, etc.), including Operational Qualification and Preventative Maintenance due dates.
  • Perform and document instrument calibrations according to the analytical plan.

Cross-Functional & Customer Support

  • Prepare developmental samples for customer evaluation.
  • Package finished product and developmental samples for shipping.
  • Serve as a technical resource for contract laboratories, customers, and internal personnel on quality-related questions.
  • Support laboratory organization, consumable inventory, and overall lab readiness.

Requirements:

  • Bachelor's degree in Chemistry or a related science (Biology, Biochemistry, Chemical Engineering) required.
  • Minimum of 6 months of experience in an analytical laboratory or quality environment.
  • Working knowledge of FDA regulations as applied to OTC pharmaceutical manufacturing (21 CFR 210/211) required.
  • Working knowledge of ISO 9001 quality management system requirements required.
  • Experience with document control and training record management, preferably within MasterControl or a similar electronic quality management system.
  • Internal or external quality audit experience required; Lead Auditor certification (e.g., ISO 9001 Lead Auditor) strongly preferred.
  • Working knowledge of analytical and organic testing methods and laboratory safety practices.
  • Fluent in English.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills.
  • Critical thinking and investigative skills.
  • Highly organized with strong attention to detail.
  • Demonstrated ability to work effectively as part of a team.

This search is being conducted by Flex HR on behalf of Nitro. Qualified candidates should submit a resume within.

Flex HR uses AI for document preparation and meeting transcription only — never to screen or evaluate candidates. All hiring decisions are made by a human recruiter. Roles may be posted on platforms like Indeed or LinkedIn, which are independent companies that may use AI in their own technology.

title: Commis I Pastry
description:
Job Summary


The Commis I Pastry Chef is responsible for assisting in the daily preparation, production, and presentation of pastries, desserts, cakes, breads, and other baked items in accordance with established recipes, quality standards, and presentation guidelines. Working under the guidance of the Chef de Partie and senior pastry team, the role requires a good understanding of pastry techniques, the ability to execute routine tasks with minimal supervision, and a commitment to maintaining food safety, hygiene, and operational efficiency.


Main Tasks and Responsibilities


1. Preparation and Production


  • Prepare and process ingredients for pastries, desserts, cakes, breads, and other bakery products, ensuring accurate weighing, measuring, and portioning.


  • Execute standard pastry techniques, including mixing, whipping, folding, kneading, rolling, laminating, piping, and shaping, in accordance with established recipes.


  • Prepare a variety of pastry products, including cookies, tarts, cakes, mousses, creams, custards, fillings, sauces, and other desserts, according to the outlet's requirements.


  • Prepare and assemble basic plated desserts and pastry items while maintaining consistency in taste, texture, portion size, and presentation.


  • Follow production plans, recipes, and instructions provided by the Chef de Partie to ensure timely preparation and availability of products.


2. Baking, Finishing, and Quality Control


  • Monitor baking, proofing, cooling, chilling, and setting processes to achieve the required product quality.


  • Apply appropriate finishing and decoration techniques to cakes, pastries, and desserts in line with established presentation standards.


  • Check the freshness, appearance, taste, texture, and consistency of ingredients and finished products, reporting any deviations to the Chef de Partie.


  • Ensure that all pastry products are prepared according to approved recipes, specifications, and portion-control requirements.


  • Assist with the preparation and presentation of buffet displays, dessert counters, afternoon tea items, and other pastry requirements as directed.


3. Mise en Place and Section Organization


  • Complete daily mise en place requirements and ensure that all ingredients, tools, and equipment are ready before production and service.


  • Organize the workstation efficiently to support smooth workflow and timely delivery of pastry items.


  • Maintain proper labelling, dating, storage, and rotation of ingredients and finished products in accordance with FIFO principles and food safety procedures.


  • Monitor stock levels of frequently used ingredients and inform the Chef de Partie of shortages, damaged goods, or products requiring replenishment.


  • Assist in receiving, checking, and storing deliveries as required.


4. Hygiene, Food Safety, and Equipment Care


  • Maintain a clean, organized, and hygienic workstation throughout preparation, production, and service.


  • Comply with HACCP procedures, food safety policies, personal hygiene requirements, and applicable local regulations.


  • Ensure correct temperature control, allergen handling, cross-contamination prevention, and safe storage of food products.


  • Clean and maintain pastry tools, machinery, utensils, and equipment according to established procedures.


  • Report equipment malfunctions, food safety concerns, and potential hazards promptly to the Chef de Partie.


5. Teamwork and Operational Support


  • Work closely with the pastry team and other kitchen team members to ensure efficient production and smooth service.


  • Follow instructions, production schedules, and established kitchen procedures while demonstrating reliability and a professional attitude.


  • Assist with the timely preparation and replenishment of pastry items during restaurant service, banquets, buffets, and special events.


  • Communicate effectively with the team regarding production progress, stock requirements, and any issues affecting service.


6. Cost Control and Waste Management


  • Follow standard recipes and portion specifications to maintain product consistency and control food costs.


  • Handle ingredients carefully to minimize spoilage, unnecessary waste, and product loss.


  • Use ingredients efficiently and ensure that surplus products are stored, reused, or discarded only in accordance with approved food safety procedures.


  • Support stock rotation, inventory checks, and responsible use of kitchen supplies.


7. Learning and Development


  • Continue developing pastry knowledge and technical skills under the guidance of senior pastry chefs.


  • Stay informed about menu changes, seasonal products, recipes, and presentation standards.


  • Participate in training sessions, product tastings, and departmental briefings as required.


  • Demonstrate initiative in improving technical skills, productivity, and product quality.


  • Carry out any other reasonable duties assigned by the Chef de Partie or Pastry Chef in support of the department's operations.

title: Internship Opportunities
description:
Disability Law Colorado (DLC) is a statewide, nonprofit organization dedicated to securing the rights of the more than one million Coloradans with disabilities. As Colorado’s Protection and Advocacy System, we use our federal authority to root out discrimination, abuse, and neglect—from schools to prisons, nursing homes to voting booths. For more information, visit disabilitylawco.org.


Key Responsibilities
Disability Law Colorado accepts internship applicants in the following areas: legal interns/externs, social work, public policy, fundraising and development, marketing, and business administration.
Generally, interns will work to support advocacy on behalf of people with disabilities. This may include work relating to housing discrimination, employment discrimination, the Division of Vocational Rehabilitation, voting access, Medicaid, access to transportation, conditions in facilities, and students with disabilities who are in or at risk of entering the school-to-prison pipeline. As the state's protection and advocacy system, Disability Law Colorado also monitors facilities where individuals with disabilities receive services. Interns may have an opportunity to participate in monitoring visits based on level of interest.
Specifically, based on internship area, interns will:
• Legal: conduct research, draft legal memos, review records, develop policy recommendations, and/or assist with both individual and systemic case work.
• Social work: assist in assessing individual factors that contribute to person’s well-being and disability-related needs, conduct research, and/or assist with both individual and systemic work.
• Public policy: review policy, conduct research, make policy recommendations, draft policy language, and/or meet with key stakeholders regarding policy initiatives.
• Fundraising and development: assist with fundraising and donor campaigns, support outreach to sponsors and foundations, assist in building giving platforms, and/or design donor-facing emails.
• Marketing: work on social media accounts, support creation of digital and print materials, assist with website development, identify media contacts, and/or work on branding.
• Business administration: assist in developing and implementing business development strategies and initiatives, learn about grant reporting, and/or work to support DLC’s staff.


Required Qualifications


• Legal interns/externs must be enrolled in an accredited law school, and social work interns must be enrolled in an accredited social work program.
• Excellent communication, organizational, and research skills.
• Passion for disability justice, equity, and self-advocacy.


Preferred Qualifications


• Fluency in Spanish.


Work Environment


DLC is promoting a mostly remote work environment, with the understanding that interns may travel and meet in person as needed for conducting their job functions and collaborating with other staff members, clients, and partners. DLC also currently has office space in Denver, which may be available for intern use upon request.


Compensation and Benefits


DLC is only able to accommodate unpaid internships at this time. Interns can seek school credit or other stipends for their work and DLC is happy to meet or consider any requirements necessary for these opportunities. Interns can work flexible hours based on their schedules and credit requirements if seeking credit.
