title: Production Project Manager — Pool Construction
location: West Palm Beach, Florida, United States
description:
About Us

Craft Master Custom Pools has been building custom gunite pools in Southeast Florida since 1994 — more than 3,000 pools across Palm Beach, Martin, St. Lucie and Broward counties.

Here is the part most job postings leave out. This is a legacy company under new ownership, and we are writing our playbook one day at a time. The reputation and the craft are thirty years old; the systems around them are being built right now, by us, this year. Some of what you need in this role will not exist yet when you start — you will help build it.

That is either exactly the job you want or exactly the one you don't, and we would rather you know which before you apply.


Role Summary

You own job-level profit and loss on 20 pool construction projects simultaneously. You live in JobTread tracking costs, approving change orders, and preventing scope creep before it bleeds margin. You pair daily with a Field Supervisor who owns execution; you own the P&L. Together, you catch problems early and move fast.


Most pool firms treat this as a scorekeeper role—someone who runs reports after the damage is done. We don't. We need someone who is proactive about finding cost and schedule risks, then does something about them before they become crises.


Owned Accountabilities

  • Job P&L ownership. Every job closes at or above the bid margin. You track actual cost vs. estimate in JobTread daily. You spot variances ($1,500+) in real time, not in month-end reports. You own material-cost coding, labor variance analysis, and warranty claims allocation.
  • Change order velocity. You price change orders, not the office. You get them in front of the client within 48 hours of the request. You confirm client signature within 72 hours. You know the contract cold—what's in scope, what triggers a CO, and what doesn't.
  • Scope control. You say "no, that's out of scope" to clients and make it stick. You have the contract reference and the cost backup. You prevent the slow scope creep that kills margins on otherwise solid jobs.
  • Client communication. You're the first call when a cost risk surfaces, a change is needed, or a delay hits the schedule. You own the tone—honest, factual, fast. You call subs and clients before problems become crises. You listen for what they're not saying (frustration, confusion, unmet expectations).
  • JobTread mastery. You manage job costing and revenue recognition daily. You code purchases by job and cost code correctly on first entry (not catching mistakes weeks later). You run your own cost reports and trend analysis. If you're waiting for the office to run a report, this role isn't right for you.
  • Daily partnership with Field Supervisor. You talk to your assigned Supervisor every day. You flag cost risks together. You coordinate change orders and material delivery against the schedule. You're united on scope and timeline—the client hears one message from both of you.


Required Qualifications

  • Pool construction experience. You've worked in pool construction (residential or commercial) for at least 3 years. You understand the materials, the trades, the typical cost drivers, and the schedule rhythms. You can challenge a plumbing sub's invoice or spot an error in a decking estimate. You know what to expect when permits slip or weather delays framing.
  • JobTread mastery. You have hands-on experience in JobTread. Not "I've seen someone use it" — you've managed job costing, run cost reports, and coded purchases. You move through JobTread confidently and know how to find and fix cost variances. If your JobTread experience is light, we will ask for examples.
  • Change order management. You've written, priced, and tracked change orders in a construction business. You understand contract language well enough to spot whether something is in scope or not. You know how to talk to clients about cost changes without sounding defensive or apologetic.
  • Comfort with numbers. You're not intimidated by cost analysis, variance reports, or P&L tracking. You can do math without a calculator and catch a $500 error in a $50,000 estimate. You think in margin percentages, not just totals.
  • Proactive communication skills. You pick up the phone instead of sending emails when there's a problem. You deliver bad news clearly and early. You listen for what clients and subs need and anticipate pushback before they voice it. You prefer talking to writing; detail is backed by conversation.
  • Attention to detail. You live in details and like it. You catch small errors before they compound. You follow up on loose ends. You maintain systems and checklists because they keep things from falling through cracks.


Preferred Qualifications

  • Southeast Florida pool market experience. You know the permit timelines, the subcontractor network, the material suppliers, and the seasonal workflows in our region. You have relationships.
  • Multi-job portfolio management. You've managed 15+ concurrent jobs and know how to prioritize where your attention matters most.
  • Warranty and service cost tracking. You've calculated warranty claims by job type and reason, and understand how to prevent repeat failures.
  • Supplier relationship management. You've negotiated terms with vendors and tracked pricing trends to improve margins over time.
  • Experience pairing with field supervisors or site managers. You know how to work with someone whose primary job is on-site execution. You don't duplicate their work; you feed them information and they feed you problems to solve.
  • Conflict resolution with clients and subs. You've navigated disputes, walked people back from bad decisions, and maintained relationships while holding firm on scope and budget.


Who Succeeds Here / Who Doesn't

You'll Thrive in This Role If:

  • You enjoy living in the details and spotting problems before they blow up.
  • You're comfortable delivering hard truths (to clients, to subs, to leadership) in a respectful way.
  • You think in systems and checklists—not because you're rigid, but because systems catch mistakes.
  • You prefer solving problems to documenting them. You move fast and correct course as you learn.
  • You like working with a Field Supervisor as an equal partner. You give feedback, they give feedback, you both own the outcome.
  • You're energized by preventing crises, not putting them out.
  • You're OK with phone calls and brief, frequent check-ins over long written reports.


You're Not a Fit If:

  • You need someone else to own the numbers. (You own them here.)
  • You avoid difficult conversations or prefer to stay out of conflict.
  • You think "that's how construction is" instead of asking "how do we do this better?"
  • You prefer field work to office work. This is an office-based role.
  • You want clear, step-by-step direction on every task. You'll be working with autonomy and expected to anticipate what needs attention.
  • You see change orders as paperwork to process, not as the heartbeat of margin protection.
  • You think a PM's job is to keep everyone happy. (It's to keep the job profitable.)
  • You need 6+ weeks to close out a job's numbers.

title: GTM Marketer

title: Onboarding Project Coordinator
description:
This role is open to candidates based in LATAM, Africa, and Eastern Europe. Please note that as this role supports U.S.-based clients, candidates must be available to work during U.S. business hours aligned with the client’s time zone.


Our client is a family-owned third-party logistics (3PL) provider specializing in eCommerce fulfillment, warehousing, and B2B retail distribution. The company supports client onboarding, retailer integrations, and fulfillment operations, with a focus on maintaining accurate processes and meeting retailer compliance requirements.


Role Overview

The Onboarding Project Coordinator will manage the execution and coordination of client onboarding activities and SPS Commerce integrations, ensuring retailer connections are configured correctly, transactions are monitored, and onboarding projects remain on schedule. This role involves troubleshooting EDI errors, coordinating with internal teams, maintaining project documentation, and supporting successful client launches.


The ideal candidate has hands-on SPS Commerce Fulfillment experience, strong project coordination skills, and practical experience using AI tools to improve operational workflows. This individual will work closely with the Onboarding Project Manager, Client Services, Operations, and Finance, with responsibilities divided approximately between SPS/EDI execution (50%), onboarding coordination (30%), and AI-driven reporting and automation (20%).


Location

Fully Remote (Work from Home) | 9:00 AM - 5:00 PM EST


Key ResponsibilitiesSPS Commerce & EDI Execution

  • Set up and test retailer connections in SPS Commerce, including EDI 850 purchase orders, 856 advance shipping notices (ASN), 810 invoices, 846 inventory, and 855/860 documents as required.


  • Manage trading partner requirements and retailer routing guides to ensure compliance.


  • Monitor SPS Commerce daily for failed or rejected transactions and resolve missing SCAC/BOL information, ASN errors, and duplicate purchase orders.


  • Identify and resolve transaction issues before they result in retailer chargebacks.


  • Coordinate GS1-128/UCC-128 compliance label and packing list testing with Operations.


  • Research retailer chargebacks and prepare root-cause and credit analyses for Client Services and Finance.


  • Track SPS support tickets and maintain accurate retailer connection statuses in project trackers.


Client Onboarding & Project Coordination

  • Maintain onboarding checklists and project trackers for new clients and sites, including Houston.


  • Schedule kickoff, integration, and go-live calls with clients and internal stakeholders.


  • Document meeting notes, publish action items, and follow up with responsible team members.


  • Collect client setup information, including item masters, SKU and kit configurations, forecasts, carrier accounts, ship-to details, and location IDs.


  • Execute bulk order updates and data corrections in the Logistics Portal under the Onboarding Project Manager's direction.


  • Prepare complete onboarding handoff documentation to support Account Managers in taking ownership of client relationships.


AI-Driven Reporting & Data Analysis

  • Use Claude and Qlik data to analyze purchase order, ASN, and order exports.


  • Identify and summarize recurring transaction errors and operational patterns.


  • Develop and maintain reusable AI prompts, skills, and templates for onboarding status updates, SPS error triage, and handoff documentation.


  • Use operational data and AI tools to improve reporting accuracy and streamline recurring tasks.


Process Documentation & Team Enablement

  • Create concise job aids and standard operating procedures (SOPs) for routine SPS Commerce processes.


  • Develop documentation that enables Account Managers to independently resolve common SPS questions.


  • Maintain organized onboarding resources, process templates, and operational documentation.


  • Identify opportunities to improve recurring onboarding and EDI workflows through reusable resources and automation.


QualificationsExperience

  • 2+ years of hands-on SPS Commerce Fulfillment experience within a 3PL, brand, or retailer environment, including end-to-end onboarding of new trading partners.


  • Experience working with core EDI documents, including 850, 855, 856, 810, and 846, as well as retailer routing guides and compliance requirements.


  • Familiarity with retailer requirements for Target, Costco, TJX, UNFI, and department stores.


  • Experience troubleshooting ASN and invoice rejections and documenting retailer chargeback disputes.


  • Practical experience using Claude, ChatGPT, or similar AI tools daily to analyze data exports, draft client communications, and develop reusable prompts or templates.

Skills

title: Senior Audit Associate / Audit Senior - Agribusiness
location: New Ulm or Plymouth, Minnesota, United States
description:
Senior Audit Associate / Audit Senior – Agribusiness


Location: New Ulm or Plymouth, Minnesota
Work Arrangement: Hybrid or on-site
Employment Type: Full-time, exempt
Department: Assurance
Industry Focus: Agribusiness
Travel: Occasional travel regionally dependent on client needs and schedule


About the Opportunity


CarlsonSV is seeking an experienced Senior Audit Associate / Audit Senior – Agribusiness to join our Assurance team. This full-time public accounting role serves farmer cooperatives, grain elevators, and other agricultural organizations throughout western Minnesota and South Dakota and may be based in New Ulm or Plymouth, Minnesota, with hybrid work options available.


The ideal candidate has at least three years of public accounting audit experience and can lead financial statement audit engagements from planning and fieldwork through completion. You will work directly with agribusiness clients, manage engagement progress, prepare and review audit workpapers, apply professional judgment to accounting and auditing matters, mentor less experienced team members, and contribute to high-quality assurance services.


At CarlsonSV, we believe great work happens when talented people are trusted to take ownership, exercise sound judgment, and build a career that leaves room for life outside of work. If you are looking for meaningful leadership opportunities without sacrificing personal well-being, you will feel at home here.


Position Highlights


• Hybrid flexibility based out of our New Ulm or Plymouth offices, with complete workspace equipment provided for approved remote-work arrangements
• Generous paid time off with three weeks of PTO to start and eleven paid holidays, including three “Recharge Days”
• Comprehensive benefits including medical, dental, vision, HSA contributions for eligible employees, employer-paid life and disability insurance, and a 401(k) match
• Career growth through professional development, leadership opportunities, and profit sharing


Build Your Career Without Putting Life on Hold


At CarlsonSV, meaningful growth and a sustainable career go hand in hand. We support work-life balance through hybrid options, flexible scheduling, generous time off, and a culture of trust—so you can lead important client work while maintaining room for life outside of work. Full benefit details are outlined below.


Who We Are
CarlsonSV: Big firm strength. Small firm feel.


We are a growing public accounting and advisory firm that cares deeply about our clients, our people, and the work we do. We provide assurance and advisory, client accounting, tax, and wealth management services while building long-term relationships as trusted advisors.


We are large enough to offer a diverse client base, meaningful professional opportunities, and access to experienced leaders. We are also small enough that colleagues know one another, ideas are heard and considered by leadership, and individual contributions make a visible difference.


Our culture is grounded in four core values:


• Strong Work Ethic
• Expect Excellence
• Genuine Care
• Do the Right Thing


Why This Role Matters


The agribusiness industry is the backbone of many communities across Minnesota and South Dakota. Our clients include farmer cooperatives, grain elevators, and other agricultural organizations that play a vital role in supporting producers and rural economies.


We are looking for an experienced auditor who understands the importance of these businesses and the people behind them. Whether your connection to agriculture comes from professional experience, your upbringing, or a personal passion for the industry, you will find meaningful work helping clients succeed while building lasting relationships.


Job Responsibilities


As a Senior Audit Associate / Audit Senior, you will take an active leadership role in audit engagements from planning through completion. This position offers significant autonomy and client interaction, allowing you to make an immediate impact.


Key responsibilities include:


• Lead financial statement audit engagements, including audit planning, fieldwork, documentation, and completion.
• Manage engagement timelines, audit workpapers, open items, and communication with managers and partners.
• Work directly with agribusiness clients to understand their operations, assess audit-related matters, and build trusted relationships.
• Apply professional judgment, critical thinking, and auditing standards to resolve complex accounting and audit issues.
• Identify opportunities to improve audit efficiency, strengthen processes, and enhance client service.
• Work independently at client locations and confidently manage engagements when managers or partners are not on-site.
• Mentor, train, and support less experienced audit team members.


Required Qualifications


Required qualifications include:


• Three or more years of public accounting audit experience.
• Demonstrated ability to lead audit engagements from planning through completion.
• Ability to take ownership of assignments, manage engagement responsibilities, and work independently.
• Strong client-service, communication, relationship-building, critical-thinking, and professional-judgment skills.
• Commitment to accurate, high-quality audit work and exceptional client service.
• Ability to travel primarily throughout western Minnesota, with occasional travel into South Dakota.
• Genuine interest in agriculture, agribusiness, and the organizations that support producers and rural communities.


Preferred Qualifications


Agribusiness audit experience is preferred but not required. Experience with farmer cooperatives, grain elevators, agricultural organizations, farming operations, or the broader agriculture industry is highly valued.


Why CarlsonSV?


At CarlsonSV, you will find meaningful work with clients who are essential to their communities, greater responsibility and autonomy than you may find at larger firms, flexible work arrangements, and a collaborative culture built on trust, respect, and support. Our leaders value professional growth and personal well-being, giving you opportunities to build long-term client relationships and make a visible impact.


Compensation and Benefits


CarlsonSV offers competitive compensation that is reviewed regularly based on experience, qualifications, responsibilities, and market conditions.


Our benefits include:


• Profit-sharing opportunities that allow employees to share in the firm’s success
• Flexible scheduling and hybrid-work options
• Complete workspace equipment for approved remote-work arrangements
• Medical insurance, with CarlsonSV contributing toward employee premiums
• Dental and vision insurance
• Health Savings Account options, including up to $5000 employer contributions for eligible employees
• Flexible Spending Account, Limited FSA, and Dependent Care FSA options
• Employer-paid life insurance
• Employer-paid short-term and long-term disability insurance
• A 401(k) retirement plan with up to a 4% company match
• Three weeks of PTO to start, increasing with years of service and available as earned
• Eleven paid holidays, including three “Recharge Days”
• Professional certification support and eligible CPA examination reimbursement
• Professional development and leadership-development opportunities


Specific plan terms, eligibility requirements, employee contributions, and benefit amounts are governed by the applicable plan documents and CarlsonSV policies


Join Our Team


If you are an experienced auditor who is passionate about client service, enjoys taking ownership, and has an interest in agriculture, we would love to hear from you. Join a team that values your expertise, supports your growth, and gives you the opportunity to make a real difference in the agribusiness community.


Apply through CarlsonSV’s careers page by submitting your resume and completing the online application.

title: Director, Proposal Management and Pricing
description:
Overview

The Director, Proposal Management and Pricing is responsible for the end-to-end development of competitive, compelling proposals and the pricing strategy behind them for L5’s commissioning, facilities management & operations, and project management & retrofit service lines. This role will be responsible for developing both halves of the win: the proposal process (capture coordination, content strategy, compliance, and production) and the pricing process (cost modeling, margin strategy, and commercial structuring). It is a highly cross-functional role, partnering closely with business development, human resources, vendor management & procurement, operations, finance, and executive leadership to convert opportunities into profitable, signed contracts.

Responsibilities

Proposal Management

  • Own the proposal lifecycle from opportunity qualification through submission.
  • Develop win strategies, proposal outlines, and compliance matrices in partnership with business development leads.
  • Lead and facilitate kickoff meetings, storyboarding sessions and production schedules, holding contributors accountable to deadlines.
  • Write, edit, and position technical and management narrative content so it speaks directly to client evaluation criteria and win themes.
  • Manage a library of reusable proposal content, past performance references, resumes, and graphics; keep materials current and audit-ready.
  • Coordinate subcontractor and teaming partner inputs, ensuring consistency and compliance across the full submission.
  • Oversee final production, formatting, and quality assurance to ensure 100% compliance with RFP/RFQ requirements and on-time delivery.
  • Support oral presentation and interview preparation when pursuits advance to that stage.

Pricing & Commercial Strategy

  • Lead development of pricing models and cost estimates for commissioning, facilities management & operations, and project management/retrofit engagements, in partnership with operations and finance.
  • Translate scope, staffing plans, and service-level requirements into accurate, defensible cost build-ups and competitive pricing strategies.
  • Partner with finance and executive leadership to set margin targets, evaluate risk, and structure commercial terms (fixed fee, cost-plus, unit rate, etc.) appropriate to each pursuit.
  • Benchmark pricing against market and competitive intelligence to inform win-rate and margin trade-off decision.
  • Build and maintain standardized pricing tools, templates, and historical cost data to improve speed and consistency across pursuits.
  • Present pricing recommendations and risk considerations to executive leadership for go/no-go and final pricing approval.

Leadership & Process

  • Establish scalable proposal and pricing processes, templates, and governance suited to a fast-growing platform business.
  • Track and report win rates, pricing trends, and lessons learned to continuously improve proposal quality and pricing accuracy.
  • Serve as a key advisor to executive leadership on pursuit strategy, resourcing, and competitive positioning.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, Real Estate, or a related field; MBA a plus.
  • Experience in commercial real estate outsourcing, facilities management, data center operations, or mission-critical environments strongly preferred.
  • Demonstrated success leading complex, high-value proposals (RFP/RFQ/RFI) and developing competitive cost/pricing models in parallel.
  • Strong financial acumen, including cost estimating, margin analysis, and commercial contract structures.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate technical and operational detail into persuasive client-facing content.
  • Proven ability to indirectly lead cross-functional teams and manage multiple concurrent deadlines under pressure.
  • Proficiency with proposal and estimating tools (e.g., Microsoft Office/Excel, estimating or CRM/pipeline software).
  • Occasional travel for client meetings as needed.

What Success Looks Like

  • A repeatable, scalable proposal and pricing process that supports L5’s national growth.
  • Improved win rates and pricing accuracy driven by consistent processes, strong content, and disciplined cost modeling.
  • Strong, trusted working relationships across business development, operations, finance, and executive leadership.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local law.

title: Crime Victim Liaison
description:
GENERAL DESCRIPTION
The position of Crime Victim Liaison performs those statutory duties imposed
upon it by the Code of Criminal Procedure; Chapter 56, Subchapter A, Crime Victims’
Rights, and Subchapter B, Crime Victim’s Compensation.
Subchapter A., Article 56.04 (d), establishes that the primary duties of the Crime
Victim Liaison are to ensure that a victim, guardian of a victim, or close relative of a
deceased victim are afforded the rights granted to victims, guardians, or close relatives
of deceased victims by Subdivisions (4),(6), and (9) of Article 56.02 (a) (4) of the Code of
Criminal Procedure.
These primary duties shall be performed in consultation with the Victim
Assistance Coordinator in the office of the attorney representing the state in the related
criminal cases to ensure compliance with state statutes and enhance effectiveness in
meeting the crime victim assistance standards established by the Texas Department of
Criminal Justice, Victim Services Division.
ESSENTIAL RESPONSIBILITIES AND DUTIES
1 (20%) The Crime Victim Liaison will ensure that those victims covered under
Article 56.02 (a)(4) of the code are afforded the right to be informed, when
requested, by a peace officer concerning the defendant’s right to bail and the
procedures involved in criminal investigations; and by the district attorney’s office
concerning the general procedures in the criminal justice system, including
general procedures in guilty plea negotiations and arrangements, restitution, and
the appeals and parole process.
2 (20%) The Crime Victim Liaison will ensure that those victims covered under
Article 56.02 (a)(6) of the code are informed of the right to receive information
regarding compensation as provided by Subchapter B, including information
related to the cost that may be compensated under that subchapter and the
amount of compensation, eligibility for compensation, and the procedures for
application for compensation under that subchapter, the payment for medical
examination under Article 56.06 for a victim of sexual assault, and when
requested, to referral to available social service agencies that may offer
additional assistance.
3 (20%) The Crime Victim Liaison will ensure that those victims covered under
Article 56.02 (a)(9) of the code are afforded the right to prompt return of any
property of the victim that is held by a law enforcement agency or the attorney for
the state as evidence when the property is no longer required for that purpose.

4 (20%) The Crime Victim Liaison will ensure that the Victim Coordinator for the
attorney representing the state receives immediate cooperation and support in
providing effective assistance to a victim as defined in Chapter 56 of the Code of
Criminal Procedure.
5 (10%) The Crime Victim Liaison will comply with all local, state, and federal
statutes related to the duties of the position held.
ADDITIONAL RESPONSIBILITIES
Items 1-9 below will constitute approximately 10% of grant funded activities.
1 Regular attendance is required.
2 Maintain a valid Texas Operators License
3 Must be bondable by county insurance carrier
4 Must be able to comply with county employee and Sheriff’s Office policies and
procedures.
5 Compile and maintain all necessary documentation required for grant position
reporting when required.
6 Compliance with state statutes related to records management.
7 Ability to testify in court proceedings in an objective and articulate manner.
8 Maintain training requirements related to the position held.
9 Establish and maintain effective working relationships with other county
employees and officials, court personnel, attorneys, and representatives of victim
assistance/advocacy groups.
10 Experienced in making community outreach presentations in various public
forums to enhance awareness of the services available to crime victims.
EDUCATION REQUIREMENTS
High school diploma or equivalent is required.
Previous formalized training in fields related to victim assistance liaison duties is
desirable.

EXPERIENCE AND SKILLS
 Working knowledge of Chapter 56 of the Texas Code of Criminal Procedure as it
relates to crime victim rights and crime victim compensation.
 Previous experience in victim’s assistance, victim’s compensation, social service,
criminal justice, or related field is desirable.
 High level of maturity and compassion in dealing with crime victims.
 Excellent communication, counseling, and interviewing skills.
 Ability to read, analyze and interpret general business periodicals, professional
journals, technical procedures, and government regulations relative to the
position of Crime Victim Liaison.
 Working knowledge of computers and the ability to learn county computer
programs related to duties.
 Excellent organizational skills are desirable.
PHYSICAL DEMANDS AND WORK ENVIRONMENT

The position of Crime Victim Liaison will require frequent travel outside of an office
environment in order to provide effective victim’s assistance. The physical demands
described here are representative of those that must be met to successfully perform
the essential duties of this position. While performing the duties of this position the
employee is frequently required to see, talk, hear, stand, kneel, climb, feel, utilize fingers to handle and arms to reach and carry. The employee must be able to lift up
to fifteen (15) pounds regularly and up to forty (40) pounds occasionally. Specific
vision required for this job includes both near and distance vision.


SPECIAL CONDITIONS
The position of Crime Victim Liaison will be in constant contact with sensitive
information related to crime victims which demands a high level of confidentiality.
The person that occupies this position must be able to demonstrate trustworthiness
by successfully passing an extensive background investigation prior to being considered for employment.
To fulfill the duties of the Crime Victim Liaison it may be necessary to work irregular duty hours and on weekends to ensure timely completion of related job
responsibilities

title: Returns Coordinator
description:
POSITION PROFILE


To oversee and manage the end-to-end processing of returned pharmaceutical products and medical

supplies. The Returns Coordinator ensures that all returned goods are processed accurately, customer

credits are initiated promptly, and product disposition (return to stock, quarantine, or destruction) strictly complies with healthcare regulations, Good Distribution Practices (GDP), and company policies.


JOB DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES


· Manage the daily operations of the returns department and coordinate the workflow of Returns

Associates.

· Review, verify, and approve Return Merchandise Authorizations (RMAs) against physical goods

received.

· Liaise directly with Customer Service, Sales, and Quality Assurance to investigate the root causes

of returns (e.g., damages, short dating, cold-chain breaches, product recalls).

· Ensure strict compliance with pharmaceutical guidelines when assessing the integrity,

temperature history, and safety of returned items.

· Process accurate data entry into the Warehouse Management System (WMS) or ERP to adjust

inventory levels and authorize customer credits.

· Coordinate the secure transfer of defective, recalled, or expired items to the quarantined area

and maintain accurate logs of these items.

· Assist with the documentation and regulatory compliance process for the certified destruction

of pharmaceutical products.

· Oversee the safe restocking of approved, saleable returned goods back into the active picking

environment.

· Generate weekly and monthly reports analyzing return volumes, root causes, and processing

times.

· Partake in and supervise cycle counts and general stock counts within the returns and

quarantine zones.

· Perform any other related duties that may be assigned.


PERFORMANCE STANDARDS

· Timely processing of all returns and customer credit authorizations within the established Service Level Agreement (SLA).

· 100% compliance with quality and regulatory standards for separating saleable stock from

quarantined/hazardous stock.

· Accurate maintenance of WMS inventory records reflecting returned goods.


QUALIFICATIONS (EDUCATION, EXPERIENCE & CERTIFICATIONS)


· An Associate’s Degree or Diploma in Logistics, Supply Chain Management, Business Administration,

or a related field.

·At least three (3) years of working experience in Inventory Management, Reverse Logistics, or Quality

Assurance, preferably within a pharmaceutical or healthcare warehouse.

· Strong IT systems knowledge, specifically with WMS and ERP software.

· Experience in leading or coordinating team activities.

title: Community Living Full-Time
description:
JOB PURPOSE

This position is responsible for providing support to individuals, within their daily lives, as needed.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • High School Diploma or equivalent
  • College preferred
  • Experience working with people with disabilities preferred

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Teach and assist persons served by The Arc of Southside, in completing activities associated with daily living; those activities include, but are not limited to: cooking, cleaning, laundry, hygiene, meal planning and preparation, grocery shopping, banking, transportation, obtaining and giving medications as prescribed, relocation, medical appointments, accessing community resources, socialization, etc.
  • Use personal vehicle during work hours, as needed, to carry out services as described.
  • Provide support and skill building, to individual’s served by The Arc of Southside, as defined by each person’s Individual Support Plan.
  • Assist persons served, in integrating into the community, and spending leisure time engaged in activities that the individual enjoys.
  • Provide guidance and behavioral support; be able to read, understand, and implement behavioral support plans/interventions, as described, for each individual.
  • Provide emergency first aid, should occasion arise, and assist persons served in obtaining prompt medical attention from a qualified professional, when necessary.
  • Document services provided, and ensure the confidentiality of information and records pertaining to persons served.
  • Respond to emergency situations and provide crisis intervention, as needed.
  • Adhere to The Arc of Southside Employee Code of Ethics and Supported Living Guidelines.
  • Serve as a liaison, on behalf of persons served, with family members, other agencies, and the general community, and represent the agency in a professional and positive manner in all interactions.
  • Complete required non-service related forms such as payroll and mileage sheets.
  • Attend team meetings, agency-wide meetings, agency-wide retreats, and other meetings, trainings, in-services, etc., as scheduled.
  • Utilize phone, text, and email as a means of efficient communication
  • Perform functions necessary for the maintenance of the individual’s residential environment.
  • Report maintenance or repair needs of the homes of persons served.
  • Follow agency policies, as they currently exist, and participate in the development and implementation of future agency policies and goals.

COMPETENCIES

  • Ability to organize and prioritize work tasks.
  • Ability to work effectively in a team.
  • Ability to present self professionally.
  • Ability to self-direct work.
  • Ability to communicate effectively, both orally and in writing.
  • Knowledge of the field of disabilities.
  • Skill in the use of behavioral support practices.
  • Skill to complete satisfactorily: Medication Certification, Medicaid Waiver Certification, First Aid/CPR, TOVA and other requirements associated with orientation.
  • Skill in decision making, judgment and action in emergency or crisis situations.
  • Skill in maintaining confidential information.
  • Skill in locating and accessing community resources.
  • Must have valid Virginia Driver’s License.
  • Must have a satisfactory criminal history check.





Leadership – Acts as a positive role-model and demonstrates strong leadership skills

Philosophy – Commitment to principles of Inclusion

Technical Skills – Ability to operate computers, email, and smart phone technology



PHYSICAL DEMANDS

Work requires a range of light to moderate physical exertion to assist persons supported with personal care, lifts, and transfers as needed. Work also requires assisting with toileting, changing linens, and other supports for individuals served in completing some activities, and other forms of physical exertion. Work requires the ability to concentrate and pay attention to detail for a majority of work time.

Ability to carry out the physical requirements of this position which include but are not limited to: lifting up to 50 pounds several times per shift as needed, ascending and descending stairs several times per shift, and sitting, standing, and walking for periods of time throughout a shift as needed.

Generally good working conditions with potential exposure to communicable diseases with little risk if proper procedures and safeguards are followed.

title: Outreach Coordinator
description:
OUTREACH COORDINATOR

Part-Time 20 Hours per Week



About Us: Building One Community (B1C) is a Stamford, Connecticut-based nonprofit supporting the successful integration of immigrants and their families. At B1C, immigrants acquire the tools they need to thrive. We provide free services that educate, employ, empower and engage immigrants and the broader community. Our programs include English Language classes, Family and Individual Support Services, Academic Enrichment Programs, Immigration Legal Services, and Workforce Development programs.



Position: The Outreach Coordinator plays a key role in expanding awareness of Building One Community (B1C) and connecting immigrant individuals and families throughout Fairfield County with B1C's programs, services, and resources. Reporting to the Community Engagement Manager, this part-time, 20-hour-per-week position is highly community-facing, implementing targeted outreach and engagement strategies to reach new participants, increase engagement, and strengthen B1C's presence in the communities we serve.

A significant portion of the role is spent in the field connecting directly with community members through outreach activities, events, tabling, and other community-based activities. The Coordinator works closely with B1C program teams to promote programs and services, reach specific communities and audiences, and gather participant feedback and community insights, ensuring outreach activities align with broader community partnership efforts.

The position has a flexible and field-based schedule, with hours that may include weekdays, evenings, and weekends based on community outreach activities and organizational events. Time may be spent in the field or at the B1C office for outreach planning, follow-up, data tracking, surveys, reporting, and administrative responsibilities.

Primary Duties:

  • Implement outreach and engagement activities that increase awareness of B1C and connect immigrant individuals and families with programs and services.
  • Maintain a consistent presence in priority communities and promote B1C programs and services through community organizations, local businesses, schools, faith communities, events, and trusted community networks.
  • Support participant recruitment and engagement through grassroots outreach, tabling, community events, and program promotion.
  • Serve as a visible B1C ambassador by representing the organization at community fairs, outreach events, meetings, and other local gatherings, and by delivering presentations to community groups and organizations.
  • Gather participant and community feedback through surveys, conversations, outreach activities, and events, and share relevant insights with B1C teams.
  • Identify new outreach opportunities, community gathering places, communication channels, and trusted messengers, and track outreach activities to assess which approaches are most effective in reaching and engaging participants.
  • Partner and collaborate with B1C program, development, and communications teams to understand outreach priorities, emerging needs and target audiences.
  • Support the planning and execution of major B1C organizational events and community engagement initiatives.
  • Maintain organized records of outreach activities, referrals, participant feedback, and community contacts.

Qualifications & Skills

  • Fluency in Spanish and English with demonstrated written and verbal communication skills required.
  • Associate's or bachelor's degree in Human Services, Community Engagement, or a related field preferred; equivalent experience may be considered.
  • Minimum of two years of experience in community outreach, community engagement, nonprofit work, or a related field.
  • Experience working with individuals and families from diverse cultural, linguistic, and socioeconomic backgrounds.
  • Excellent interpersonal, communication, organizational, and project management skills, including comfort delivering presentations to groups.
  • Comfortable working independently in community settings and representing B1C publicly.
  • Reliable transportation required for regular travel to community sites and events.
  • Availability to work some evenings and weekends based on outreach and event schedules.
  • Strong proficiency with Microsoft Office; familiarity with Salesforce or other database systems is a plus.
  • Commitment to B1C's mission, values, and goals.

Compensation & Benefits

B1C offers a competitive salary commensurate with experience, along with a comprehensive benefits package. B1C is an equal opportunity employer committed to building a diverse and inclusive team that reflects the community we serve.

Benefits include medical, dental and vision insurance, employer-sponsored life insurance, 401(k) with employer contribution, paid time off, paid holidays and other company-sponsored benefits.

Building One Community is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

title: Program Associate (Grants & Programs)
description:
JOB DESCRIPTION

TITLE: Program Associate

REPORTS TO: Senior Director of Grants & Programs

STATUS: Regular, Full-time, Non-Exempt

POSITION DESCRIPTION: The Program Associate will provide support that guides the grant distribution process and execution of programs through the review of proposals, interacting with prospective applicants and electronic record keeping. This position will play a meaningful role in supporting community groups working in our main areas of community concern and providing funding to address key community needs.

MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Assist with Community Grant proposal and grant processing. Includes:
    • Working directly with people seeking grant funding to provide clarification of Foundation priorities, assist them with the application process and share feedback with them on their proposals
    • Analyzing grant proposals through written materials, site visits, interviews with other funders and relevant agencies
    • Preparing and presenting written and oral analyses of grant recommendations for Community Foundation staff, board, donors and/or committee members
    • Reviewing grant reports as part of a team and updating grants database system with grant results
  • Assist with research and implementation of existing and new nonprofit capacity building programs. Includes:
    • Collecting information on needs within the nonprofit community
    • Assisting with events that bring together the nonprofit and residential communities, including Community Insights Forum and Nonprofit Speed Networking events
    • Coordinating with members of the Community Investment team to ensure thoughtful and impactful programming
  • Assist the Community Investment team with implementing various community initiatives, including grant portal and database administration
  • Conduct research on issues or concerns of importance to the Community Foundation
  • Participate in activities of the philanthropic field such as conferences and meetings to enhance overall operations

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Deep interest in and commitment to the Central New York area, its people and their concerns
  • Commitment to be guided in all work by the vision of diversity, equity and inclusion that has been established by our staff and board
  • Familiarity with the Central New York area, its opportunities and challenges
  • Relevant work experience a plus
  • Ability to work both independently and as an effective team member
  • Ability to organize and prioritize work and manage multiple priorities simultaneously
  • Willingness to learn and utilize any community foundation systems

TIME REQUIREMENT: This is a full-time, non-exempt position requiring 37.5 hours per week. Work hours are 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. with some flexibility. Tuesdays through Thursdays are designated in-office days. Staff that choose to work a hybrid work schedule may choose to do so on Mondays and/or Fridays, dependent on management approval. Occasionally, early, late or weekend hours are required for duties onsite and offsite.

BENEFITS: Salary range is $50,000-$55,000. Employee benefits include health insurance, annual vacation and sick days, 12 paid holidays, term life insurance, additional disability insurance, parking, 401(k) retirement savings program with employer contribution and match, optional flex spending accounts for medical or dependent care expenses and other benefits as outlined in the employee handbook.


DISCLAIMER:

This description should not be construed to contain every function or responsibility that may be required to be performed by an incumbent in this job classification. This job description is intended to be general and will evolve over time. The description is subject to periodic updating. At management’s discretion, the employee may be assigned different or additional duties from time to time.

title: Maintenance I - Clinics
description:

UnityPoint Health

Maintenance I - Clinics

Join a team dedicated to creating a safe and reliable healthcare environment. In this hands-on role, you will maintain and repair a wide range of building systems and clinical support equipment, perform preventive maintenance, and help ensure compliance with safety and regulatory standards. Working alongside colleagues and vendors, you’ll use your technical expertise, problem-solving skills, and commitment to service to support exceptional patient care while keeping critical hospital operations running smoothly.

Why UnityPoint Health?

At UnityPoint Health, you matter. We’re proud to be recognized as a Top 150 Place to Work in Healthcare by Becker's Healthcare several years in a row for our commitment to our team members.

Our competitive Total Rewards program offers benefits options that align with your needs and priorities, no matter what life stage you’re in. Here are just a few:

  • Expect paid time off, parental leave, 401K matching and an employee recognition program.
  • Dental and health insurance, paid holidays, short and long-term disability and more. We even offer pet insurance for your four-legged family members.
  • Early access to earned wages with Daily Pay, tuition reimbursement to help further your career and adoption assistance to help you grow your family.

With a collective goal to champion a culture of belonging where everyone feels valued and respected, we honor the ways people are unique and embrace what brings us together.

And, we believe equipping you with support and development opportunities is a vital part of delivering an exceptional employment experience.

Find a fulfilling career and make a difference with UnityPoint Health.

Responsibilities

  • Accepts and responds to work requests for general maintenance and repair of closures, mobile equipment, installed facility systems, various piping systems, minor plumbing, minor electrical, move requests, simple temperature complaints, and other assignments from management
  • Repairs and maintains facility equipment such as beds, wheelchairs, stretchers, kitchen appliances, exercise equipment, nurse call and other communication systems, as assigned
  • Performs minor carpentry, painting, plastering, and electro‑mechanical repairs; performs repairs and preventive maintenance on pneumatic tube systems and medical gas outlets
  • Ensures urgent requests are handled timely and that repairs are made correctly and completely while maintaining positive relationships and communications with patients, visitors, and staff
  • Keeps shops and mechanical rooms clean and free of unnecessary items; observes accepted procedures in the care and use of equipment and tools
  • Cooperates with supervisors and co‑workers to maintain equipment, parts, and supplies, and makes recommendations regarding desired changes in operation and maintenance procedures
  • Performs preventive maintenance orders for facility departments to ensure compliance with healthcare standards; updates and creates preventive maintenance schedules as equipment is installed
  • Inspects and initiates repairs to life safety equipment and systems including fire doors, fire/smoke walls, fire barriers, medical gas systems, egress and emergency lighting, fire sprinkler and suppression systems, and fire alarm systems
  • Understands, observes, and complies with all safety precautions and procedures; performs assigned duties during internal and external disasters, codes, and drills
  • Completes regulatory reports related to life safety equipment and systems and conducts Infection Control Risk Assessments, obtaining permits as required for work in patient areas
  • Utilizes logs and maintains documentation required in accordance with standard operating procedures and applicable authorities having jurisdiction
  • Records time, date, labor, and materials expended on jobs and maintains files of pertinent records on machinery and equipment in the work order maintenance system
  • Communicates with supervisors and co‑workers to achieve understanding in a positive manner; balances team and individual responsibilities, gives and welcomes feedback, and contributes to positive team goals.
  • Participates in department training groups and attends and teaches training subjects in formal, informal, computer‑based, and on‑the‑job settings; keeps informed through training and other sources to further job knowledge
  • Suggests improvements to equipment or management policies to supervisors; displays initiative and judgment in determining the extent of repairs and selecting appropriate materials, methods, and techniques
  • Maintains responsibility and accountability for knowledge of conditions of assigned mechanical equipment and assumes responsibility for timely completion of job responsibilities

Qualifications

Education:

  • High School Diploma/GED or equivalent job experience required.
  • Associate’s degree in industrial technologies or a related skilled trade (e.g., HVAC, electrical, electronics, mechanical); completion of a trade/technical school program or trade apprenticeship is preferred.

Experience:

  • Five (5) years’ experience in operations, including maintenance and/or repair, with familiarity with mechanical systems and building maintenance techniques for systems and equipment required.
  • Two (2) years safety systems/low voltage field experience preferred.
  • Four (4) years of healthcare/hospital maintenance experience preferred.
  • Five (5) years of maintenance experience in a commercial setting preferred.

License(s)/Certification(s):

  • Valid Iowa driver’s license for at least three years with an acceptable or clear rating according to the Motor Vehicle Record chart. (see below).
  • Must have a minimum of two years driving experience with no record of DUI, DWI, or similar alcohol or drug related offenses over the past five years.
  • No record of reckless driving, careless driving, speeding over 15 miles above the speed limit, fleeing or eluding a police officer, chemical test refusal, leaving the scene of an accident, driving after revocation or suspension, or passing a stopped school bus in the last five years.

title: Outcomes Coordinator
description:
Outcomes Coordinator

Reports to the Outcomes Manager


Join the Team at Cincinnati Animal CARE

At Cincinnati Animal CARE (CAC), we do work that matters.

Every day, our team protects animals, supports our community, and helps save thousands of lives each year through compassionate care, advocacy, and education.

This work is meaningful, fast-paced, and can be challenging, but for the right person, it’s incredibly rewarding.

We are a team built for impact, made up of people who care deeply, work hard, support one another, and show up every day committed to making a difference.

If you are passionate about animals, thrive in a mission-driven environment, and want your work to have purpose, we’d love to have you join us.


About the Role

We are looking for an Outcomes Coordinator to join our team and play an important role in supporting CAC’s mission.

In this position, you will:

  • Coordinate daily operations, ensure efficient workflow and maintain high levels of customer service to maximize live outcomes for shelter animals. You will also assist in tracking and analyzing data, managing placement logistics, and ensuring alignment with organizational objectives.

This is a great opportunity for someone who enjoys meaningful work, takes pride in helping others, and wants to contribute to a growing organization making a real impact in the community.


What You’ll Be Responsible For

Your day-to-day may include:

  • Facilitate animal placements through Adoption, Rescue, Return to Owner, or Transfer to Rescue, ensuring live outcomes with minimal shelter time.
  • Oversee the accurate completion of all adoption and outcome processes, including verifying medical records, microchips, and licenses.
  • Manage and maintain relationships with rescue partners, serving as the primary point of contact for the organization.
  • Monitor the program's success, using data to identify areas for improvement and suggest data-driven initiatives to enhance or expand the program.
  • Provide high-level customer service to visitors, adopters, and community members, handling inquiries and ensuring a positive experience.
  • Coordinate the scheduling of animal showings and releases, advocating for both the customer and the animal’s well-being.
  • Work with other departments - Medical, Behavior, Foster, Community Support, and Animal Care - to facilitate animal placements.
  • Assist in monitoring and maintaining program inventory, ensuring essential supplies are stocked and managed effectively.
  • Provide guidance to Outcomes Specialists, fostering a positive and collaborative work environment.
  • Educate the public and promote the organization’s mission, ensuring alignment with best practices and adoption philosophies.
  • Support new staff and volunteers in training, ensuring adherence to department protocols and standards.
  • Report any incidents or program needs promptly to the Outcomes Manager.
  • Perform other duties as assigned by the Outcomes Manager or other management staff.
  • Supporting additional organizational needs as they arise


What Makes Someone Successful in This Role

We’re looking for someone who:

  • Is passionate about CAC’s mission and animal welfare
  • Brings a positive, team-first attitude
  • Communicates openly and professionally
  • Takes ownership and solves problems proactively
  • Thrives in a fast-paced, ever-changing environment
  • Can balance compassion with accountability
  • Is dependable, adaptable, and eager to learn


Qualifications

Preferred/Required:

  • Minimum of 1-2 years of experience in animal welfare or a related field; experience in placements is preferred.
  • Strong understanding of basic animal behavior and progressive shelter practices.
  • Proven problem-solving skills with the ability to think critically and creatively.
  • Excellent communication skills, capable of engaging with diverse audiences within and outside the organization.
  • Ability to manage relationships with rescue partners, staff, volunteers, and community members effectively.
  • Competency in operating computers and commonly used software programs.
  • Detail-oriented, capable of maintaining accurate records and adhering to established protocols.
  • Strong organizational skills, with the ability to prioritize tasks and manage time effectively.
  • Ability to handle challenging situations with compassion, professionalism, and diplomacy.
  • Demonstrated ability to work both independently and collaboratively in a team environment.
  • Adaptable and resilient, capable of handling various environmental conditions within a shelter setting.
  • Valid driver’s license and clean driving record preferred.
  • Willingness to work a flexible schedule, including evenings, weekends, and holidays as needed.
  • Commitment to upholding the organization’s policies, procedures, and values with integrity.


Why Join CAC?

At CAC, you’ll be part of more than just a workplace. You’ll join a team of people doing meaningful work together.

We offer:

  • The opportunity to make a real difference every day
  • A mission-driven, supportive team culture
  • Growth and development opportunities
  • Competitive benefits package
  • A workplace where your work directly impacts animals and the community

Compensation & Benefits

  • Pay: Minimum pay of $22.20 after successful 90 day training period. $19.43 during training period.
  • Retirement plan with employer match
  • Health, Dental, and Vision Insurance
  • Paid Time Off
  • Professional Development Assistance
  • Life Insurance


Working Conditions / Physical Requirements

  • While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to sit, stand, walk, talk and hear. The employee is occasionally required to use hands to finger, handle, or operate objects, controls, or tools listed above; reach with hands and arms; climb or balance; stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl; and taste or smell.
  • The employee must occasionally lift and/or move more than 50 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, and the ability to adjust focus.
  • While performing the duties of this job, the employee frequently works in outside weather conditions. The employee occasionally works near moving mechanical parts; in high, precarious places; and is occasionally exposed to wet and/or humid conditions.
  • The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate to high.
  • Exposure and handling unvetted animals and their waste is frequent.

title: BALTIMORE AREA 56 HRS A WEEK
description:
ITLE OF POSITION: CERTIFIED NURSING ASSISTANT (CNA)/HOME HEALTH AIDE (HHA)


TITLE OF IMMEDIATE SUPERVISOR: Registered Nurse/Nursing Supervisor


RISK OF EXPOSURE TO BLOODBORNE PATHOGENS – HIGH




DUTIES


  1. Provides personal care and related services in the home, which is consistent with State regulations, delegated and supervised by a registered nurse or licensed practical nurse.
  2. Tasks to be performed by a CNA/HHA must be assigned by and performed under the supervision of an RN who will be responsible for client services provided by the CNA/HHA.
  3. Under no circumstances may a CNA/HHA be assigned to receive or reduce any intravenous procedures, or any other sterile or invasive procedures, other than rectal temperatures or enemas.


RESPONSIBILITIES


  1. Follows the plan of care to provide, safe, competent service to the client.
  2. Helps the client to maintain good personal hygiene and assists in maintaining a healthful, safe environment.
  3. Plans and prepares nutritious meals, markets when instructed to do so by the nurse.
  4. Assists the client with ambulation as ordered by the physician and approved and supervised by the nurse.
  5. Assists the therapy personnel as needed with rehabilitative processes.
  6. Encourages the client to become as independent as possible according to the nursing service plan.
  7. Attempts to promote client's mental alertness through involvement in activities of interest.
  8. Gives simple emotional and psychological support to the client and other members of the household and establishes a relationship with client and family which transmit trust and confidentiality.
  9. Reports any change in the client's mental or physical condition or in the home situation to the staff nurse, or to the Aide supervisor.
  10. Performs routine housekeeping tasks as related to a safe and comfortable environment for the client, as instructed by the professional nurse.
  11. Prepares a visit report promptly and incorporates same in the clinical record weekly.
  12. Confirms on a weekly basis, the scheduling of visits so that other necessary visits by staff members can be coordinated.
  13. Works with personnel of other community agencies involved in the client's service as directed by the nurse.
  14. Attends in-service as required by regulation and agency policy.
  15. Notifies the Agency of absences due to illness, emergency leave, normal vacation periods, or special professional meetings which will affect agreed service with the agency.


JOB CONDITIONS


  1. The ability to drive and the ability to access clients’ homes which may not be routinely wheelchair accessible are required.
  2. Hearing, eyesight and physical dexterity must be sufficient to perform a physical assessment of the client's condition and to perform client care.
  3. On occasion, may be required to bend, stoop, reach and move client weight up to 250 pounds; lift and/or carry up to 30 pounds.
  4. Must be able to communicate clearly, both verbally and in writing, in English


EQUIPMENT OPERATION


Use of BP cuff, thermometer and stethoscope Hand washing materials


COMPANY INFORMATION


Has access to all client medical records which may be discussed with the Registered Nurse and the Nursing Supervisor.


QUALIFICATIONS


1. Preferably a high school diploma or equivalent.


2. Must have successfully completed a nurse aide training and competency evaluation program:


  • Is certified by the Maryland Board of Nursing as a certified nursing assistant


  • Ambulation and transfer of clients, including positioning
  • Assistance with bathing, toileting, grooming, shaving, dental care, dressing and eating
  • Basic first aid and CPR
  • Caring for clients with special conditions and needs that are in the scope
  • Home management
  • Home safety and sanitation
  • Infection control in the home
  • Medically related activities to include the taking of vital signs
  • Proper nutrition




3. Must be free from health problems that may be injurious to client, self and co-workers and must present appropriate evidence to substantiate this.


4. Must comprehend the basics of personal care, housekeeping and meal preparation.


5. Must understand and respect clients including ethics and confidentiality.


6. Must have cleared background screening.




7. Must have current CPR certification

title: Senior Data Analyst and Reporting Developer
description:

title: Operator Technician Level 1
description:
Job Title: Operator Technician Level 1

Reports To:Textile and Technology Lead

Location: Morganton, NC Onsite

Job Type: Full-Time Hourly Non-Exempt, M-F 7am-3pm


About Material Return: Material Return is building a circular textile economy by transforming textile waste into high-quality recycled yarns. Based in Morganton, NC, we are creating innovative manufacturing solutions that reduce waste, strengthen domestic supply chains, and advance sustainable textile production in the United States. Material Return is an equal opportunity employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws.


Job Overview:

The Operator Technician is responsible for carrying out the preparation of raw fibers and materials for the full cycle of yarn production, while ensuring quality and consistency throughout each stage of the process. This role requires the technician to operate and monitor all machines, ensure that materials are handled properly, and procedures are carried out accurately to achieve precise results. The Operator/Technician will have a strong understanding of fibers and the disciplines surrounding yarn production, which will serve as the foundation for production-based teamwork, ability to collaborate and improve processes, all while maintaining high standards.


Essential Functions

  • Operate, set up, and maintain opening room and spinning equipment to support safe, efficient, and high-quality production.
  • Prepare equipment and materials for production runs and perform equipment cleanouts between orders in accordance with established procedures.
  • Monitor raw material supplies, track material movement between production areas, and communicate inventory needs or shortages to management.
  • Meet established production targets while maintaining product quality and following applicable safety procedures.
  • Support opening room, spinning, and warehouse operations based on production demands and operational priorities.
  • Produce bales and assist with material handling, shipping, and receiving activities in coordination with warehouse personnel.
  • Follow established standard operating procedures and maintain clean, organized, and safe production and warehouse work areas.
  • Identify and report equipment issues, material shortages, quality concerns, and other production obstacles to the appropriate team lead or manager.
  • Proactively prepare equipment, stage materials, and organize work areas to support efficient production and workflow.
  • Perform other related duties as assigned by the team lead or manager to support production and warehouse operations.


Preferred Knowledge, Skills, and Experience

  • One (1) or more years of manufacturing experience preferred, including experience in production or warehouse environments.
  • Experience operating production machinery and warehouse equipment preferred.
  • Knowledge of common fiber types, textile materials, and their impact on equipment performance and product quality preferred.
  • Familiarity with textile manufacturing equipment, including opening room, carding, drawing, and spinning machinery, or demonstrated ability to learn and operate specialized equipment.
  • Ability to identify equipment issues, perform routine equipment maintenance and cleaning, and communicate technical problems to the appropriate team lead or manager.
  • Ability to maintain clean, organized, and safe work areas in accordance with established procedures and applicable workplace safety requirements.
  • Ability to accurately maintain production records, track materials, document daily activities, and follow established standard operating procedures (SOPs).
  • Familiarity with inventory tracking methods, spreadsheets, or inventory management software preferred.
  • Ability to identify opportunities to improve workflow, reduce material waste, and increase efficiency while maintaining quality and safety standards.
  • Demonstrated adaptability, initiative, attention to detail, and willingness to learn new equipment, processes, and production systems.
  • Ability to work collaboratively across production and warehouse operations while adapting to changing operational priorities.


Physical Demands and Work Environment:

  • Ability to remain stationary for extended periods.
  • Ability to move throughout the office, meeting, warehouse, and work environments to access equipment, materials, and communicate with others.
  • Ability to occasionally lift and move materials weighing up to 40 pounds.
  • Ability to travel locally and regionally as needed to support business operations.
  • Ability to perceive, process, and communicate information presented in written, verbal, and electronic formats in English.
  • Ability to operate or work safely around powered industrial equipment and moving machinery, when required by the position.
  • Able to wear a required NIOSH-approved respirator. The selected candidate must complete the employer's required medical clearance process, including pulmonary function testing, before beginning work
  • Work is performed in both office and warehouse/manufacturing environments.
  • Regular exposure to warehouse conditions, including varying temperatures, elevated noise levels, moving equipment, dust, and airborne cotton fibers.


Pay and Benefits

  • Wage: Competitive, with an anticipated hourly range of $18-$22 based on experience.
  • Benefits: Health, dental, and vision insurance, paid time off, and holidays.

title: CNC Mill and Lathe Setup/Programmer
description:
Job Summary: As a CNC Setup/Programmer, you will play a crucial role in manufacturing processes by creating, optimizing, and maintaining the CNC (Computer Numerical Control) programs used to control precision machinery and equipment. Your expertise will be vital in translating engineering designs and specifications into machine instructions that result in accurate and high-quality machined parts. This role requires a strong understanding of machine principles, programming languages, and the ability to work collaboratively with engineers, machinists, and production teams.



Responsibilities

Program Development:

  • Interpret engineering drawings, models, and specifications to develop CNC programs that guide the machine in producing parts to required dimensions and tolerances utilizing 3- Axis Mill’s and 9-Axis Lathe’s. Swiss Screw Machine experience programing and/or Tombstone milling a plus.
  • Utilize CAD/CAM software to generate tool paths, define machining processes, select appropriate cutting tools, speeds & feeds and establish machining sequences. SOLIDWORKS SolidCAD/SolidCAM experiences a plus.

Programming and Optimization:

  • Write, edit, and optimize CNC programs to achieve efficient machining processes, minimize cycle times, and reduce waste e.g. path logic.
  • Ensure proper tool and material selection for each job to achieve desired surface finish and dimensional accuracy.
  • Edit: At machine center editing/data entry.

Setup and Testing:

  • Collaborate with machinists and production teams to set up CNC machines and load programs onto the machines.
  • Run simulations and perform test runs to verify the accuracy of the CNC programs before full production.
  • Setup through First Article inspection to include Work Center Setup Sheet and First Article Data Sheet documentation.

Troubleshooting:

  • Identify and resolve programming, tooling, or machining issues that arise during production.
  • Modify existing programs to rectify errors, improve efficiency, and/or implement design changes.

Documentation:

  • Maintain accurate and organized records of CNC programs, tool selections, machining parameters, and any adjustments made for future reference.
  • Quarterly backup of all work center programs; destination: Network Engineering item folder.

Continuous Improvement:

  • Stay updated on industry trends, machining technologies, and software advancements to suggest and implement process improvements.
  • Collaborate with engineering teams to provide input during the design phase to optimize manufacturability.
  • Assist management with the training of all Level I, II, III, and IIII Machinist/Operators.

Quality Control:

  • Conduct regular quality checks on machined parts to ensure they meet specified standards and make necessary adjustments to programs if deviations are detected.
  • Assist management with the training of all Level I, II, III, and IIII Machinist/Operators.

Safety and Compliance:

  • Adhere to safety protocols and standards while working with CNC machines and equipment.
  • Ensure compliance with company policies and regulations related to machining operations.
  • Assist management with the training of all Level I, II, III, and IIII Machinist/Operators.

Qualifications and Skills:

  • 4 years minimum work experience.
  • Proficiency in CAD/CAM software for generating tool paths (e.g., SolidWorks, CAM Works, etc.).
  • Strong understanding of machining principles, cutting tools, feeds and speeds, and material properties.
  • Knowledge of programming languages used in CNC machining (G-code, M-code, etc.).
  • Problem-solving skills to diagnose and troubleshoot machining issues while at the machine editing the program.
  • Attention to detail and precision to ensure accurate production of parts.
  • Effective communication skills to collaborate with cross-functional teams.
  • Ability to adapt to changing priorities and manage multiple projects simultaneously.
  • ISO 9001 and/or AS 9100 familiarity a plus.

Job Type:

Full-time 40 per week.

Benefits:

  • 401(k)
  • Dental insurance
  • Health insurance
  • Life insurance
  • Paid time off
  • Vision insurance

Work Location: In person

title: Director of Global Missions
description:
ABOUT OUR CHURCH

Christ Community exists to make gospel-centered disciples among all people for the glory of God.


The Gospel Above all

More than anything else, Christ Community is a church that is about the gospel. Jesus tells his disciples and those who would follow, “All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me. Go therefore and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, teaching them to observe everything I have commanded you. And remember, I am with you always, to the end of the age.” -Matthew 28:18-20


We believe Jesus radically changes a person’s life. We are to remind ourselves daily that we have been set free from the power of sin and condemnation and to live in light of this freedom. We do not work for our salvation, but our salvation has been given to us freely by God himself through faith in Christ.


Community & Culture

Located in the fast-growing Lake Norman region of North Carolina, Huntersville is a suburban community which offers an exceptional quality of life and an intentional small-town atmosphere. The area is home to Davidson College, Lowe's Corporate, and Trump National Golf Club.


Sharing a border with Charlotte, one of the nation’s top financial centers, Huntersville attracts many relocating families seeking a variety of quality educational opportunities for their children, as well as older families who want the conveniences of a major metro area in a more suburban setting.


The region is perfect for sports fans, and beaches and mountains are only a short drive away. Charlotte Douglas International Airport is a major hub for air travel, and local universities and seminaries offer opportunities for continuing adult education.


Christ Community, a member of the Southern Baptist Convention, is a Great Commission church focused on evangelism, missions, and discipleship. The church has over 1,100 active members and averages over 1,700 people on Sundays. The church's annual ministry budget is over $5 million, with nearly 20% designated to local and international missions. The church is debt-free and is poised for exceptional growth and multiplication.


JOB DESCRIPTION

Purpose and Primary Responsibilities: The Director of Global Missions provides strategic leadership for all local, domestic, and international missions and church planting efforts at Christ Community Church. This role champions the church’s mission beyond its walls by stewarding strategy, partnerships, and leadership development in alignment with the overall vision and direction of the church


Essential Responsibilities:

Strategy & Execution

  • Translate the church’s vision for missions and multiplication into clear strategies, priorities, and actionable plans, in close collaboration with and under the leadership of the Lead Pastor.
  • Establish goals, success metrics, and evaluation processes for missions and multiplication efforts to ensure faithfulness, fruitfulness, and alignment with church priorities.

Church Planting & Multiplication

  • Champion church planting and revitalization efforts, providing strategic oversight of the church multiplication pipeline by identifying, evaluating, and launching new congregations.
  • Cultivate and maintain relationships with church planting networks and partner organizations.
  • Represent Christ Community in church planting and multiplication conversations, partnerships, and networks as needed.

Global Missions & Sending Strategy

  • Oversee the missionary pipeline, including identification, assessment, preparation, sending, support, and long-term care.
  • Maintain and manage high-level partnerships with sending agencies and global ministries, including the International Mission Board, North American Mission Board, and other trusted partners.
  • Provide leadership in cultivating a culture of sending at Christ Community Church, with a particular emphasis on mobilizing members for short- and mid-term mission opportunities.
  • Ensure systems and leadership structures are in place to mobilize, prepare, and support mission teams and missionaries effectively.
  • Travel as appropriate to support missionaries, global partnerships, and mission initiatives.

Leadership & Oversight

  • Provide leadership, coaching, and evaluation for missions staff, ensuring clarity of roles, healthy rhythms, and alignment with strategy.
  • Collaborate with the senior leadership to integrate missions and multiplication into the broader life of the church.
  • Carry out other responsibilities as assigned.

Essential Attributes

  • Must model a deep commitment to Jesus.
  • Must be committed to the mission, vision, and values of Christ Community Church.
  • Must maintain membership at Christ Community Church.
  • Must be highly organized with attention to detail.
  • Must possess an attitude of service with a drive to accomplish our mission.
  • Must agree with the Baptist Faith and Message 2000.

Details

  • Seeking full-time, exempt position.
  • Salary & benefits commensurate with experience.


Equal Employment Opportunity:

Christ Community Church is committed to providing equal employment opportunities in accordance with applicable federal and state law.

description:
