title: Field Services Clerk
description:
Field Services Clerk

Job Type: Full-time

Base Pay: $17.55 during training period; $20.06 after successful 90 day period

Work Location: On site

Work Schedule: Friday-Tuesday 9am-6pm

Reports to Chief Dog Warden


Join the Team at Cincinnati Animal CARE

At Cincinnati Animal CARE (CAC), we do work that matters.

Every day, our team protects animals, supports our community, and helps save thousands of lives each year through compassionate care, advocacy, and education.

This work is meaningful, fast-paced, and can be challenging, but for the right person, it’s incredibly rewarding.

We are a team built for impact, made up of people who care deeply, work hard, support one another, and show up every day committed to making a difference.

If you are passionate about animals, thrive in a mission-driven environment, and want your work to have purpose, we’d love to have you join us.

About the Role

We are looking for a Field Services Clerk to join our team and play an important role in supporting CAC’s mission.

In this position, you will:

  • Provide high-level clerical records and support the field services team
  • Ensure field operations are legally compliant, well documented, and efficiently supported

This is a great opportunity for a results-driven, customer-focused professional who thrives in a fast-paced, public-facing environment. The ideal candidate demonstrates exceptional organizational skill, sound judgment, and a continuous improvement mindset. They maintain professionalism and empathy while interacting with diverse community members and supporting staff who operate in complex and sometimes high-risk environments involving people and animals.


What You’ll Be Responsible For

Your day-to-day may include:

Administrative & Records Management

  • Serve as the Division’s Public Records Clerk, managing and fulfilling public records requests in compliance with Ohio public records law.
  • Organize, maintain, and audit physical and electronic case files related to investigations, bites, dangerous dog designations, seizures, quarantines, citations, and court actions.
  • Prepare, enter, and maintain accurate data in applicable case management, records, and reporting systems.
  • Prepare correspondence, notices, citations, support documents, affidavits, and standard letters (e.g., dog-at-large notifications, compliance notices, court-related communications).
  • Ensure records meet evidentiary, legal, and retention standards necessary to support enforcement actions by DDWs, and APOs.

Court & Legal Coordination

  • Track cases from intake through resolution to ensure deadlines, court dates, hearings, releases, bonds, restitution, and compliance requirements are met.
  • Coordinate with County judicial districts regarding court schedules, appearances, subpoenas, and required documentation.
  • Monitor bond payments, care costs, restitution orders, and disposition outcomes; ensure accurate documentation and follow-up.
  • Prepare and distribute required daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly, and annual reports related to enforcement activity and outcomes.

Operational & Officer Support

  • Support field staff by communicating officer schedules, training schedules, court appearances, and operational updates.
  • Prepare and distribute End-of-Day reports and other operational summaries.
  • Represent the Field Services Division during daily huddles and internal coordination meetings.
  • Assist with onboarding of new field staff by coordinating documentation, training enrollment, uniforms, equipment, and administrative setup.
  • Enroll officers in required and elective training as directed; track certifications, training hours, and associated documentation.

Fleet, Inventory & Resource Management

  • Track and coordinate fleet maintenance, inspections, repairs, and compliance documentation.
  • Inventory uniforms, equipment, supplies, and field resources; coordinate ordering and replenishment.
  • Assist with tracking equipment assignments and returns for FROs, DDWs, and HAs.

Communication & Customer Service

  • Answer phones and respond to emails professionally and accurately, providing information or routing inquiries appropriately.
  • Serve as a point of contact for community members, partner agencies, courts, and internal staff regarding records, cases, and procedures.
  • Maintain a calm, supportive, and professional demeanor during high-stress or emotionally charged interactions.

Program & Continuous Improvement Support

  • Support short-term and long-term departmental goals by providing data, insights, and administrative support to the Chief Dog Warden.
  • Assist with program development initiatives, process improvements, and documentation updates.
  • Identify inefficiencies, risks, or gaps in administrative processes and proactively recommend solutions.

Other Duties

  • Perform other clerical, administrative, and operational support tasks as assigned.
  • Operate standard office equipment including computers, phones, copiers, and related technology.
  • Drive division vehicles as needed to transport supplies, documents, or equipment.
  • Assist with the cleaning and maintenance of the dog warden office and vehicles.
  • Supporting additional organizational needs as they arise


What Makes Someone Successful in This Role

We’re looking for someone who:

  • Is passionate about CAC’s mission and animal welfare
  • Brings a positive, team-first attitude
  • Communicates openly and professionally
  • Takes ownership and solves problems proactively
  • Thrives in a fast-paced, ever-changing environment
  • Can balance compassion with accountability
  • Is dependable, adaptable, and eager to learn

Qualifications

Preferred/Required:

  • Minimum of 3 years of clerical or administrative experience in a fast-paced or regulated environment.
  • Minimum of 5 years of customer service experience
  • At least 1 year of project coordination, program support, or similar experience, preferred.
  • Working knowledge of, or ability to quickly learn, county and state ordinances, including Ohio Revised Code Chapters 955 and 959.
  • Demonstrated ability to anticipate issues, identify risks, and proactively solve problems with incomplete or evolving information.
  • Strong critical thinking skills with the ability to manage competing priorities and meet deadlines.
  • Highly effective written and verbal communication skills across all levels of an organization and with external partners.
  • Proven ability to collaborate cross-functionally and support enforcement and operations teams.
  • Experience working in a start-up, high-growth, or rapidly evolving organization is strongly preferred.
  • Valid driver’s license with the ability to safely operate division vehicles.

Core Competencies

  • Attention to detail and accuracy
  • Legal and regulatory awareness
  • Confidentiality and ethical judgment
  • Customer service excellence
  • Organization and time management
  • Adaptability and resilience
  • Continuous improvement mindset


Why Join CAC?

At CAC, you’ll be part of more than just a workplace. You’ll join a team of people doing meaningful work together.

We offer:

  • The opportunity to make a real difference every day
  • A mission-driven, supportive team culture
  • Growth and development opportunities
  • Competitive benefits package
  • A workplace where your work directly impacts animals and the community

Compensation & Benefits

  • Pay: From $19.74/hour after 90 day training period
  • Retirement plan with employer match
  • Health, Dental, and Vision Insurance
  • Paid Time Off
  • Professional Development Assistance
  • Life Insurance

Working Conditions / Physical Requirements

  • While performing the duties of this position, the employee is frequently required to sit, stand, walk, talk, and hear. The employee may occasionally be required to use hands to handle or operate office equipment; reach; climb; balance; stoop; kneel; crouch; or crawl.
  • Ability to occasionally lift and/or move items exceeding 50 pounds.
  • Specific vision abilities include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, and the ability to adjust focus.
  • Noise levels are typically moderate to high.
  • Frequent exposure to unvetted animals and animal waste.
  • Potential exposure to aggressive or sick animals.
  • Potential exposure to zoonotic diseases and parasites.
  • The work environment may include extreme heat or cold.
  • May require evening, weekend, holiday, and on-call availability based on operational needs.
  • Rotating shifts may be required.
  • 8- or 10-hour shifts depending on scheduling needs.

title: Senior Client Service Associate
description:
Summary

This full-time, hourly position is based in Framingham, Massachusetts and plays a critical role in delivering exceptional client experience for Bartholomew Private Wealth (BPW) clients and advisor teams. Bartholomew & Company is a financial services firm headquartered in Worcester, MA managing approximately $6 billion in assets across two divisions: Governments and Institutions, which serves public entities and institutional clients, and Private Wealth, which serves individuals, families, and business owners. This role sits within BPW, which manages approximately $2.5 billion for clients across the country using a disciplined, client-centered approach tailored to each client's goals and risk tolerance. The Senior Client Service Associate (Sr. CSA) oversees complex client service workflows, serves as a senior operational resource to advisors, and helps ensure consistent, high-quality service standards across the firm. The Sr. CSA acts as a trusted point of contact for clients, proactively addressing service needs, resolving complex issues, and supporting the operational execution of client relationships, while also mentoring junior service associates and contributing to process improvement initiatives that enhance operational efficiency and client satisfaction.




About Us

At Bartholomew Private Wealth (BPW), prudent management is our core tenet because we take our clients’ dreams for a sound financial life as seriously as they do. BPW manages approximately $2.5 billion in assets for private clients, families, and business owners across the country. We practice risk-sensitive portfolio management, aiming to maximize gains in accordance with each client’s personal tolerance for risk. Our deep expertise in institutional asset management provides clients with access to opportunities, sophistication, and diversification not typically available to individual investors.



Core Responsibilities

Required Skills and Qualifications

  • Demonstrated ability to process high-complexity transactions accurately.
  • Experience with operational workflow optimization.
  • Ability to promote service excellence and operational discipline; mentors and coaches junior service team members, as applicable.

Preferred Skills and Qualifications

Core Skills, Competencies & Characteristics

Be Curious: Demonstrates genuine enthusiasm for financial markets, planning concepts, and the wealth management profession through inquisitiveness, and is receptive to feedback and actively applies mentorship to develop technical expertise and understanding of the advisory process.

title: Stock Replenisher
description:
POSITION PROFILE


To ensure an uninterrupted supply of goods for the order fulfillment process by proactively transferring inventory from bulk storage (reserve) to active picking areas (pick faces). The Stock Replenisher monitors inventory levels on the warehouse floor, safely operates material handling equipment, and accurately updates system records to maintain optimal stock availability and prevent order processing delays.


JOB DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES


· Continuously monitor active pick bins and forward pick locations to identify low stock levels and

anticipate replenishment needs before stock-outs occur.

· Safely locate, retrieve, and transport bulk inventory from high-racking reserve storage to

designated active picking zones.

· Strictly adhere to First-In, First-Out (FIFO) or First-Expired, First-Out (FEFO) inventory rotation

principles, particularly for perishable or pharmaceutical goods, ensuring older stock is placed at

the front of the pick face.

· Accurately record all stock movements and internal transfers in real-time using RF scanners and

the Warehouse Management System (WMS) to ensure 100% system-to-physical accuracy.

· Break down bulk pallets, remove shrink wrap, and neatly organize individual cases or units into

the active pick bins.

· Identify, document, and report any damaged, defective, or expired goods encountered during

the replenishment process, transferring them to the secured quarantine area.

· Promptly clear empty pallets, cardboard, shrink wrap, and debris from the warehouse aisles to

maintain a clean and safe working environment.

· Assist the Inventory Team with periodic cycle counts and general physical stock audits to ensure

bin accuracy.

· Communicate with Pickers and Warehouse Supervisors to resolve immediate stock shortages or

bin discrepancies.

· Perform any other related warehouse duties that may be assigned.


PERFORMANCE STANDARDS

· Zero fulfillment delays caused by stock-outs in active picking locations when inventory is available in

reserve.

· 100% accuracy in updating the WMS during internal stock transfers.

· Strict compliance with FIFO/FEFO rotation standards to prevent product expiry on the shelves.

· Maintenance of clean, safe, and unobstructed aisles during and after replenishment tasks.


QUALIFICATIONS (EDUCATION, EXPERIENCE & CERTIFICATIONS)


· A minimum of three to five (3-5) CXCs, including Mathematics and English.

· At least one to two (1-2) years of working experience in a fast-paced warehouse, logistics, or

distribution environment.

· Valid certification to operate Material Handling Equipment (MHE) such as Reach Trucks, Forklifts, or

Electric Pallet Jacks is a distinct asset.

· Familiarity with RF scanners and Warehouse Management Systems (WMS)

title: Project Controls Manager
description:
We are seeking an exceptionally qualified Project Controls Manager to lead the Project Controls function at the consortium level for a landmark SAR ~7 Billion Metro infrastructure project.

Reporting directly to Project Leadership, the successful candidate will be responsible for providing strategic oversight, rigorous governance, and end-to-end management of planning, scheduling, delay analysis, commercial exposure, and cost control across a complex multi-partner Joint Venture / Consortium environment.


Key Responsibilities

  • Consortium-Level Leadership: Drive and manage the overall Project Controls strategy across all consortium partners, ensuring full alignment on schedules, reporting metrics, risk mitigation, and project milestones.
  • Master Planning & Scheduling: Direct baseline management, progress monitoring, earned value management (EVM), critical path analysis, and accurate schedule forecasting using Primavera P6. Oversee recovery and acceleration plans when required.
  • Time Claims & Claims Management: Lead forensic delay analysis, Extension of Time (EOT) submissions, disruption claims, and Time Impact Analysis (TIA) to protect the consortium’s contractual and commercial interests.
  • Cost & Commercial Governance: Provide high-level oversight of project budgeting, cash flow, forecasting, variations, commercial claims, and overall contractual risk exposure.
  • Risk Management: Oversee schedule and cost quantitative risk assessments, identifying key risk drivers and establishing proactive mitigation strategies.
  • Executive & Stakeholder Reporting: Direct senior-level dashboard reporting, KPI tracking, and effective coordination with Consortium Board Members, the Client, Project Management Consultants (PMC), and external stakeholders.


Key Requirements & Qualifications

  • Metro / Rail Experience (Mandatory): Direct, proven experience holding a leadership Project Controls role on major Metro or Railway EPC megaprojects.
  • Overall Experience: Minimum of 15 years of progressive, hands-on Project Controls experience on large-scale infrastructure and EPC projects.
  • Consortium / JV Leadership: Proven track record leading multidisciplinary Project Controls teams within complex Joint Venture or Consortium arrangements.
  • Forensic Delay Analysis: Deep expertise in EOT claims, disruption analysis, and contractual schedule dispute resolution.
  • Technical Mastery: Master-level knowledge of Primavera P6, delay analysis methodologies, and integrated cost/schedule control systems.
  • Stakeholder Management: Exceptional communication, negotiation, and executive presence required to manage interactions with high-level Client and Partner representatives.
  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering, Construction Management, or a related discipline. Advanced certifications (e.g., PMP, CCP, PSP, RICS) are a strong plus.

Skills

Technical & Domain Expertise

  • Metro & Rail Engineering/EPC: Expert understanding of civil, trackwork, systems, and MEP interfaces in heavy rail/metro environments.
  • Planning & Scheduling: Baseline development, Critical Path Method (CPM), Earned Value Management (EVM), S-curve analysis, and progress S-curves.
  • Forensic Delay Analysis: Extension of Time (EOT) claims, Time Impact Analysis (TIA), Windows Analysis, disruption and productivity loss calculations.
  • Cost & Commercial Control: Budgeting, cost forecasting, cash flow modeling, variation order management, and contractual exposure evaluation.
  • Risk Management: Quantitative Schedule & Cost Risk Analysis (QSRA/QCRA), risk register management, and mitigation planning.


Software & Tools

  • Primavera P6: Advanced / Master user level.
  • Delay Analysis & Risk Software: Primavera Risk Analysis (Pertmaster), Deltek Acumen Fuse, or similar.
  • Cost & Reporting Tools: PRISM, SAP, MS Excel (Advanced modeling), and Power BI / Tableau dashboards.


Leadership & Soft Skills

  • Consortium & JV Governance: Ability to align competing priorities, manage multi-cultural team dynamics, and maintain unified standards across partner firms.
  • Executive Stakeholder Communication: High-level presentation skills for direct reporting to Consortium Board, Client, and PMC leadership.
  • Negotiation & Claims Defense: Contractual acumen to support dispute resolution and commercial negotiations.

title: Lead Ground Systems Engineer (ESS-SR)
description:
Overview

Stellar Solutions, a nationally recognized “Great Place To Work”, has exciting opportunities providing Engineering solutions for innovative new-entrant space companies, as well as established space systems manufacturers, commercial space system operators and service providers, and other industry stakeholders including investors.

At Stellar Solutions, we offer talented, energetic, and immediately productive resources to satisfy our customers’ critical needs in systems engineering and integration, mission operations, program management and strategic planning. Role/Responsibilities/Qualifications

The successful candidate will:

  • Lead and oversee technical efforts of four systems engineers providing enterprise-wide, high-impact systems engineering services for SIGINT, GEOINT, and Operations Center ground systems
  • Develop technical requirements for SIGINT and GEOINT ground processing system updates, monitor and supervise scheduling of system deliveries, system testing and documentation of discrepancies
  • Anticipate, assign, drive projects and customer requirements to closure; continually assess team’s tasks, realign/reprioritize/augment assignments as appropriate
  • Work with government managers program leadership to organize and plan ground team support; maintain awareness of government’s evolving needs and proactively provide analysis, insights, recommendations to improve delivery of services and/or exploit opportunity to enhance process or resource effectiveness or efficiency
  • Provide technical support to government points of contacts; identify and communicate status, risks, issues, opportunities, assumptions, mitigations, and dependencies for ground system activities
  • Promote and facilitate collaboration with government, SETA team members, and other contractors supporting the government – across the enterprise
  • Develop assessments and staffing products for a variety of audiences, convey information in a clear and articulate manner to Government leadership

QUALIFICATIONS

Required:

  • US Citizenship
  • Active TS/SCI clearance with polygraph
  • Bachelor’s degree in science, technology, engineering, or mathematics (STEM) and 14 years or more experience; Master’s in STEM field and 12 years or more experience; PhD or JD in STEM and nine (9) years or more experience. *STEM is a contractual requirement
  • Demonstrated leadership success on variety of complex ground systems engineering projects impacting mission operations
  • In-depth experience with NRO systems engineering and mission readiness processes; familiar with readiness events, control gates, and associated entry/exit criteria; systems engineering governance
  • Knowledge of GEOINT and SIGINT overall space and ground architecture including mission management, mission control and mission processing functions
  • Program lifecycle experience from concept development and design to deployment, operations, and maintenance, decommission
  • CONOPS requirements development, interface control documentation, technical specification review, architecture development
  • Experience in systems development methodologies (e.g Agile, DevOps, Spiral, Waterfall, etc.) and cloud technologies
  • Self-starter, proactively addresses customer requirements with no supervision; expert at defining solutions for broad, abstract topics—drives tasks to closure
  • Polished communicator (written/verbal); impeccable interpersonal skills and personal judgment
  • Master at collaboration and coordination with multiple stakeholders -- consensus builder
  • Proficient with MS Office (Word, PowerPoint, Excel), MS Outlook, MS Project)

Desired:

  • Experience with Digital Engineering (DE)/Model Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) and associated tools.
  • Real-time operations experience as a spacecraft or ground systems operator
  • SAFe, Agile, INCOSE certifications
  • Proficient with MS Project

Compensation

The typical salary pay range for this position is USD $150,000 – $175,000. Individual pay is determined by many factors including work location, job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

In addition to base salary, this position is eligible for a comprehensive total rewards package that includes an annual performance bonus, an employer-funded Profit-Sharing Plan (PSP) contribution based on base compensation, and comprehensive employer-paid medical benefits, PTO pay-out options, along with additional company-sponsored benefits. All of these benefits represent an additional 30-40% to your base compensation for a total compensation package.

Deliverable(s)

Deliverables will be in the format of reports, briefings, spreadsheets, or other documents as directed by the Government. The nature of the work will, at times, require a quick response to stringent deadlines and always in a high quality, professional manner.

title: Senior AR Analyst, Credit Control

Senior AR Analyst, Credit Control | London

About Convene Hospitality Group

Convene Hospitality Group designs and operates experiential event venues, bringing premium meeting and event experiences to some of the world's leading organisations. Through a growing portfolio of brands including Convene, etc.venues and NeueHouse, we operate a network of nearly 40 venues and are the largest single provider of dedicated meeting and event spaces across the US and UK.

The UK is central to that story. From our Convene venues across the City of London to etc.venues in London and Manchester, and with our new West End destination, Convene Rathbone, our UK footprint continues to grow, and so does the pace of the events we deliver. Every conference, board meeting and live event our clients host relies on a finance team that keeps things moving behind the scenes.

About the Role

We are seeking an experienced Senior Accounts Receivable (AR) Analyst, Credit Control to join our UK Finance team and help lead AR operations across our UK venue portfolio. Reporting to the AR Manager, you'll take ownership of billing, credit control and cash allocation, turning client contracts and booking data into accurate, timely invoices, following up on outstanding balances, allocating customer receipts and keeping customer accounts clean and reconciled in our financial systems.

This is a role with real visibility. You'll work closely with Sales, Event Operations and client procurement teams, acting as a trusted partner who keeps cash flowing while protecting the strong client relationships our business is built on. For someone who brings both rigour and a commercial mindset, it's an opportunity to make a direct impact on the financial health of a growing UK business.

What You'll Do

Daily Operations & Cash Management:

  • Prepare multi-bank reconciliation spreadsheets (Santander, JPM, Online Credit Cards) and resolve unapplied cash exceptions
  • Process incoming payments (ACH, credit cards, wires, cheques) and apply them accurately to customer accounts in NetSuite
  • Issue final invoices for standard customer accounts and review/process credit memos and billing adjustments with proper approvals
  • Manage customer record updates in NetSuite

Credit Control & Collections:

  • Take direct ownership of chasing overdue accounts via calls, emails, and structured collection cycles
  • Review the AR Aging report weekly to track overdue accounts, identify delinquent trends, and prioritise high-value collection efforts
  • Escalate severely overdue or high-risk accounts to Finance/Sales Management and Legal/Collections where necessary
  • Assess and assign credit limits for new and existing accounts based on payment history and financial reviews

Experience Required

  • 5+ years of dedicated Accounts Receivable or Finance experience
  • Strong proficiency in NetSuite (or comparable ERPs) and intermediate to advanced Excel

  • Experience managing key enterprise client accounts, including submitting and tracking invoices via customer supplier portals (e.g. Coupa, SAP Ariba, Tungsten Network), purchase order-led invoicing and resolving rejected or queried invoices, is a strong advantage

  • Solid understanding of month-end AR reconciliations
  • Excellent problem-solving skills and cross-functional communication



We're Here For You:

At Convene Hospitality Group, we want you to feel supported in every part of your life. Here's what you can expect:

  • Health & Wellness: Private medical insurance, subsidised fitness and eye care, plus well-being and personal support programs. Because your well-being matters, inside and outside of work.
  • Time Off & Balance: 25 days annual leave, bank holidays, and company sick pay.
  • Financial Benefits: Bonus scheme, interest-free loans for rail travel or further education, and a Cycle to Work program. We invest in you so you can grow personally and professionally.
  • Growth & Recognition: Career development opportunities and programs to celebrate your achievements.
  • Community & Impact: Volunteer, donate, and make a real impact through your work.

At Convene Hospitality Group, we believe great teams are built by bringing together people with different backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences. title: Master Level Clinician
description:
AOC Outreach Services

Mental Health Associate



Mission Statement
AOC Outreach Services mission is to provide special needs children and
adults, and their families, the opportunity to succeed with our innovative and
effective programs. We strive to provide the best quality mental health services in
an effort for individuals to become self-empowering and develop strengths to live a
healthy and productive life.


Our Vision
AOC Outreach Services strives to provide life changing services to the
community of Texas. We will leave no stone unturned in the pursuit to extend the
pool of mental health resources while eradicating the negative stigma behind
mental health.


Role Purpose

The LPC-Associate will provide professional counseling and related behavioral health services under the supervision of an approved LPC Supervisor and in accordance with Texas law, the employee’s license and level of competence, applicable payer requirements, and AOC Outreach Services policies and procedures. The LPC-Associate will support clients in achieving their behavioral health goals through ethical, culturally responsive, and evidence-based counseling practices while maintaining accurate and timely clinical documentation.

The LPC-Associate is expected to practice within the scope of their provisional license and approved supervision arrangement and may not independently represent themselves as a fully licensed LPC when Texas law requires the LPC-Associate designation.



Responsibilities


  • Provide individual, family, and/or group counseling services within the scope permitted by the LPC-Associate license and approved supervision plan.
  • Complete clinical assessments, treatment planning, progress notes, and other required documentation in a timely and accurate manner.
  • Develop and maintain therapeutic relationships with clients while promoting a safe, respectful, and supportive environment.
  • Implement appropriate counseling interventions based on client needs, treatment goals, clinical training, and evidence-based practices.
  • Monitor client progress and communicate relevant changes, concerns, or barriers to treatment with the supervising LPC and appropriate members of the treatment team.
  • Participate in ongoing clinical supervision and incorporate supervisory feedback into clinical practice.
  • Maintain compliance with all applicable Texas laws, licensing board requirements, ethical standards, payer requirements, and AOC policies and procedures.
  • Maintain appropriate professional boundaries and protect client confidentiality in accordance with applicable laws and organizational policies.
  • Complete all required clinical, administrative, and compliance documentation within established timelines.
  • Participate in case consultations, staff meetings, trainings, and other professional development activities as required.
  • Coordinate with other service providers, caregivers, community resources, and members of the client’s support system when appropriate and authorized.
  • Identify and appropriately respond to client safety concerns, including following established procedures for crisis intervention, risk assessment, and mandatory reporting.
  • Maintain current licensure, supervision documentation, and other required professional credentials.
  • Perform other duties and responsibilities related to the position as assigned.


Qualifications


  • Current Texas LPC-Associate, LMSW, or LMFT license in good standing.
  • Active supervision relationship with a Texas Board-approved Supervisor, as required.
  • Knowledge of counseling principles, behavioral health practices, and ethical standards.
  • Ability to provide counseling services within the scope of training, competence, and licensure.
  • Strong communication, interpersonal, organization, and documentation skills.
  • Ability to establish and maintain professional therapeutic relationships with clients and families.
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality and exercise sound professional judgment.
  • Ability to work collaboratively with supervisors, clinical staff, clients, families, and community partners.
  • Commitment to ethical, culturally responsive, client-centered, and trauma-informed care.
  • Ability to meet AOC Outreach Services’ documentation, compliance, scheduling, and productivity requirements.
  • Must successfully complete all required onboarding, orientation, background checks, and organizational training.



Education


  • Master’s degree or higher in Counseling, Clinical Mental Health Counseling, Social Work, Psychology, or a closely related behavioral health field from an accredited institution.
  • Completion of educational and clinical requirements necessary to obtain and maintain Texas Associate licensure.
  • Additional training or continuing education related to behavioral health, trauma-informed care, crisis intervention, or specialized populations is preferred.

title: Stock Monitor
description:
POSITION PROFILE


To monitor, control, and maintain accurate inventory levels within the warehouse facility. The Stock Monitor ensures stock integrity, minimizes shrinkage, identifies discrepancies between physical counts and system records, and supports the efficient flow of goods in and out of the warehouse.


JOB DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES


Distribution Responsibilities


· Conduct daily, weekly, and monthly cycle counts of inventory across designated warehouse zones.

· Reconcile physical stock counts with the Warehouse Management System (WMS) or inventory

database.

· Replenish stock from the bulk storage areas to the designated active picking areas to ensure

continuous availability of products for order fulfillment.

· Investigate, document, and report any inventory discrepancies, missing items, or stock anomalies to

the Inventory Manager.

· Monitor stock levels of fast-moving items to prevent stockouts and alert the purchasing or

replenishment teams when minimum thresholds are reached.

· Identify, document, and separate damaged, defective, or expired goods, ensuring they are placed

in the secured quarantine area.

· Verify the accuracy of incoming shipments against purchase orders and outgoing loads against

dispatch tickets to ensure inventory accuracy is maintained.

· Ensure all goods are properly labeled, binned, and stored in their correct designated locations.

· Assist in the preparation and execution of full quarterly and annual physical stock counts.

· Monitor the warehouse floor to ensure that stock handling procedures are being followed by

warehouse staff to prevent damage or loss.

· Maintain accurate and organized records of all stock checks, adjustments, and reports.

· Any other related duties that may be assigned.


PERFORMANCE STANDARDS


The job is satisfactorily performed when the key results of the following strategic objectives of the

department are consistently achieved:

· When inventory accuracy metrics (e.g., 98%+ system-to-physical accuracy) are consistently maintained.

· Timely completion of scheduled cycle counts and discrepancy reports.

· Uninterrupted workflow for the picking team due to timely stock replenishment.

· Reduction in untraced inventory loss (shrinkage) within assigned zones.


QUALIFICATIONS (EDUCATION, EXPERIENCE & CERTIFICATIONS)


· A minimum five (5) CXCs including Math & English/ Diploma in Logistics, Inventory, Business

Administration or related field.

· At least two (2) years working experience in Logistics or Warehouse Environment

· Strong IT systems knowledge

· Experience in delivering results in a team environment

title: Salesforce Administrator
description:
🌍 Salesforce Administrator

📍 Onsite - Seville | Verto Education
🔗 Learn more about us:

🌍 About Verto

Verto is on a mission to provide the best possible start to college. We make travel and experiential education a core part of the first year, enabling students to begin their academic journey overseas before transferring to one of 70+ partner universities in the United States.


We are building a more accessible, more impactful model of higher education. We are a fast-growing, mission-driven organisation creating transformational global experiences.

✨ About the Role

We're hiring a Salesforce Administrator to own the day-to-day health of our org and help us build what comes next. You'll report to our Engineering Team Manager and work alongside our engineers, PMs, and the ops teams who live in Salesforce every day.

This isn't a ticket-closing job. We want someone who fixes the root cause, cleans up as they go, and tells us when a request is the wrong idea.


Location: Seville, Spain. Occasional travel between our European sites.


Hours: You'll need regular overlap with US working hours, particularly US Eastern. e.g. available until 19:00 CET at least four days a week, with occasional later calls for US Pacific developers.


🚀 What You’ll Be Doing

Responsibilities:

  • Build new features end-to-end with declarative tools. Take a feature request from the business, work out what's really needed, and deliver it with Flow, objects and fields, Lightning pages, Dynamic Forms and the rest of the platform's click-based toolset. Code is the last resort, not the first.
  • Own user management and access. Profiles kept minimal, permission sets and permission set groups doing the real work, sharing rules that make sense.
  • Build and maintain automation in Flow. Keep it documented, testable, and easy for the next person to read. Help us retire old automation that nobody understands anymore.
  • Configure objects, fields, page layouts, Lightning pages, validation rules and record types as the business changes.
  • Work in sandboxes and move changes through our release process. No building straight in production.
  • Keep data clean. Duplicate rules, imports and updates with Data Loader or similar, and fixing bad data at the source instead of patching reports.
  • Build reports and dashboards people actually use, and help teams answer their own questions.
  • Take part in security reviews: field-level security, audit trail, login and session settings, connected apps.
  • Read the release notes three times a year and tell us what matters, including the AI and Agentforce features worth trying and the ones that aren't ready.
  • Triage and resolve Salesforce requests from staff, and write down what you learned so it doesn't come back.
  • Partner with engineers on integrations and code-backed features, and with PMs on requirements before anything gets built.


🧠 What We’re Looking For

Must-have:

  • English at B2 level or higher (CEFR). Required. Our team and our students work in English, and you'll be writing requirements, documentation, and Slack messages every day. You don't need to be a native speaker. You do need to follow a fast technical conversation and explain a change clearly in writing.
  • Ability to work on-site in an office environment
  • Salesforce Certified Platform Administrator (formerly Salesforce Certified Administrator). Required and current.
  • 3+ years administering a live Salesforce org with real users and real data.
  • A track record of shipping new features with declarative tools, not just maintaining an org. Be ready to walk us through one you built from request to release.
  • Solid Flow experience: record-triggered, screen and scheduled flows, plus fault handling.
  • A security-first habit with permissions. You grant the least access that gets the job done.
  • Comfortable working remotely and asynchronously. You write things down, you ask when you're stuck, and you don't wait to be chased.
  • Good judgment about when to say no, or "not like that", to a request.


Nice-to-have:

  • Apex experience. Reading it well enough to debug a trigger or explain what a class does is a real plus. Writing and testing it is better. We don't expect you to be a developer, but knowing where config ends and code begins helps a lot.
  • Additional Salesforce certifications, for example:
  • Platform App Builder
  • Advanced Administrator
  • Platform Developer I
  • Sharing and Visibility Architect or Data Architect
  • Agentforce Specialist
  • Experience with source control and deployment tools: Git, Salesforce CLI, DevOps Center or a third-party tool like Gearset or Copado.
  • SOQL for troubleshooting and ad hoc data questions.
  • Experience with Experience Cloud or integrations with outside systems.
  • Background in education, higher ed or study abroad.


How we work:

Small team, a lot of trust. Work is tracked in Asana and talked about in Slack. We use AI tools every day and expect you to as well. We'd rather ship a small, well-scoped thing on time than a perfect thing late, and we follow a documented process so stakeholders always know what we need from them and when.

🌱 Why Join Verto?
The below are for full-time Employees, international staff benefits vary by location and meet or exceed local standards)

  • 🌍 Be part of a mission-driven organisation reimagining higher education
  • ✈️ Work in a globally-minded, international environment
  • 📚 Exposure to cross-functional teams (academics, operations, student life)
  • 🌴 22 working days paid vacation + Public Holidays
  • 🚀 Opportunity to grow in a fast-moving, impact-driven organisation

Even if you don’t meet 100% of the above qualifications, you should still seriously consider applying. Studies show that you can still be considered for a role if you meet just 50% of the role’s requirements.


💲Compensation
 At Verto, base salary is one part of your total compensation package.

Final base pay will depend on your location (aligned to Verto’s compensation regions), as well as your experience, skills, and relevant qualifications. Your recruiter/hiring manager can share the specific range for your location during the hiring process.

Seville -Onsite — Anticipated Base Salary Range
€30k–€45k Seville

⚖️ Right to Work

You must have the legal right to work in Spain. Verto Education is unable to sponsor visas for this role.

♿ Accessibility & Accommodations

Verto is committed to providing reasonable accommodations to candidates with disabilities. If you require support during the recruitment process, please let us know.

🔐 Data Privacy

By applying for this role, you acknowledge that Verto Education will process your personal data for recruitment purposes. This includes assessing your application, communicating with you, and managing the hiring process. Your data will be handled in accordance with applicable data protection laws, including the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) where applicable.

description:
QMHP-CS Headquarters


AOC Outreach Services is a community-based child mental health care agency serving children between 3-17 years-old. Our Agency is seeking to award contracts to community partners in the Houston area, who want to become self-employed business-owners working in the mental health field.

The purpose of this position is to provide a range of services geared toward engaging, supporting, and coaching parents, children, and youth in child welfare. The goal is to develop rapport with the child/youth and aid in optimizing the child's functioning in the most efficient and effective manner possible. The Qualified Mental Health Professional (QMHP-CS) will provide goal directed interventions to stabilize children and youth in transition. We are seeking qualified QMHP-CS with a degree in the field and at least one year of experience in the field. Completion of Daily session notes with 24 hours after session.

QMHP-CS providers are eligible to deliver MHTCM and MH rehabilitation services and must meet the following minimum credentialing requirements:

  • Schedule & attend weekly client sessions.
  • Complete & submit session notes within 24 hours after session.
  • Achieve 80 % of client’s weekly hours target goal.
  • Attend continuing education meetings such as Community Partner Clinical Supervision meeting (virtual) by-weekly.
  • Participate continuing education meetings such as in person community partner meetings by-weekly.
  • Participate continuing education meetings such as Community Partner Coaching session (In-person & virtually) by-weekly
  • Completed a standardized training curriculum
  • Demonstrated competency in the work to be performed
  • Must have at least 3-5 years of experience in the field

QMHP-CS providers are eligible to deliver Mental Health Targeted Case Management and Mental Health rehabilitative services and must meet the following minimum credentialing requirements:

  • A bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university with a minimum number of hours that are equivalent to a major in psychology, social work, medicine, nursing, rehabilitation, counseling, sociology, human growth and development, physician assistant, gerontology, special education, educational
  • psychology, early childhood education, or early childhood intervention
  • A license as a registered nurse (RN) Staff administering the assessment instruments must have documentation of current certification in the Child and Adolescent Needs and Strengths Assessment (CANS) or the Adult Needs and Strengths Assessment (ANSA). Certification must be updated annually through an approved entity. An individual who possesses any of the following licenses is considered a Licensed Practitioner of the Healing Arts (LPHA) and is automatically certified as a QMHP-CS:
  • Physician
  • Physician Assistant * Advanced Practice Registered Nurse
  • Psychologist * Licensed Clinical Social Worker (LCSW)
  • Licensed Marriage and Family Therapist (LMFT)
  • Licensed Professional Counselor (LPC) A QMHP-CS must be clinically supervised by another QMHP-CS. If a QMHP-CS is clinically supervised by another QMHP-CS, the supervising QMHP-CS must be clinically supervised by an LPHA.
  • Completion of Daily session notes with 24 hours after session

title: Children's Education Facilitator
description:
About the role:

The Children’s Education Facilitator is responsible for developing and providing educational programming, academic support, and recreational activities that promote resilience, stability, and positive social and emotional development of NYWS’ children and youth clients, including through supporting their caregivers. This role will design age-appropriate educational and recreational programs in alignment with our principles of trauma- informed practice.


What you will be doing:

  • Foster and maintain a trauma-informed, respectful, and inclusive environment for Clients, colleagues, volunteers, and other members of the NYWS internal and external community while adhering to NYWS' policies and procedures.
  • Facilitate activities and programs for Client caregivers of children and youth to help increase capacity to respond to their children’s post-trauma needs through supporting attachment recovery and emotional regulation.
  • Support with facilitating age-appropriate activities and programs for NYWS’ children and youth Clients where required, to help promote positive social and emotional development e.g., building confidence and self-esteem, healthy relationships, self-regulation and coping, based on guidance and direction from the Manager, Programs and Services and project requirements.
  • Foster diversity, equity, and inclusion by considering diverse cultures, physical abilities, neurodiversity, and lived experiences of children and youth in the delivery of programs as well as in communication with children and youth and their caregivers.
  • Support with facilitating programming in age-appropriate ways using a blend of individual and group learning experiences to support a variety of learning styles, developmental milestones, and alignment with school curriculum.
  • Adapt facilitation and delivery to accommodate diverse needs, interests, and abilities of participants, ensuring engaging, inclusive, and enjoyable learning opportunities for all.
  • Support children’s positive social skill development by empowering their caregivers to model clear communication, and constructive conflict resolution.
  • Support caregivers to stimulate curiosity in their children to help support intellectual growth and foster a sense of achievement.
  • Provide to caregivers, children and youth, including group interactions that foster safety, trust, and well-being.
  • Provide individualized attention as needed to both adults and children, recognizing and responding to children’s and unique needs of participants.
  • Recognize and de-escalate challenging situations in a trauma-informed manner.
  • Notify the Programs and Services leadership of any supplies or equipment needed to support programming.
  • Prepare program spaces and materials before activities and ensure program areas are cleaned, organized, and restored following each shift.
  • Follow protocols for safety and security and proactively identify and report safety and operational concerns with the Programs and Services leadership.
  • Maintain accurate and consistent program documentation including incident reports, key performance indicators/ metrics to support operational effectiveness and program evaluation, funder requirements, compliance, and continuous improvement of child and youth programs and activities.
  • Demonstrate professional conduct that aligns with NYWS's values and provides safety, support, and empowerment for Clients.
  • Collaborate with the Programs and Services team to support areas where children and youth may need additional support.
  • Support caregivers to encourage both academic and character growth by ensuring children are able to build relationships with others, while developing self-regulation and problem-solving skills through play and inquiry-based learning.
  • Support caregivers to engage in positive interaction with children to build confidence and self-esteem.
  • Design and follow a full schedule of activities and identify suitable learning material including creative facilitation methods such as stories, media, indoor/outdoor games, etc.).
  • Support caregivers to address inappropriate behavior in a respectful and inclusive manner which helps facilitate reflection and growth.
  • Empower and educate parents and caregivers; help them formulate appropriate Individual Education Plan goals, accommodations, modifications, behavior plans, and identify appropriate related services such as Speech and Language, Occupational Therapy, Assistive Technology, Adaptive PE, and aide support as appropriate.
  • Facilitate homework clubs and assist in children and youth’s homework completion.
  • Demonstrate professional conduct that aligns with NYWS's values and provides safety, support, and empowerment for Clients.
  • Uphold confidentiality of all Clients and staff in accordance with organizational policies.
  • Attend and participate in additional team building, training, and community outreach projects as required.
  • Support NYWS in remaining current and active in harm reduction policy development and community advocacy.
  • Collaborate closely with staff to ensure continuity of care and consistent, high-quality support for children and youth.
  • Proactively uphold our principles of trauma-informed practice.
  • Additional duties as assigned.

Who you are:

Your Education and Experience:

  • You have completed or are currently enrolled in your last year of post-secondary education in Early Childhood Education Child Development and/or presently hold a Bachelor’s Degree in Psychology, Child Development, Education, and Family and Social Services.
  • You have experience and/or training in designing and implementing programs and activities for parents to support children and youth.
  • You have 2-3 years of experience working in adult programming, summer camps, after-school programs, recreational programs, or similar child and youth-focused and multicultural environments.
  • You have working knowledge of community services and resources and how to access them.
  • You have in-depth knowledge of child development milestones and understanding of best practices in early childhood learning and development.
  • You have experience and/or training in trauma-informed care or mental health.
  • You have or are willing to provide a satisfactory Vulnerable Sector Check (PVSC) with future checks.
  • You have completed CPR Level C and First Aid certifications.
  • You have superb written and oral communication skills and ability to tailor communication style to children and youth, caregivers, and staff.
  • You have excellent organization and time management skills
  • Strong knowledge and experience with harm reduction, anti-racist/anti-oppression strategies and trauma informed practice.
  • Current CPR and First Aid training
  • Satisfactory Vulnerable Sector Checks (PVSC)



Your Skills and Competencies:

  • You have basic knowledge of Microsoft Office tools e.g., Outlook and Word.
  • You take ownership for tasks and have strong work ethic.
  • You demonstrate excellent professional and empathetic communication skills.
  • You have strong problem solving and critical thinking skills.
  • You are able to document and take comprehensive notes.
  • You can work effectively independently as well as part of a team.
  • You are committed to understanding and working from an intersectional feminist, anti-racist, and anti-oppressive lens.
  • You have a high degree of confidentiality and discretion.
  • You can work under pressure and in crisis situations.
  • You are comfortable working in a pet-friendly environment.

The following additional qualifications would be considered assets:

  • Experience working with survivors of violence and their dependents.
  • Experience working with adults, children and youth who have witnessed intimate partner violence and/or situations of violence to possible risks of managing conflicts amongst women and children in crisis
  • Fluency with speaking and/ or writing in additional languages

Working conditions:

  • This role operates in a Gender-Based Violence (GBV) Shelter which provides client services inclusive of adults, children, youth, and houses pets (dogs and cats).
  • May be required to lift up to 30 lbs.
  • Walking, standing, bending, stooping, reaching, twisting, lifting, pushing, pulling, and/or moving items.
  • Speaking and listening on the telephone and using a computer.
  • Exposure to GBV and IPV subject matter and cases.
  • Occasional exposure to animals (dogs and cats).
  • Occasional exposure to loud sounds.
  • Occasional exposure to interpersonal conflict.
  • Occasional exposure to substance use.

Does this sound like the right opportunity for you? If so, please apply with your resume on BambooHR. Only applications submitted by October 13, 2026 at 5PM through the BambooHR application portal will be considered. Only candidates selected for an interview will be contacted. Please do not call the Shelter.

title: TrailWalker
description:
TrailWalker – Outdoor Behavioral Health Program

Location: Mesa, Arizona / Remote Arizona Backcountry
Schedule: 8 Days On / 6 Days Off
Starting Pay: $15.15/hour + applicable overtime (subject to minimum-wage verification)
Employment Type: Seasonal | Non-Exempt
Commitment: Minimum six months requested

Make a Difference. Experience the Trail.

Are you looking for meaningful work that challenges you physically, develops your leadership skills, and allows you to make a difference in the lives of others?

As a TrailWalker with ANASAZI Foundation, you will live and work in Arizona's backcountry, mentoring and supporting a small group of adolescents and young adults participating in our Outdoor Behavioral Health Care Program.

TrailWalkers serve as positive role models, providing direct care, protective oversight, outdoor education, and encouragement while helping participants develop personal responsibility, healthy relationships, and meaningful life skills.

This is an immersive outdoor position requiring dedication, adaptability, teamwork, and a commitment to participant safety.

Previous wilderness or behavioral health experience is preferred but not required. ANASAZI provides position-specific training.

What You'll Do

  • Monitor participant safety, well-being, hygiene, hydration, nutrition, and daily activities.
  • Teach outdoor living skills, personal responsibility, communication, and ANASAZI principles.
  • Support treatment goals established by the clinical team while maintaining appropriate professional boundaries.
  • Use approved communication, behavioral-support, and de-escalation techniques.
  • Assist with hiking, camping, food preparation, sanitation, water management, and field safety.
  • Maintain regular communication with field leadership and collaborate with clinical personnel.
  • Respond appropriately to emergencies, injuries, behavioral concerns, and environmental hazards according to training and established procedures.
  • Maintain accurate documentation and comply with confidentiality, client rights, and mandatory-reporting requirements.

TrailWalkers do not independently provide psychotherapy, diagnose behavioral health conditions, develop treatment plans, or perform nursing services.

Schedule & Outdoor Living

This is not a traditional 9-to-5 position. TrailWalkers live outdoors during assigned rotations and work in a remote, technology-limited environment.

  • Eight consecutive days on the trail, followed by six days off.
  • Overnight camping and outdoor living throughout each rotation.
  • Assignments may include weekends, holidays, and irregular hours.
  • Limited access to personal technology and modern conveniences.
  • Exposure to heat, cold, rain, rugged terrain, wildlife, and changing environmental conditions.

Physical Requirements

This position requires the ability to:

  • Hike approximately 3–15 miles per day over rugged and uneven terrain.
  • Carry a backpack weighing approximately 50 pounds or more for extended periods.
  • Stand, walk, climb, bend, kneel, lift, and carry equipment.
  • Participate in multi-day outdoor assignments under varying environmental conditions.
  • Maintain appropriate participant supervision and respond to field-safety needs.

Qualified individuals must be able to perform essential job functions with or without reasonable accommodation.

Minimum Qualifications

  • High school diploma or GED.
  • Current CPR and First Aid certification before required field assignments.
  • Arizona Fingerprint Clearance Card, as required by law and ANASAZI policy.
  • Ability to meet applicable background screening and job-related clearance requirements.
  • Successful completion of required orientation, field training, safety training, and competency assessments.
  • Dependability, sound judgment, adaptability, and strong interpersonal skills.
  • Willingness to make a minimum six-month employment commitment.

Experience working with youth, outdoor recreation, education, mentoring, or behavioral health is preferred.

Wilderness First Aid (WFA), Wilderness First Responder (WFR), EMT, or other advanced first-aid certifications are beneficial.

Professional Expectations

At ANASAZI, we believe the example our staff set is an important part of the experience we provide to participants and families.

Employees are expected to demonstrate integrity, personal responsibility, sound judgment, respect, appropriate professional boundaries, and conduct consistent with ANASAZI's mission and established policies.

TrailWalkers must maintain a substance-free working environment, comply with ANASAZI's alcohol, tobacco, drug, and safety policies, and refrain from reporting to or performing work while impaired.

Pre-Employment Training & Evaluation

Applicants selected to advance in the hiring process will be invited to participate in ANASAZI's pre-employment training and evaluation program.

This program includes approximately 5–6 days of backcountry instruction and 2–3 days of classroom-based orientation, during which participants learn about ANASAZI's philosophy, outdoor living practices, safety expectations, and program procedures.

Participation does not guarantee an offer of employment. Candidates will be evaluated throughout the process to determine their qualifications and suitability for the TrailWalker position.

The pre-employment training is unpaid, subject to applicable wage-and-hour requirements. Food and necessary field equipment will be provided during backcountry training.

Candidates selected for employment will receive compensation for all subsequent required work and compensable training, including supervised field assignments.

Hiring Process

  1. Submit an application.
  2. Participate in an initial screening call.
  3. Complete a virtual or in-person interview.
  4. Receive an invitation to pre-employment training and evaluation, if selected.
  5. Complete the backcountry and office training/evaluation components.
  6. Receive a conditional employment offer, if selected.
  7. Complete required pre-employment screening and onboarding.
  8. Participate in paid, supervised field training.
  9. Complete final competency verification before receiving an independent field assignment.

Compensation & Benefits

  • Starting pay: $15.15 per hour, plus applicable overtime, subject to applicable minimum-wage requirements.
  • Food provided during assigned trail rotations.
  • Initial field gear provided.
  • Wilderness First Aid training/certification opportunities.
  • Access to outdoor industry pro-deals.
  • Potential eligibility for insurance benefits upon transition to a qualifying regular full-time position, subject to plan terms and ANASAZI policy.

Actual earnings depend on compensable hours worked, applicable overtime, and assigned schedules.

Pre-Employment Requirements

Selected candidates may be required to complete applicable background screening, fingerprint clearance, medical clearance, and other position-related requirements.

Any required medical examinations or disability-related inquiries will be conducted after a conditional employment offer and in accordance with applicable law.

Additional information regarding documentation, potential applicant expenses, training dates, and onboarding requirements will be provided during the hiring process.

Ready to Become a TrailWalker?

If you enjoy the outdoors, value meaningful relationships, and want to help others develop skills that can positively influence their lives, we encourage you to apply.

Join ANASAZI Foundation and become part of a team dedicated to helping individuals and families find hope, strengthen relationships, and move toward meaningful change.

ANASAZI Foundation is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Reasonable accommodations are available to qualified applicants and employees in accordance with applicable law.

title: Summer Analyst, Asset Management
description:
Summer Analyst, Asset Management - The Coury Firm

The goal of the Summer Analyst, Asset Management position at The Coury Firm is to provide an opportunity for real world application of financial concepts and investment strategies learned in the academic environment. Individual instruction combined with shadowing mentors allows interns to make the connection between theory and practice.

Primary responsibilities of the Summer Analyst, Asset Management include:

  • Supporting the Asset Management team members in the execution of their duties
  • Contributing to the portfolio construction process and investment committee meeting preparation
  • Assisting in construction of the model portfolio menu, portfolio fulfillment options, manager fact cards, and the model portfolio interface
  • Assisting with the production of research reports and thought leadership pieces, including quarterly and annual investment outlooks
  • Assisting with macro-economic research and key macro slides and charts

  • Contributing to product research and development, including stock strategy research, futures hedging / overlay strategies, and quantitative strategies
  • Communicating with fund managers and key investment counterparties on matters related to due diligence, product development, and operational matters relevant to investment strategy and implementation
  • Assisting with client management and support, including transition sheets, client portfolio / holdings analysis, and client presentation support
  • Supporting private investment reporting for client portfolios
  • Contributing to ad hoc industry, company, and investment research projects
  • Administering and delivering the weekly market monitor model and commentary
  • Assisting with client material preparation and portfolio analysis
  • Assisting with client reporting technologies, including asset class coding, model portfolio coding, IPS frameworks, and private investment reporting
  • Coordinating with and assisting the Private Wealth team in administering and implementing investment recommendations as necessary
  • Other duties and special projects as assigned

QUALIFICATIONS

The Summer Analyst, Asset Management must meet the following qualifications to qualify for application/consideration:

  • Be a 2nd or 3rd year undergraduate candidate in a finance or business track program, or a current graduate student pursuing an MBA
  • Be open to all academic degrees; a background in Finance, Business, Economics, or a related field is preferred
  • Be in good academic standing with a minimum GPA of 3.3
  • Be proficient in MS Office Suite (Outlook, Excel, Word, and PowerPoint)
  • Be able to work in a fast-paced, team-based environment with minimal supervision
  • Possess strong communication skills
  • Demonstrate excellent work ethic, a desire for continual improvement, and strong intellectual curiosity

FOUNDING PRINCIPLES

Our Culture

At The Coury Firm, we foster a collaborative, entrepreneurial environment where team members are empowered to take initiative, think strategically, and grow both personally and professionally. We believe in a hands-on, client-focused approach rooted in trust, transparency, and excellence. Every team member plays a critical role in delivering exceptional outcomes for our clients.


Equal Opportunity Employer

The Coury Firm is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. All employment decisions are made based on qualifications, merit, and business needs, without regard to race, religion, gender, age, disability, or any other protected status.

title: Senior Operator
description:
Company Overview:

NDS, part of the Advanced Drainage Systems (ADS) family of companies, is a leading provider of stormwater, irrigation, and flow management solutions. Since 1972, NDS has helped protect and enhance properties through innovative water management products and trusted customer support. Together with ADS, we are committed to preserving water for future generations while delivering sustainable solutions for residential, commercial, infrastructure, and agricultural applications.

Responsibilities and Qualifications:

We are seeking a Second Shift Senior Operator who is responsible for performing the core functions of a Machine Operator while providing additional operational support to the production team. In coordination with the Sr. Lead and/or Supervisor, the Senior Operator assists with employee break and lunch coverage, ensures workstations remain supplied with required components, and supports the movement and preparation of finished product for warehousing. This position also assists with pallet wrapping and staging, box building, scanning, labeling, and label printing. The Senior Operator helps maintain safe, organized, and efficient production operations while supporting quality, productivity, and adherence to company policies and procedures.

Responsibilities:

Safety and 5S

  • Follow all company safety policies and requirements.
  • Wear PPE as required.
  • Follow proper ergonomic practices, including safe lifting, bending, and twisting techniques.
  • Report incidents in a timely manner.
  • Identify and report potential safety risks through VBS.
  • Maintain 5S standards throughout the plant and complete required 5S checklists, including keeping work areas clean and ensuring shadow boards are properly stocked.

Production and Material Handling

  • Load and unload items from machines, conveyors, and conveyances.
  • Assist Machine Operators with production activities.
  • Remove products or work pieces from production equipment.
  • Load and unload inserts into molds when required.
  • Process products, including assembly, inspection, and wrapping.
  • Monitor operating equipment to detect malfunctions.
  • Operate electric and manual pallet jacks.
  • Operate wrapping machines as required.
  • Examine products to verify conformance to quality standards.
  • Scan production parts using handheld scanners.

Support Machine Operators

  • Provide break and lunch coverage as assigned by the Sr. Lead and/or Supervisor and complete hourly boards when substituting for Machine Operators.
  • Remove completed pallets from machines.
  • Wrap completed pallets using hand wrap and automatic wrapping equipment.
  • Provide backup support to Machine Operators as needed.
  • Ensure workstations have the required WIP components.
  • Retrieve, build, and deliver boxes to machines.
  • Print and deliver labels as required.

Production Documentation

  • Read, understand, and complete travelers accurately.
  • Record production scrap data on production scrap reports.
  • Complete hourly boards as required.
  • Understand and sign break and lunch forms and confirm operators are complying with company break and lunch policies.

Other

  • Perform other duties and responsibilities as directed from time to time.

Position Requirements:

Education

  • High school diploma or General Education Degree (GED).

Experience

  • Three to six months of related experience and/or training; or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Ability to coordinate hand movements and use both hands to grasp, manipulate, or assemble objects.
  • Ability to bend, stretch, twist, or reach with the body, arms, and/or legs.
  • Ability to make fast, simple, repetitive movements with the fingers, hands, and wrists.

Work Conditions:

  • Work environment may occasionally include cold, hot, wet, and humid conditions.
  • Exposure to moving mechanical parts, confined work areas, and high noise levels. Hearing protection will be provided.
  • Ability to perform physical activities that require moving the whole body, including climbing, lifting, balancing, walking, and stooping.
  • Physical activities often require considerable use of the arms and legs, including the physical handling of materials.

This job description is not intended to be all-inclusive. Employee may perform other related duties to meet the ongoing needs of the organization.

Company Benefits:

NDS offers excellent benefits options as part of the total compensation package with a suite of options covering Life, Medical, Dental, and Vision as well as a 401k Retirement Plans.

EEO Statement:

ADS supports an inclusive workplace that values diversity of thought, experience, and background. We celebrate the power of our differences to create better solutions for our customers by ensuring employees can be their authentic selves each day. ADS is an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, ancestry, age, physical or mental disability, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity/expression, pregnancy, veteran status, marital status, creed, status with regard to public assistance, genetic status or any other status protected by federal, state or local law.

title: Media Production Specialist/Audio-Video Editor
description:
JOIN A MISSION-DRIVEN TEAM CREATING IMPACTFUL CONTENT

The American Association of Christian Counselors (AACC) is a leading organization committed to advancing the development of counseling professionals within a Christian framework.


We are seeking a creative and motivated Media Production Specialist/Audio-Video Editor to join our team and help produce high-quality video and audio content that inspires, educates, and engages our audience.


This role offers an exciting opportunity for individuals passionate about production and editing, as well as informative, educational, and clinical digital content. The ability to collaborate and the desire to grow their skills while contributing to projects that advance our mission is crucial.

WHY YOU’LL LOVE WORKING HERE

  • Work on meaningful projects that support Christian counseling professionals
  • Collaborate with designers, content creators, and other team members in a creative environment
  • Opportunity to develop and grow your video and audio production skills
  • Access to professional tools, software, and studio equipment
  • Be part of a mission-driven organization where your work makes a real difference

DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Video Editing: Edit footage into cohesive, engaging videos, both longform and shortform, with high production values, utilizing the latest leading styles and techniques, managing the narrative and communicating clearly with compelling storytelling
  • Audio and Video Production: produce, record and engineer high-quality video and audio for courses, podcasts, programs, voiceovers, and other media using studio gear and software
  • Creative Collaboration: Work closely with content creators, designers, and other team members to understand project requirements and deliver content aligned with brand and mission
  • Technical Proficiency: Use video editing software and graphic editing software (e.g., Adobe Premiere Pro, Final Cut Pro, After Effects, and Illustrator) and operate studio equipment such as switchers, routers, cameras, and audio mixers
  • Media Management: Organize, archive, and maintain video and audio files efficiently, following proper file naming and backup procedures
  • Quality Control: Review your own work as final content for submission for accuracy and quality, making revisions based on feedback
  • Creative Input: Conceptualize, design and implement graphics; search for B-roll and stock music, and place appropriately to help communicate and facilitate storytelling
  • Deadline Management: Manage multiple projects simultaneously and deliver work on time
  • Continuous Learning: Stay current with industry trends, techniques, and software updates to enhance creative output
  • Broadcast Duties: Support weekly in-studio production and postproduction for culture/faith/politics news-talk TV program
  • Event Production Support: Travel to conferences and events across the United States as needed to record and capture media content in studio and field environments

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor’s degree in Communications, Digital Media, Film Production, or a related field, or equivalent work experience
  • Proficiency in video editing software such as Adobe Premiere Pro or Final Cut Pro
  • Basic experience with audio editing and production (Adobe Audition or similar)
  • Strong attention to detail, high interest in digital content, and creative vision
  • Ability to collaborate effectively in a team environment
  • Strong communication skills and openness to feedback
  • Comfortable working in a fast-paced studio environment
  • Ability to lift and transport equipment up to 45 pounds as needed

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Basic knowledge of motion graphics, visual effects, and color grading
  • Experience managing media files and archiving procedures
  • Familiarity with studio equipment operation and setup
  • Experience producing short-form content for social media
  • Experience with videography and camera operation in both studio and field environments
  • Knowledge of camera setup, lighting techniques, and production best practices
  • Ability to assist with studio and field production setup and breakdown
  • Experience capturing high-quality audio in studio or live event environments
  • Proficient writing skills
  • Copywriting experience
  • Technical writing ability
  • Experience writing captions for social media and teleprompter script
  • Spanish-English skills a plus!


BENEFITS

  • Paid time off and holidays
  • Competitive benefits package including health, dental, and vision insurance
  • 401(k) retirement plan with employer match
  • Life insurance coverage
  • Health Savings Account (HSA) options available
  • Opportunities to grow within a national organization
  • Work with a supportive team in a purpose-driven environment
  • Participation in AACC events and ministry initiatives
  • On-site role with regular team interaction and collaboration
