title: Clinical Auditor
description:
Overview

UnityPoint Health is hiring a Clinical Auditor! This position will help develop and implement the education program aimed at enhancing documentation and coding practices across the organization. The Auditor will promote documentation accuracy by auditing and updating training tools for providers, clinical staff, coders and billing specialists. This role acts as a liaison between the providers, clinical staff and coders, provides updated and new materials, and helps answer documentation and coding questions.

Candidates that hold a certification in coding and have at least 3 years of experience in coding are encouraged to apply!

Location: Remote - applicants must reside within the UnityPoint Health footprint of Iowa, Illinois, or Wisconsin

Hours: Monday-Friday, standard business hours

Why UnityPoint Health?

At UnityPoint Health, you matter. We’re proud to be recognized as a Top 150 Place to Work in Healthcare by Becker's Healthcare several years in a row for our commitment to our team members.

Our competitive Total Rewards program offers benefits options that align with your needs and priorities, no matter what life stage you’re in. Here are just a few:

  • Expect paid time off, parental leave, 401K matching and an employee recognition program.
  • Dental and health insurance, paid holidays, short and long-term disability and more. We even offer pet insurance for your four-legged family members.
  • Early access to earned wages with Daily Pay, tuition reimbursement to help further your career and adoption assistance to help you grow your family.

With a collective goal to champion a culture of belonging where everyone feels valued and respected, we honor the ways people are unique and embrace what brings us together.

And, we believe equipping you with support and development opportunities is a vital part of delivering an exceptional employment experience.

Find a fulfilling career and make a difference with UnityPoint Health.

Responsibilities

Clinical Documentation Review and Reporting

  • Assess clinical documentation for compliance in accordance with the American Medical Association and the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services Coding and Documentation guidelines, regulations of federal and state agencies, and third party payers
  • Validate clinical documentation in conjunction with charges and evaluate accuracy and timeliness of the billing process
  • Investigate, evaluate and identify opportunities for improvement and provide guidance and counsel to providers with face-to-face meetings
  • Identify and audit areas requiring attention, performing special audits/investigations as requested, share this information with leadership and provide one-on-one education with the provider and in a timely manner
  • Collect and analyze data, submit reports as assigned and monitor monthly audits to ensure that they are completed timely
  • Report/record all documentation and coding issues that require follow-up reviews to coding manager
  • Work the EPIC follow-up and account work queues to keep queues in a manageable state; inform leadership of workflow issues with suggestions for improvement
  • Be aware of what is happening in clinic/department and the organization by attending clinic/department meetings, reading e-mails/in-basket messages and regularly checking information on the organization’s intranet site
  • Monitor environmental conditions in order to secure protected health information
  • Demonstrate initiative to improve quality and customer service by striving to exceed customer expectations
  • Balance team and individual responsibilities; be open and objective to other’s views; give and welcome feedback; contribute to positive team goals; and put the success of the team above own interests
  • Perform other duties at the request of various departmental leadership groups to facilitate the smooth and effective operations of the organization

Clinical Coding Research and Education

  • Participate in development and implementation of Office of Inspector General Work Plan
  • Research coding inquires and be a resource for providers, clinical, billing and coding staff
  • Monitor payment status of services with specific coding requirements as needed
  • Maintain compliance with CLIA, OSHA, Safety and Risk Management guidelines
  • Investigate, evaluate and identify opportunities for improvement and provide guidance and counsel to coding/billing staff by setting up small group meetings or training sessions
  • Provide regular education to providers, clinical, billing and coding staff regarding coding documentation standards
  • Help in updating the coding department’s newsletters, education, reference documents
  • Be involved in coding team activities, partnering with other departments to capitalize on our FOCUS values

Qualifications

Education:

  • Required: High school diploma or equivalent
  • Preferred: AAS Degree in Health Information Management

Experience:

  • Required: Effectively utilize resource tools to complete audits
  • Required: Proficient in organization’s electronic coding system
  • Preferred: Three (3) years of coding experience

Licenses:

  • Required: Will need to obtain and hold AHIMA or AAPC Coding certification within 12 months of start date
  • Required: Valid driver’s license when driving any vehicle for work-related reasons
  • Preferred: Coding certification through AHIMA: Registered Health Information Administrator (RHIT), Registered Health Information Technician (RHIA), Certified Coding Specialists (CCS), or AAPC Certified Professional Coder (CPC)

title: Lead Technical Data Analyst
description:
Who We Are

Addepar is a global data and AI platform empowering investment professionals to turn complex financial information into actionable intelligence. Addepar unifies portfolio, market and client data in a total portfolio view and delivers AI-powered insights within investment and client workflows. More than 1,500 firms in 60 countries use Addepar to manage and advise on nearly $10 trillion in assets. Its open platform integrates with 650 software, data and consulting partners to power end-to-end investment operations across firms of all sizes and levels of complexity. Addepar supports clients worldwide with offices in New York City, Salt Lake City, São Paulo, London, Edinburgh, Geneva, Warsaw, Dubai, Pune and Singapore.

The Role
As a Team Lead, Technical Data Analyst you will serve as a player-coach - guiding a team of analysts while also executing complex data work yourself. At this level, you are developing your people management skills while leveraging your product, industry, and technical knowledge to advance. You will be the technical anchor for your team, providing the daily guidance needed to navigate complex data challenges and meet project deadlines. You take the vision set by leadership and turn it into reality, ensuring the team stays aligned with our core processes. Your focus is on problem-solving and technical steering, acting as the first line of support to ensure your team's success. This role focused on the functional coaching and project delivery.

Applicants must have, and maintain, the right to work in the United Kingdom from the first day of employment. Please note that visa sponsorship is not available for this role.

What You’ll Do

  • Provide functional leadership and daily operational guidance to the team within the technical data function
  • Execute hands-on contribution to projects through data migration and data transformation using Python-based ETL tools.
  • Manage the team’s work allocation and coordinate activities to ensure results are driven by the team in collaboration with others.
  • Guide the team in issue resolution and escalate blockers proactively, maintaining alignment with stakeholders.
  • Support career development by providing continuous feedback loops on technical and project execution
  • Identify and drive opportunities to improve tools, workflows, and automation for greater efficiency.

Who You Are

  • Experience: 2+ years of related experience and a Bachelor’s degree, or 2+ years and a Master’s degree.

  • Technical Skills: Proficient in Python and knowledgeable in ETL workflows and data transformation logic.
  • Communication: Strong communication skills, able to conduct technical presentations and convey complex ideas clearly.
  • Organization: Highly organized with attention to detail, able to coordinate activities and deliver results that may impact schedules and costs.
  • Mindset: Solutions-driven mindset with a desire to improve processes and a commitment to personal growth in people management

Our Values

  • Act Like an Owner - Think and operate with intention, purpose and care. Own outcomes.
  • Build Together - Collaborate to unlock the best solutions. Deliver lasting value.
  • Champion Our Clients - Exceed client expectations. Our clients’ success is our success.
  • Drive Innovation - Be bold and unconstrained in problem solving. Transform the industry.
  • Embrace Learning - Engage our community to broaden our perspective. Bring a growth mindset.

In addition to our core values, Addepar is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We seek to bring together diverse ideas, experiences, skill sets, perspectives, backgrounds and identities to drive innovative solutions. We commit to promoting a welcoming environment where inclusion and belonging are held as a shared responsibility.

We will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please contact us to request accommodation.

title: Metallurgy Internship
description:
Subsidiary

Steel Dynamics

Overview

What Does Steel Dynamics Do?

Steel Dynamics is a leading industrial metals solutions company that produces lower-carbon, high-quality steel products primarily from recycled scrap. Operating through a circular manufacturing model, the company manufactures a wide range of steel products including flat roll, structural, and long products for industries such as construction, automotive, energy, and manufacturing. In addition to steel production, Steel Dynamics operates metals recycling facilities, steel fabrication plants, and aluminum production operations, serving customers across North America with a focus on innovation, efficiency, and sustainability.

What Makes This Internship Different?Steel Dynamics’ metallurgy internships stand apart from others in the market because they provide a true balance of office-based engineering work and hands-on industrial experience. Interns are not confined to observing from a distance; instead, they actively work alongside operators and maintenance teams on the production floor, applying engineering principles directly to equipment, systems, and processes. This immersive approach gives interns the opportunity to design solutions, test them in real-world conditions, and see the immediate impact of their work. At SDI, metallurgy is not limited to research and development, it is a dynamic combination of technical analysis and practical application that exposes interns to the full scope of how metallurgy drives production success.

Internship Location

This internship is located at the Steel Dynamics Engineered Bar Products Division located in Pittsboro, IN, in the Quality Department. This internship will take place Summer 2027.

Internship Benefits

  • Furnished Housing Free of Cost
    • Provided for interns living more than 50 miles from their work site, including essential furnishings to ensure a comfortable stay during the internship.
  • 401(k) & Company Match
    • Eligibility to participate in the company 401(k) plan with a 10–50% company match that vests immediately.
  • Employee Discounts
    • Access to discounts on hotels, vehicles, and other goods and services through Steel Dynamics’ nationwide partner network.
  • Employee Assistance Program
    • Up to five free visits per issue, per year for counseling, legal advice, financial guidance, and other daily living resources.
  • Intern Extravaganza
    • A two-day event at company headquarters featuring facility tours, networking with company leaders, cultural immersion, and connecting with other interns from across the country.
  • Competitive Pay
    • Competitive hourly wages for all internship positions, rewarding the value interns bring to the company.

Responsibilities

What Are My Responsibilities as a Metallurgy Intern at Steel Dynamics?

  • Assist with scrap and steel analysis using spectrometry and other lab tools to support quality and efficiency efforts.
  • Support steelmaking and rolling operations by collecting and analyzing production data, identifying yield loss points, and recommending improvements for efficiency and recovery.
  • Collaborate with operators, engineers, and lab personnel across shifts to ensure consistency in data collection, quality assurance, and process improvements.
  • Gain hands-on experience in steelmaking, rolling, NDT, heat treating, and laboratory operations tasks.

Qualifications

What Qualifications Do I Need?

  • Candidates should be enrolled in a Bachelor’s degree program in Metallurgical and/or Materials Science or Engineering
  • Preferred GPA of at least 2.7

Examples of Projects Steel Dynamics Metallurgy Interns Have Completed

  • Develop proprietary method to characterize microstructural banding in gear steels
  • Characterized variability of heat treat process and developed targeted melt process for high strength quenched and tempered steels
  • Characterized variation in electromagnetic stirrer design and operations
  • Developed grain refinement techniques and evaluated effects on grain size and toughness
  • Modeled and measured cooling curves and resulting impact on mixed as-rolled microstructures

title: LINC Instructor
description:
Position Summary

KCR is seeking a passionate and adaptable LINC Instructor to deliver English language instruction to adult newcomers in a welcoming, inclusive, and engaging learning environment. The LINC Instructor will plan and facilitate lessons aligned with the Canadian Language Benchmarks (CLB) and Portfolio-Based Language Assessment (PBLA) guidelines. The successful candidate will support learners in developing practical language skills, building confidence, and progressing toward their settlement, employment, and community goals.


This is a part-time, 15-hour-per-week contract position ending in March 2027, with the potential for extension based on program needs and funding availability. With a regular work schedule of Monday to Friday, 8:30 AM to 11:30 AM. Classroom instruction takes place from 9:00 AM to 10:30 AM daily, with the remaining scheduled hours dedicated to lesson planning, class preparation, learner assessments, administrative duties, and other program-related responsibilities.


Reporting Structure:

Reports to LINC Coordinator

Key Responsibilities

Instruction and Lesson Planning

  • Deliver English language instruction to adult newcomers in accordance with CLB principles, PBLA guidelines, and LINC curriculum requirements.
  • Develop module plans and lesson plans that reflect learner needs, language levels, and settlement goals.
  • Create an inclusive classroom environment that respects and values cultural diversity.
  • Provide learners with appropriate classroom and program orientations, including information about safe practices.
  • Adapt instructional approaches and materials to support different learning styles and abilities.

Assessment and Learner Progress

  • Develop assessment tasks to evaluate learner progress in accordance with CLB and PBLA guidelines.
  • Accurately benchmark learner progress and maintain up-to-date learner portfolios.
  • Provide clear, timely, and constructive feedback to support continued learning and development.
  • Identify learners who may require additional support and collaborate with appropriate staff when needed.

Administration and Documentation

  • Maintain accurate attendance records, lesson plans, assessment records, and other required program documentation.
  • Prepare and submit quarterly reports to support program monitoring and reporting requirements.
  • Ensure all records and documentation are completed accurately and within required timelines.

Technology and Blended Learning

  • Use online teaching platforms, including Avenue.ca, to support blended and digital learning.
  • Incorporate multimedia, digital resources, and interactive tools to enhance instruction and learner engagement.
  • Support learners in developing the digital literacy skills required to participate successfully in online and blended learning environments.

Collaboration and Professional Development

  • Collaborate with instructors, program staff, and community partners to share resources, strategies, and best practices.
  • Participate in team meetings, professional development opportunities, and required training.
  • Complete or maintain relevant training, including LearnIT2teach, as required.
  • Contribute to a positive, respectful, and collaborative workplace culture.


Qualifications:

  • Undergraduate degree with a TESL Certification from a training institute accredited by TESL Canada.
  • Minimum 1 year of experience teaching ESL to adult newcomers; ELSA or LINC experience preferred.
  • Exceptional written and oral English language communication skills.
  • Sound knowledge of Canadian Language Benchmarks and PBLA principles with the ability to benchmark student progress.
  • Online teaching experience is an asset.
  • Experience teaching Literacy is an asset.
  • Familiarity with Avenue.ca and LearnIT2teach training and experience.
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a group environment.
  • Ability to work in a blended learning environment.


Application Process:

KCR Community Resources welcomes and encourages applications from people with diverse abilities. We will strive to provide reasonable accommodations, accessible formats, and communication support upon request to people with diverse abilities in all aspects of the recruitment and selection process.

If you require accommodation as part of the application process, please contact HR at our main office on 250 763 8008.


About KCR Community Resources:

KCR is a not-for-profit agency fostering diversity, collaboration, and resourcefulness by tailoring services to meet the community, family, and individual needs. We believe in a community where individuals and families are supported in leading healthy, productive, and fulfilling lives.

title: Associate Advisor
description:
About Us

Bartholomew & Company is a financial services firm headquartered in Worcester, MA managing approximately $6 billion in assets across two divisions: Governments and Institutions, which serves public entities and institutional clients, and Private Wealth, which serves individuals, families, and business owners.


This role can be based in our Worcester, MA or Framingham, MA office within our Private Wealth division, which manages approximately $2.5 billion for clients across the country. We take a disciplined, client-centered approach to wealth management, tailoring strategies to each client's goals and risk tolerance. Our deep expertise in institutional asset management provides clients with access to opportunities, sophistication, and diversification not typically available to individual investors.


About the Role

This full-time, salaried position is a client-focused advisory support role designed for professionals who want to build and apply their knowledge of financial planning, investments, and wealth management while contributing meaningfully to client experience and outcomes. Working closely with Wealth Advisor(s) and other members of the advisory team, the Associate Advisor supports client relationships, meeting preparation and follow-up, financial planning activities, investment-related needs, and business development initiatives. Over time, the role provides opportunities to deepen technical expertise, expand client-facing responsibilities, and develop greater ownership of client relationships. The Associate Advisor role is designed to support multiple career paths within Bartholomew & Company. For individuals who aspire to become a Wealth Advisor, the position provides the experience, mentorship, licensure, professional development, and client exposure necessary to progress toward an independent Wealth Advisor role. For individuals who prefer to build a long-term career as a highly skilled, planning-focused member of an advisory team, the Associate Advisor may also serve as a rewarding career role focused on client service, planning support, relationship management, and advisor partnership. Success in the role is defined by the Associate Advisor's contribution to clients, the advisory team, and the firm — not solely by progression to a Wealth Advisor position.


Essential Responsibilities and Duties

Learning & Professional Development

  • Pursue and obtain FINRA licensure (SIE, Series 7, Series 66) within the timeframe specified.
  • Actively participate in firm training, advisor mentorship programs, and professional development activities.
  • Study toward professional designations as directed by management.
  • Shadow Wealth Advisor(s) in client meetings and progressively assume responsibility for defined portions of meetings as readiness is demonstrated.

Client Service & Relationship Support

  • Assist licensed Wealth Advisor(s) with client meeting preparation, presentation materials, meeting agendas, and follow-up activities.
  • Gather and organize client financial data in support of financial planning development and ongoing client reviews.
  • Respond to routine client inquiries under the supervision and direction of a licensed wealth advisor.
  • Maintain accurate client records and document client interactions, decisions, and follow-up items in the CRM system (WealthBox).
  • Develop familiarity with client relationships and service standards in order to assume increasing client-facing responsibility over time, including proactive client outreach.

Financial Planning & Advisory Support

  • Support the preparation of financial planning analyses and recommendations using firm-approved planning tools and processes (Right Capital, Holistiplan, others as appropriate).
  • Build working knowledge of the firm's investment philosophy, planning approach, client segmentation, and service model.
  • Develop the ability to explain core financial planning and investment concepts clearly and accurately to clients and internal team members.
  • Coordinate with advisors, teammates, and other internal resources to ensure planning and investment-related follow-up is completed accurately and on time.

Business Development & Team Growth

  • Develop the relationship-building and discovery skills necessary to contribute meaningfully to new client acquisition and asset growth.
    • Participate in firm-sponsored community, client, and business-development events, as appropriate.
    • Begin building and maintaining a professional network and pipeline of prospective clients under the guidance of wealth advisors.
    • Support Advisors in prospecting activities, including materials preparation, opportunity tracking, and follow-up coordination.


Core Skills, Competencies & Characteristics

  • Clients First. Always: Approaches every client-related task with care, professionalism, responsiveness, and a commitment to delivering an exceptional experience.
  • Own Your Role: Takes a proactive approach to problem solving and contributing to team and client success, demonstrates sound judgment, follows through on commitments, upholds high ethical standards and a fiduciary mindset in all work and client interactions, and appropriately escalates matters outside the scope of the role.
  • Pursue Excellence: Holds work to a high standard rather than the minimum required, demonstrating exceptional attention to detail across client data, financial planning documentation, and compliance records, as errors can directly impact client outcomes and firm compliance, while continually looking for ways to improve accuracy, clarity, and quality.
  • Stay Humble. Be Curious: Demonstrates genuine enthusiasm for financial markets, planning concepts, and the wealth management profession through inquisitiveness, and is receptive to feedback and actively applies mentorship to develop technical expertise and understanding of the advisory process.


Required Skills and Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in any field of study.
  • 0-5 years of financial services and/or advisory experience; internship or academic experience in financial services preferred.
  • FINRA SIE, Series 7, and Series 66 must be obtained within the timeframe specified in the employment offer; Bartholomew & Company will sponsor required licensure and study materials.
  • Demonstrated academic achievement and a strong interest in financial planning, investment management, and wealth management.
  • Strong written and verbal communication, organization, attention to detail, and follow-through.


Technology Skills

  • Microsoft Office 365, with proficiency in Word, Excel, Copilot, and PowerPoint.
  • CRM platforms (e.g., Wealthbox, ClientWorks); training provided.
  • Financial planning software (e.g., RightCapital, Holistiplan, or equivalent); training provided.
  • Video conferencing platforms, including Zoom and Microsoft Teams.
  • Proficiency in AI platforms and ability to use them in accordance with firm policies and procedures.


Optional Career Progression: Advancement to Wealth Advisor

For Associate Advisors who choose to pursue the Wealth Advisor career path, advancement is based on demonstrated readiness for greater client, advisory, and business-development responsibility rather than tenure alone. Meeting the criteria below establishes eligibility for consideration but does not guarantee promotion. Final advancement decisions remain subject to management approval, business needs, and the employee's overall performance and conduct.


Licensing & Registration: SIE, Series 7, and Series 66 are completed within the required timeframe; all applicable registrations are maintained in good standing.


Professional Development: Required firm training is completed and the Associate Advisor demonstrates meaningful progress toward firm-approved professional designation, as directed by management.


Technical Planning & Investment Proficiency: Can accurately gather and analyze client information, prepare financial plans, use firm systems effectively, and explain foundational planning and investment concepts with limited supervision.


Client-Facing Readiness: Can lead defined portions of client meetings and, when assigned, routine review meetings; communicates clearly and professionally, completes follow-up reliably, and demonstrates appropriate judgments with clients.


Relationship Ownership: Demonstrates the ability to manage assigned client responsibilities or a defined segment of relationships with increasing independence, identify client needs, coordinate internal resources, and escalate complex matters appropriately.


Business Development: Maintains an active professional network and prospect pipeline and demonstrates the ability to contribute to new client acquisition and asset growth. Any specific AUM, revenue, or production threshold for advancement will be established by management.


Execution, Compliance & Risk Management: Consistently maintains accurate CRM documentation, follows firm procedures, meets deadlines, protects client information, and demonstrates sound compliance and risk-management practices.


Performance & Core Competencies: Consistently meets or exceeds performance expectations and demonstrates the firm's core competencies, including initiative, client focus, coachability, ownership, integrity, and sound judgment.


Management Readiness Review: The supervising advisor(s) and management determine that the Associate is prepared to assume Wealth Advisor-level client responsibility, accountability, and growth expectations.


Physical Requirements

Primary functions require sufficient physical ability and mobility to work in an office setting; to stand or sit for long periods of time; to occasionally stoop, bend, kneel, reach, and twist; to lift, carry, push, and/or pull light to moderate amounts of weight; to operate office equipment requiring repetitive hand movement and fine coordination including the use of a computer, keyboard, copy machine, printer, and calculator; and ability to communicate information and ideas in a manner that others will understand.


EEO Statement

Bartholomew & Company is an Equal Opportunity employer and does not discriminate in employment on the basis of race, color, religious creed, sex (including pregnancy and gender identity), national origin, political affiliation, sexual orientation, marital status, disability, genetic information, age, membership in an employee organization, retaliation, parental status, military service, and/or other status protected under law.

title: Client Assistance Program (CAP) Advocate
description:
Client Assistance Program (CAP) Advocate





ABOUT DISABILITY JUSTICE

Disability Justice is a nonprofit civil rights organization. Over the last 50 years, we’ve led the fight for dignity and inclusion — recognizing, as Dr. King did, that “injustice anywhere is a threat to justice everywhere.” Our team of advocates, attorneys, and investigators forms Colorado’s Protection and Advocacy system. Our goal: to make Colorado the best place in America for people with disabilities to live, work, and thrive.



POSITION OVERVIEW

The Client Assistance Program (CAP) Advocate provides advocacy for clients who have complaints about services they have or have not received from the Division of Vocational Rehabilitation (DVR) and Centers for Independent Living (CILs). The CAP Advocate gathers information from clients, provides clients with information about their rights and options, reviews DVR and CIL case files, and facilitates information-gathering and dispute resolution between clients and DVR/CIL staff.

The CAP Advocate stays current on the laws and regulations governing DVR and CILs and provides training to DVR and CIL staff on CAP. As appropriate, the CAP Advocate also coordinates with other Disability Justice staff on cases, community trainings, and outreach.



REPORTING RELATIONSHIPS

The CAP Advocate reports directly to one of the Co-Legal Directors. The CAP Advocate has no direct reports.



PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES

The following duties are an overview of the primary duties and responsibilities of the CAP Advocate and should not be considered an all-inclusive list:

  • Responds promptly to newly assigned clients and manages cases from initial contact through resolution.
  • Gathers information from clients and investigates complaints of wrongful denial or delay of services by DVR or CILs, including outright/constructive denials, process barriers, and communication breakdowns.
  • Advocates on behalf of clients, informing them of DVR's and CILs' service obligations and their rights.
  • Documents casework accurately and communicates case status to the attorney supervisor, requesting guidance as needed.
  • Maintains subject-matter expertise on laws and regulations governing DVR and CILs, and stays current on rules regarding the unauthorized practice of law.
  • Develops and maintains up-to-date CAP materials, fact sheets, and resources for clients and the community.
  • Conducts outreach for CAP and PABSS programs statewide, including transition events (events supporting youth with disabilities as they prepare to move from high school to post-secondary education or employment).
  • Represents the organization on community committees (e.g., the State Rehabilitation Council)
  • Monitors case numbers and client feedback to ensure effective use of resources and high-quality service.
  • Assists with federal reporting requirements related to CAP.
  • Upholds the values of the disability rights movement and Disability Justice's reputation as a trusted, competent resource.
  • Performs other duties as assigned, including additional advocacy work directed by the Co-Legal Directors and participation in Disability Justice meetings.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The individual must also possess these qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent work experience
  • At least 3 years of experience providing direct client services
  • Ability to obtain suitability credentials from the Social Security Administration, as required by our grant, within the first six months of employment. You do not need to complete this process before applying for this position. For more information about the process, please see: shorturl.at/abeR6
  • Ability to work independently in a hybrid or remote environment, as well as under general supervision and on a team
  • Experience entering data correctly and in a timely manner into a database system
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills
  • Demonstration of appropriate and professional behavior in working with members of the public who may often be in crisis
  • Proficiency with office technology, databases, Microsoft Suite applications, email, the Internet, and other relevant applications, such as Zoom
  • Understanding of and commitment to legal ethics for nonlawyers
  • Ability to work nonstandard hours and/or travel, as needed

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

The following qualifications are highly desired to advance our work, but they are not required:

  • Bilingual or multilingual
  • Three years experience working with and advocating on behalf of individuals with disabilities
  • Bachelor’s or advanced degree in a relevant field, such as social work, legal studies, or public policy
  • Personal or professional experience navigating the vocational rehabilitation system
  • Experience working with ASL interpreters, assistive technology, people whose primary language is not English, and accessibility problem-solving



WORK ENVIRONMENT

Applicants for this position must live in Colorado or be willing to relocate to Colorado before beginning employment. We allow employees to work from home or from our Denver office, with the understanding that they will meet in person as needed to conduct their job functions and collaborate with colleagues, clients, and partners. We provide equipment to employees to work successfully in a remote environment, including but not limited to laptops and phones.

Disability Justice provides reasonable accommodations to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of their jobs and participate in the recruitment and interview processes. For support with the application process, please contact Gina Brown at gbrown@disabilitylawco.org.

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS

The hiring range is 65,000 to 72,000 annually, depending on experience. This is a full-time position of 36 hours per week. Disability Justice offers paid holidays, parental leave, annual leave, sick leave, and bereavement leave; as well as medical, vision, dental, and retirement plans for full-time employees.

APPLICATION PROCESS

Candidates must use Bamboo to submit a cover letter, outlining their interest and qualifications, along with their resume. Applications submitted on other portals will not be considered. Applications are due by October 19. We will consider applications as they are received.


Disability Justice strives to build a team that reflects the community we serve. The call of disability rights work is: “Nothing about us without us.’’ We encourage candidates with disabilities and others with lived experience and diverse backgrounds to apply.

ANTI-DISCRIMINATION POLICY

Disability Justice prohibits harassment and discrimination based on disability; age; ancestry; national origin or ethnicity; citizenship; immigration status; race; color; hair style or hair texture; marital, registered domestic partner, or civil union status; pregnancy and perceived pregnancy (including breastfeeding or related medical conditions); religion; sex; gender, gender identity or expression; sexual orientation or an employer’s perception thereof; wage disclosures; lawful off-duty, off-premises activities; because the person is a victim of a crime, domestic violence, sexual assault, or stalking; military or veterans’ status; family or medical care leave status; or any other basis protected by federal, state, or local law or ordinance or regulation. This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation, and training.

title: Blood Bank Manager
description:
Continental Services Group is looking for an individual with supervisory and managerial experience to assist in the operation our blood bank in Miami. You will be responsible for overseeing the center and the center's operational staff in any area directly dealing with blood donors. Continental has been in business for over 50-years and is a private for-profit blood banking company. We service pharmaceutical and research companies all over the world, and our product is used for research and diagnostic testing materials. With two centers, one in Fort Lauderdale and one in Miami, we provide our blood donors with quality customer services.


Your Responsibilities Will Include:


  • Organizing staff schedules to ensure efficiency for the center operations, while managing overtime
  • Reviewing SOP and processes to ensure staff are following Continental SOP's and complying with FDA Regulations and cGMP
  • Directing staff for safe and efficient work flow
  • Monitoring the assignment of donors, to ensure company orders are fulfilled in a timely fashion
  • Professionally interact with donors and staff to assure the donor experience is a safe, efficient and enjoyable process


Ideal Candidates Meet the Following Requirements:


  • Must fluently speak, understand and write English; the ability to speak Spanish is a plus
  • Must be highly organized and have a strong attention to detail
  • Must be able to operate in a fast-paced environment
  • Must have proficient computer skills
  • EMT certification is a plus
  • May have previously demonstrated exceptional customer service and management in another work environment
  • May have a background and interest in the medical health field


What You Can Expect from Us:


  • You’ll Be Treated Fairly-- We are a family-owned and operated company, and we consider each of our employees as part of our larger family. We operate and make our decisions based on merit, qualifications and performance.
  • You’ll Be Challenged-- We hold very specialized and several regulatory licenses, which means our work environment is constantly evolving as agencies continue to update and improve their standards.
  • You’ll Be Provided with Benefits-- After a probationary period, you have the option to part take in the health insurance we provide. You also will have the option to start a 401k, all expenses of setting up the account covered by us. You’ll also have access to profit sharing.


What We Expect From You:


  • Communication - We feel this is the most important aspect of any job. You must be in communication with your supervisor, and make sure they are familiar and in agreement with your everyday tasks.
  • Timeliness - Everything we do--from shipping out specialty products to scheduling specific donors--is on a schedule. While we are very flexible in terms of time off and scheduling, we operate on the assumption that our employees will be timely, and if necessary, gives plenty of notice of their future absence.
  • Team Work - Our operations, testing and systems are complex and multifaceted, so we expect you to work well with our current team members--from those in the lab to those in administration--to ensure we work most cohesively.
  • Flexibility - We have two centers: our home office in Miami, and a second in Fort Lauderdale. We expect that if necessary, you are willing to work at either location, in the case of an emergency. Your gas and time would be compensated for a short period, if we ask that you work in a station that is not your home station. We also expect that you’ll be willing to jump in anywhere in the office where we might need you.
  • Willingness to Learn - While we expect you’ll come in with a variety of basic skills, we ask that you come also knowing you’ll learn a lot here.


Salary & Benefits


  • Competitive salary within the field. Final determination will depend on experience level and qualifications.
  • 401k & Profit Sharing Program - 401k available after one year of service, and profit sharing program is fully funded and invested.
  • Medical, Gap, Dental and Vision Insurance - A majority of the insurance fees is paid for by Continental. We can talk to you about what kind of plan will work for you and your family.
  • Life Insurance Policy - We offer a life insurance policy for each of our employees, and this cost is covered completely by CSG.


About Continental Services Group Inc.


We are an FDA-licensed company that has been in business for over 50 years. We provide blood components and other biological raw materials to our customers, who use the material for the further manufacturing of in-vitro diagnostic products. The vast majority of the product we sell is used for manufacturing test kits and controls, which are used in hospitals around the world. Holding some of the industry's most specialized certifications, we draw the blood and other raw material from a wide base of donors, a majority of which repeatedly and consistently visits every 56 days. This repeat-donor base allows us to provide extensively tested and unique products to the pharmaceutical industry.


Continental has been an FDA licensed facility since 1971, holding multiple city, state and federal licenses, and has been ISO 9001 certified since 2003.

title: Institutional Giving and Grants Manager
description:
ABOUT CANDLELIGHTERS

Founded in 1978 by two families facing childhood cancer, Candlelighters Childhood Cancer Foundation of Nevada is the state’s first and oldest nonprofit dedicated to supporting families affected by childhood cancer. The organization provides emotional support, quality of life programs, and financial assistance to children and their families, serving approximately 400 families and more than 1,800 children each year. All services are offered at no cost, with a mission to help families focus on their child’s journey and well-being, and a vision to ensure no family faces childhood cancer alone.


JOB SUMMARY

Candlelighters is looking for an Institutional Giving and Grants Manager to lead our corporate giving and institutional grant fundraising efforts. This role builds relationships with funders, researches funding opportunities, writes and submits proposals, solicits corporate support, and prepares final reports for annual and special project funding campaigns.

Working closely with the Family Services team and other staff, the Institutional Giving and Grants Manager aligns funding opportunities with organizational needs and is responsible for achieving our annual grant and institutional funding goals.

  • Write compelling grant and corporate proposals to secure funding for annual and special project campaigns that meet or exceed annual funding goals.
  • Gather information from internal departments for inclusion in proposals/reports.
  • Liaise with corporate/foundation/government staff for information gathering; proposal/report compilation and submission; and solicitation of funding.
  • Expand the base of institutional and corporate funders, resulting in financial growth in grants and corporate giving support.
  • Plan, organize, and execute funder cultivation and stewardship events.
  • Develop and update schedule of grant applications and reporting deadlines for current and potential funders.
  • Manage grant tracking and required reporting.
  • Record up-to-date funding records in the donor management system.
  • Ensure receipt and recognition of grants and financial support from institutional and corporate funders.
  • Participate in and assist at Development events to interface with donors/funders and provide support to the Development Team.
  • Act as an ambassador for the organization by attending community events, networking functions, and fundraising forums. Engage with the public at tabling events effectively promoting and raising awareness about Candlelighters' missions.
  • Effectively leverages AI tools to increase efficiency, productivity, and effectiveness in completing job responsibilities.
  • Regularly conduct tours of office and programs.
  • Stay updated on industry trends and best practices.
  • Performs other related duties as assigned.



REQUIRED SKILLS/ABILITIES:

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to interact comfortably and effectively with the community.
  • Strong interpersonal and relationship-building skills.
  • Ability to work collaboratively across departments to support the preparation and implementation of grant proposals and corporate contributions.
  • Demonstrate strategic thinking and planning abilities.
  • Ability to manage and meet multiple, and at times competing, deadlines.
  • Proficient in computer software including but not limited to word processing, email, spreadsheets, and databases. Experience with CRM software Bloomerang, a plus. Experience with design programs like Canva or Adobe a plus.



EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

  • Bachelor's degree in fields such as nonprofit management, business administration, marketing, communications, public relations, or a related field is required.
  • A minimum of five years of fundraising or sales experience with at least three years of grant-writing experience.
  • Familiarity with the nonprofit sector, including trends, best practices, and legal and ethical considerations related to fund raising and donor relations.
  • Experience in planning, organizing, and executing donor cultivation and stewardship activities.
  • Knowledge of local corporation and foundation giving trends and success in securing gifts $10,000-$300,000.

TRAVEL

The position may require occasional overnight or extended travel.


SCHEDULE

Monday through Thursday, on-site, occasional evenings and weekends.


LICENSE AND EMPLOYMENT REQUIREMENTS

Position requires proof of authorization to work in the U.S., fingerprinting, and background check.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

  • Ability to sit or stand for extended periods
  • Must be able to lift 15 pounds at times
  • Frequent use of a computer, phone, and office equipment


WORK ENVIRONMENT

  • Thrive in a fast-paced do-it-yourself environment with occasional periods of intense workloads.
  • Ability to work well within a cross-function team environment and diverse communities.
  • Enthusiasm for working in a small organization where flexibility, teamwork, and a good sense of humor are absolute necessities.


JOB BENEFITS

  • Healthcare Insurance (medical, dental, and vision)
  • Life Insurance and AD&D
  • 401(k) Plan
  • Generous paid time off
  • 9 Paid holidays

Candlelighters is an equal opportunity employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws.

title: Junior Marketing Data Analyst
description:
IC Markets Global is one of the most renowned Forex CFD provider, offering trading solutions for active day traders and scalpers as well as traders that are new to the forex market. IC Markets Global offers its clients cutting edge trading platforms, low latency connectivity and superior liquidity.

IC Markets Global is revolutionizing online forex trading. Traders are now able to gain access to pricing previously only available to investment banks and high net worth individuals. Our management team have significant experience in the Forex, CFD and Equity markets in Asia, Europe and North America. It is this experience that has enabled us to select the best possible technology solutions and hand pick some of the best pricing providers available in the market.


About the role

We are looking for a Junior Marketing Data Analyst to support our Snowflake data environment and marketing reporting. Working with the marketing, data and Risk teams, you will help maintain consistent data across connected systems, prepare analysis and gradually contribute to predictive modelling projects. Training and guidance will be provided, with responsibilities increasing as your knowledge and practical skills develop.

  • Support Snowflake connections, integrations and routine data updates, helping investigate issues with the data team.
  • Run and adapt SQL queries to prepare datasets for reporting and analysis.

  • Coordinate agreed data exchanges with the Data and Risk teams, checking that incoming and outgoing datasets match the required definitions and formats.
  • Maintain and update Power BI dashboards, answer routine data requests and prepare figures and observations for monthly presentations.
  • Contribute to supervised predictive modelling experiments, such as exploring the likelihood of clients completing onboarding or making a first deposit.
  • Document queries, data checks and reporting processes so that results can be reviewed and reproduced.
  • What we are looking for
  • A recent graduate in computer science, data analytics or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience. Academic projects and internships are welcome.
  • Basic SQL skills, working knowledge of Excel and familiarity with Power BI.
  • Attention to detail, logical problem solving and the ability to explain findings clearly.
  • Willingness to learn, collaborate across teams and seek guidance when needed.
  • Python, pandas and introductory statistics or machine learning experience would be useful. Previous Snowflake experience is helpful but not required.

title: General Manager – Big Molly Operations
description:
WAYFINDER CORP is a privately held, Alberta-based company that provides total proppant management for oil and gas E&P companies. We make extra efforts to support our clients in achieving their goals, as their success is linked to ours.


Concentrating on serving the Western Canadian Sedimentary Basin, we strive to exceed the expectations of all stakeholders by empowering our team members and by continuously improving upon our strategic goals.


Our Big Molly site near Glenevis (40 minutes northwest of Spruce Grove) is our regional Sand Processing Facility where we mine, wash and dry frac sand for direct shipment to our customers. We take pride in our product and value our employees while providing a close-knit, local place to work.


Wayfinder’s compensation and benefits are competitive and comprehensive to ensure our employees and their families are taken care of. We have implemented a Total Rewards package that includes employer-paid comprehensive extended health and dental coverage, a health spending account, RRSP matching, and career development opportunities.


THE OPPORTUNITY

Reporting to the Director – Operations and based at the Big Molly site, the General Manager – Big Molly Operations is accountable for the safe, reliable, efficient, and profitable performance of the operation.


The position provides integrated leadership across mine and extraction activities, production, maintenance, operational optimization, site services, and technical support.


As the senior operational leader for Big Molly, the General Manager translates corporate strategy into site plans, aligns people and resources to business priorities, and ensures the operation consistently achieves its safety, environmental, production, quality, cost, customer service, and workforce objectives.


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Operational Management:

⁕ Lead the safe, efficient, reliable, and profitable operation of Big Molly, with overall accountability for mine and extraction activities, production, maintenance, operational optimization, and supporting site functions

⁕ Coach, upskill and mentor management teams to perform optimally and in alignment with our core values of integrity, teamwork, service and excellence

⁕ Deliver production, product quality, operating cost, asset reliability, and customer service objectives while balancing immediate operating needs with long-term asset health

⁕ Oversee annual and monthly operating plans, production schedules, resource allocation, shutdown priorities, and asset performance

⁕ Establish and monitor meaningful key performance indicators, operating rhythms, and corrective action plans to improve performance and strengthen accountability

⁕ Drive operational excellence through disciplined planning, data-informed decision-making, root-cause analysis, and continuous improvement

⁕ Ensure effective coordination across Operations, Maintenance, Logistics, HSE, Geology, Projects, Finance, Human Resources, and other corporate functions


Safety and Compliance:

⁕ Champion a safety-first culture through visible field leadership, consistent expectations, and active engagement with employees and contractors.

⁕ Ensure compliance with applicable occupational health and safety, environmental, regulatory, permit, and corporate requirements.

⁕ Lead site risk management and emergency preparedness efforts to protect employees, contractors, assets, the environment, and business continuity.

⁕ Partner with the HSE team to strengthen safety systems, reporting, investigations, corrective actions, and organizational capability.

⁕ Ensure leaders maintain effective contractor management, safe work practices, training compliance, and audit readiness.


Leadership and Workforce Capability:

⁕ Lead, develop, and mentor a high-performing team of operational, maintenance, technical, and site-support leaders

⁕ Foster a culture of accountability, respect, teamwork, open communication, and continuous improvement

⁕ Oversee workforce planning, organizational design, succession planning, talent development, and leadership coverage for the site

⁕ Ensure effective goal setting, performance management, competency development, progression planning, and training compliance

⁕ Partner with Human Resources on employee and labour relations matters, workforce programs, leadership development, and change management

⁕ Align leaders and teams to corporate priorities, business objectives, and clearly defined decision rights


Budgeting and Cost Management

⁕ Maintain accountability for operating budgets, forecasts, cost controls, and capital expenditures for Big Molly

⁕ Lead capital planning, business case development, and investment prioritization based on safety, reliability, production, risk, and return

⁕ Review financial and operating performance, identify variances, and implement timely corrective actions

⁕ Identify and execute opportunities to improve profitability, operating efficiency, equipment utilization, and asset life

⁕ Partner with Finance and executive leadership to support annual business planning, forecasting, and performance reporting

Strategic Planning:

⁕ Collaborate with executive leadership to develop and execute long-term business and operating strategies for Big Molly

⁕ Develop long-range operational, workforce, maintenance, infrastructure, and capital plans that support sustainable growth and operational resilience

⁕ Identify opportunities for innovation, technology adoption, process improvement, and operational advancement

⁕ Monitor industry trends, market requirements, regulatory developments, and emerging operational risks to support strategic decision-making

⁕ Lead site readiness for growth initiatives, major projects, changes in production requirements, and evolving customer needs

⁕ Ensure environmental performance meets regulatory, permit, and corporate expectations

⁕ Promote responsible resource development, efficient resource use, and sustainable operating practices

⁕ Integrate environmental considerations into operating plans, capital decisions, mine planning, and risk management

QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE

⁕ Minimum 15 years of progressive experience in mining, aggregates, manufacturing, or industrial operations, including 5 years in a senior leadership role

⁕ Demonstrated success leading large-scale operations with accountability for safety, operational performance, financial results, and people leadership

⁕ Strong leadership and team development skills with a proven ability to build high-performing teams

⁕ Strong business acumen with the ability to make data-driven decisions and execute long-term strategic plans

⁕ Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to effectively engage employees, customers, regulators, and community partners

⁕ Bachelor's degree in Business, Engineering, Operations Management, or a related discipline. Equivalent experience may be considered

title: Event DJ & Master of Ceremonies

title: Irrigation Technician

description:

description:

title: Quality Control (QC) Technician
description:
LifeLens Technologies, Inc. is a medical device developer located in beautiful Bucks County, PA. We are pioneering innovative, next-generation treatment devices for personal health monitoring.

We are hiring a Quality Control (QC) Technician. In this role, you are responsible for the testing and evaluation of finished devices, printed circuit board assemblies (PCBAs), mechanical and electronic sub-assemblies. Duties will also include reviewing electronic and paper records associated with the processing, inspection, and testing of finished devices and executing Quality Assurance release of product that conforms to specified requirements including Good Documentation Practices (GDP). You play an essential role in product testing, acceptance, and defect tracking.


Your passion and drive will be rewarded with a competitive salary, benefits, and long-term growth opportunities.

This is a full-time, on-site position.

Responsibilities:

  • Conduct quality inspections and testing throughout the production process, including incoming, in process and final inspections.
  • Inspect PCBAs for defects, including solder quality and visual damage.
  • Confirm all documentation including production and quality records supporting product release fully adheres to acceptance criteria and good Documentation Practices (GDP) including data integrity. Escalate any discrepancies immediately.
  • Maintain, monitor, and manage the batch record management system, including closure and disposition, data collection, and archiving of the records.
  • Log data from batch records into the quality metrics database. Generate reports on manufacturing yields and defects for management and engineering staff.

Education and Training:

  • Associate’s degree in a science or technical field, or HS diploma with applicable work experience.
  • Direct experience and knowledge of Good Documentation Practices (GDP)
  • Knowledge of quality management systems and regulatory compliance requirements FDA Quality System Regulation ISO 13485 is preferred.
  • Strong organizational and attention to detail skills.

Experience:

  • Minimum of 2 years of experience in a QA or QC role in medical device manufacturing or related industry. Manufacturing Quality Record review experience is strongly preferred.
  • Experience using a variety of measurement tools, including multimeters, calipers and micrometers.
  • Experience with PCB assembly and/ or electronics manufacturing
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint).
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to work independently and manage multiple priorities

Physical Demands:

  • Able to use standard office equipment (computer, mouse, keyboard, printer, etc.)
  • Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust and focus.
  • Must be able to lift 25 lbs.

Benefits:

  • Health Insurance
  • Dental & Vision Insurance
  • Stock Options
  • Paid Time Off
  • Flextime

title: Electrical Instructor
description:
Electrical Instructor


The Trades Institute is seeking a full-time or part-time, skilled and passionate Electrical Instructor in our Fair-Chance school who is committed to both teaching and changing lives. In this role, you will deliver engaging, hands-on instruction within our three 6-week stackable certificate programs, helping students build technical skills and workplace readiness.

Instructors serve not only as educators, but as mentors, supporting individuals as they gain the confidence and skills needed to pursue sustainable careers in the trades. This is an opportunity to make a meaningful impact in the community while sharing your expertise.

At Emerge, our values guide how we live, lead, and serve. Rooted in faith and renewal, they reflect our mission to restore lives through hope, integrity, and purpose.

We Excel: We always grow and improve, pursuing continuous learning and a hunger for quality.

We Own: We take responsibility for our actions and choices, demonstrating integrity through accountability.

Position Overview:
A qualified expert in the electric field to provide engaging and thorough instruction to novice men and women enrolled in our 6-week stackable course curriculum. Instructor will ensure students’ mastery of the information presented within the given course.


Principal Responsibilities:

  • Conducting classroom and hands-on training sessions for students
  • Developing and delivering engaging learning instruction
  • Providing guidance and support to students throughout their learning journey
  • Assessing student performance and providing feedback
  • Collaborating and coordinating with other industry leaders, staff and students to enhance the training program
  • Staying updated on industry trends and advancements in relevant fields
  • Recording students’ attendance and grades


Required Knowledge, Abilities, and Working Conditions


Knowledge of: The instructor must possess strong working knowledge of the electrical field, including industry standards, safety practices, tools, and real-world applications relevant to entry-level learners. This role requires an understanding of basic instructional methods and adult learning principles to effectively deliver course content. Knowledge of classroom and hands-on training techniques, student assessment practices, and record-keeping for attendance and grades is essential. Familiarity with current industry trends and a commitment to staying up to date with advancements in the electrical trade are also required.


Abilities: The instructor must be able to clearly communicate technical concepts to students with little to no prior experience, both verbally and in writing. This role requires the ability to develop and deliver engaging instruction, assess student comprehension, and provide constructive feedback that supports skill development and mastery. Strong organizational skills are needed to manage lesson plans, student work, and course materials. The instructor must be able to work collaboratively with staff, industry partners, and students, demonstrate professionalism and integrity at all times, and remain coachable with a willingness to continuously improve teaching and instructional skills.


Working Conditions: The position involves working in both classroom and hands-on training environments, requiring frequent standing, walking, and demonstration of electrical tools and techniques. The instructor may be exposed to noise, equipment, and materials commonly found in a training lab setting. Physical activities may include bending, lifting, and moving instructional materials or equipment. The role requires regular interaction with students and staff in a structured learning environment and is typically performed indoors during scheduled course hours aligned with program needs.


Qualifications and Education Requirements

  • Minimum of three (3) years of experience in the electrical field with proficient or expert knowledge in the subject area
  • High School Diploma or GED required
  • Strong verbal and basic written communication skills
  • Basic arithmetic and organizational skills to track student performance and grades
  • Ability to effectively instruct and support adult learners with limited prior experience
  • Willingness to be coached and develop instructional skills
  • Demonstrated professionalism, integrity, and reliability
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with staff, students, and industry partners
  • Basic computer skills, including email, word processing, and presentation software
  • Experience developing instructional materials and assessing student performance
  • Strong observation and listening skills to identify and support student learning needs

title: Quality Specialist
description:
Job Title: Quality Specialist

Location: Kent, WA
Reports To: Quality Assurance Manager
Job Type: Full-Time - Monday-Friday 8:00AM-4:30PM


At Promise Confections. We’re passionate about crafting delicious, high-quality candies that bring joy to everyone who tastes them. Located in Kent, Washington, our SGF team thrives in a lively, collaborative environment where creativity, teamwork, and a love for sweet things come together. We are looking for enthusiastic individuals who are excited to contribute to our growing candy brand and help spread happiness one treat at a time. As part of the crew, you’ll enjoy hand-on experience with unique confections, opportunities to innovate with flavors and designs and a workplace that celebrates both playfulness and professional growth. If you’re eager to join a fun, flavor-filled company where your ideas matter and your passion for sweets shine, Promise confections is the perfect place for you!


Company Overview:
Join our team at a SQF Certified food manufacturing facility, where we are dedicated to producing high-quality products in a safe and compliant environment. We offer a competitive salary, comprehensive health benefits, and paid vacation.


Position Overview:

Monitors the manufacturing of food products to ensure they conform to product specifications.


Key Responsibilities:

  • Conduct regular quality checks on raw materials, in-process products, and finished goods in accordance with established standards.
  • Perform routine inspections of equipment, processes, and packaging to ensure compliance with SQF standards and internal procedures.
  • Check in ingredients and packaging per approved supplier and receiving procedures.
  • Document and maintain accurate records of inspections, tests, and findings in compliance with food safety regulations and internal policies.
  • Assist in identifying and reporting any non-conformities in the production process and follow-up on corrective actions.
  • Support the development and implementation of food safety and quality programs, including HACCP, GMP, and SQF certifications.
  • Monitor sanitation processes and ensure adherence to hygiene standards across production areas.
  • Conduct environmental and microbial sampling as needed.
  • Assist in training production staff in quality control procedures and food safety practices.
  • Collaborate with the Quality Assurance team to ensure all quality systems are maintained and updated.
  • Assist in audits, both internal and external, and ensure continuous improvement of quality systems.
  • Request supplier documentation for raw materials received from vendors and inform other departments via Teams.
  • Control and file QC technician pre-op check, and production paperwork daily.
  • Organize the sending of micro test samples and filing test results for Seattle Gourmet Foods and private label companies- daily, monthly, annually.
  • Perform monthly glass and brittle plastic audit.
  • Send reminders to QA personnel according to the quality calendar.
  • Review, file, and remove (if necessary) labels from the label folder.
  • Create and maintain image folders for raw materials, final products, and other necessary documentation.
  • Manage the annual instrument calibration program.
  • Learn how to conduct daily QC inspections and assist the team when necessary.
  • Provide back-up support to QC technicians or the Quality Manager as needed.
  • Conduct allergen, sanitation, and swabbing as needed.
  • Ensure retention sampling, recording and storage is satisfactory maintained
  • Special Projects as assigned by the Quality Manager


Qualifications:

  • High school diploma or equivalent; an associate’s degree or certification in Food Science, Microbiology, or a related field is preferred.
  • 1-2 years of experience in a quality control or food safety role, preferably in a food manufacturing environment.
  • Knowledge of SQF, HACCP, and GMPs is highly desirable.
  • Strong attention to detail and ability to follow procedures meticulously.
  • Excellent communication and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, Outlook).


Benefits:

  • Competitive salary based on experience.
  • Health benefits, including medical, dental, and vision.
  • Paid vacation and holidays.
  • Opportunities for professional growth and advancement.


About Promise Confections

At Promise Confections, we take immense pride in being an award-winning manufacturer of everyday chocolate and confectionery products. Our commitment is to continually challenge the norms of traditional confectionery, pushing boundaries to deliver exceptional experiences. Comprising Edward Marc Brands, Seattle Gourmet Foods, Pearson’s Candy Co., and Annabelle Candy Co., we boast a diverse range of capabilities including panning, enrobing, extruding, clusters, barks, brittles, gummies and breath mint/sour candy tableting. With our extensive reach, servicing major retailers and offering private label and contract manufacturing services, we stand as emerging industry disrupters in confectionery. title: Part-Time Program Coordinator - Abilene, TX
description:
Code2College is dramatically increasing the number of minority and low-income high school students who enter and excel in STEM undergraduate majors and careers and is looking to hire a Part-Time
Program Coordinator to support its mission.

This is a hybrid position with in-person responsibilities for recruitment, events, and classes. Program coordinator will support in person courses.

OVERVIEW

As a Part-Time Program Coordinator, you will support a cohort of students and schools in Abilene, Texas and across the United States. You will support Code2College classes virtually and in person, lead student check-ins, support recruitment, and participate in Code2College events and other program activities.

RESPONSIBILITIES

Student & Program Support

  • Support a portfolio of student participants in Abilene, Texas and across the United States, serving as a consistent point of contact throughout their program experience.
  • Lead student check-ins, monitor engagement and participation, and provide follow-up and support as needed.
  • Support virtual and in-person Code2College classes, including observing classes and helping ensure students have the support they need to participate and succeed.
  • Draft and coordinate student-facing communications, reminders, and other program materials.
  • Support student recruitment and onboarding activities.

Program Data & Improvement

  • Track and analyze student-level performance and engagement data to identify meaningful insights and opportunities to improve program effectiveness.
  • Support programmatic projects and initiatives, including implementation, coordination, and follow-through.

Stakeholder Engagement

  • Build and maintain relationships with student participants, volunteer instructors, schools, and other stakeholders.
  • Help cultivate a strong sense of community within and across Code2College programs.
  • Support communication and coordination with program partners and other stakeholders.

Events & In-Person Programming

  • Participate in and support Code2College in-person events, including recruitment events, workshops, promotional events, partner events, and lunch and learns.
  • Support event preparation, execution, and follow-up as needed.

SCHEDULE & AVAILABILITY

  • Must be available Monday through Friday, 3:00–6:00 PM CST to support Code2College classes, with additional availability outside these hours for events and caseload responsibilities, for up to 30 hours per week.
  • Additional availability outside of these hours is required for student support, program responsibilities, and events.
  • This position is up to 30 hours per week.
  • May require occasional work outside of normal business hours and on Saturdays.
  • Other duties as assigned.

WHAT YOU’LL BRING

We are looking for someone who is early on in their career or looking to move into the non-profit education space, is eager to grow and develop, and is committed to our mission to equip minority and low-income high school students with the professional skills they need to excel in STEM degrees and careers.

  • You have a love of learning. You believe that your talents can be developed and you see feedback as an investment in your personal and professional growth.
  • You build trust and operate with integrity. You communicate openly and honestly when there is an issue so we can address it together.
  • You consider yourself a natural problem solver. You are always thinking about ways to do things better or differently, and you love to find solutions to tough problems.
  • You have an entrepreneurial spirit. You see yourself as a self-starter who is driven by setting and meeting goals, and getting better all the time. You are motivated by challenges and bounce back quickly from set-backs.
  • You prioritize outcomes over inputs and “why” over “what.”
  • You are driven by goals and data, and you see outcomes as your north star.
  • You consistently align yourself to the “why” of the work to determine the how and the what.

Additionally, to be successful at Code2College, you will be aligned with our core values:

  • Resourcefulness: we're a lean startup and none of us are experts; there are so many opportunities to leverage relationships, free and low-cost resources and communal assets to the betterment of our students and organization.
  • Urgency: the work that we do is important and every moment is an opportunity to change the lives of our students.
  • Transparency: we are candid with each other, share challenges as well as triumphs and have an orientation toward learning from our mistakes by talking about them openly.
  • Humility: every success is a team success and we're stronger as one unit; none of us can do this without the support of others.

Ideal candidates will have:

  • MUST live in the Abilene, Texas area.
  • Must have reliable transportation.
  • Willingness to work various evenings and weekends required.
  • Experience in a 6-12 setting prioritized.
  • Experience in an education setting is preferred.
